title: Advanced Diffusion MRI in the Human Brain: Microstructure Imaging and Structural Connectivity.
abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) is one of the most powerful MRI techniques for exploring the brain's microstructure in vivo. By measuring how water molecules move within tissue, it provides unique insight into the cellular and fiber architecture of the brain-information that conventional MRI cannot reveal. In clinical settings, diffusion imaging is now a valuable tool for early stroke diagnosis, tumour characterization, and surgical planning. In research, it enables the study of brain development, ageing, and disease progression, linking imaging findings to cellular and molecular processes. Over the past three decades, diffusion MRI has evolved from simple diffusion-weighted imaging and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps to advanced models that capture the complexity of tissue organization. Techniques such as diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), diffusional kurtosis imaging (DKI), and multi-compartment biophysical models now allow estimation of parameters related to axonal density, myelination, and water exchange between cellular compartments. Combined with tractography, these methods enable noninvasive reconstruction of white-matter pathways and network-level connectivity, transforming dMRI into a central tool for both neuroscience and clinical use. This chapter introduces the principles and applications of diffusion MRI in a progressive manner. We begin with the fundamental physics of diffusion contrast and its clinical relevance, then move to advanced microstructural models that provide richer biological specificity. Subsequent sections describe tractography methods used to map brain connectivity and analyze structural networks. Together, these sections aim to provide readers, especially those with limited imaging background, with an accessible understanding of how diffusion MRI reveals the brain's hidden microstructure and connects it to biological function.

title: [Trauma-From diagnosis to intervention].
abstract: Abdominal trauma represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge because the large number of potentially involved organs and the complexity of the underlying injuries are difficult to capture within a standardized diagnostic approach. Both blunt and penetrating abdominal injuries can be involved as well as falls from a great height, traffic accidents or violent encounters. In addition, patients may be polytraumatized and the abdomen represents only one component of the injuries sustained but is often clinically prioritized due to the potentially immediate life-threatening nature of injuries to abdominal organs. Such injuries represent an interdisciplinary challenge and their treatment is increasingly carried out using minimally invasive procedures, often within the involvement of interventional radiology. This article aims to present both appropriate diagnostic approaches and minimally invasive treatment options.

title: [Image-guided minimally invasive treatment options for endometriosis].
abstract: Background Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age with a mean diagnostic delay of 7-10 years. Image-guided procedures show increasingly promising results as minimally invasive alternatives to excision. Objective Structured overview of image-guided minimally invasive treatment options for endometriosis with focus on percutaneous cryoablation. Results Percutaneous cryoablation demonstrates the strongest evidence for extraperitoneal and intramuscular lesions and represents a valid minimally invasive alternative to excision. Three institutional cases illustrate technique and outcomes. Ethanol sclerotherapy is established for ovarian endometriomas. High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) shows promising results for abdominal wall disease; radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and microwave ablation are investigational. Conclusion Interventional radiology offers a growing therapeutic spectrum. Prospective randomized trials are needed for guideline integration.

title: Hybrid CNN-transformer model with gated feature fusion and GAN-based augmentation for MRI image classification.
abstract: Objective Brain tumor classification based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a critical role in clinical diagnosis, yet it remains challenging due to high intra-class variability, inter-class similarity, and limited annotated data. To address these challenges, this study proposes a gated hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN)-transformer architecture (GHCT-Net) that effectively integrates local and global feature representations for robust brain tumor classification in data-limited medical imaging scenarios. Methods The proposed framework combines a ConvNeXt-based convolutional branch for fine-grained spatial feature extraction with a Swin Transformer branch for modeling long-range contextual dependencies. A gate-based fusion mechanism is introduced to adaptively balance the contribution of each feature stream. Additionally, a conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial network (cDCGAN) is employed to generate class-consistent synthetic MRI samples to mitigate data scarcity. The model was evaluated on a public dataset of 7023 MRI images across four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no tumor) under three training scenarios: original, traditionally augmented, and GAN-augmented datasets. Results The results demonstrate that the GHCT-Net achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art CNN and Transformer architectures, reaching a classification accuracy of 98.39% on the GAN-augmented dataset. Quantitative analysis, along with confusion matrices, t‑distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) visualizations, and gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability studies, confirms that the model successfully learns discriminative and clinically relevant features. Conclusion Combining a gated hybrid CNN-transformer architecture with GAN-based data augmentation provides a highly effective and robust solution for brain tumor classification, particularly in scenarios constrained by limited medical imaging data.

Objective

Brain tumor classification based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a critical role in clinical diagnosis, yet it remains challenging due to high intra-class variability, inter-class similarity, and limited annotated data. To address these challenges, this study proposes a gated hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN)-transformer architecture (GHCT-Net) that effectively integrates local and global feature representations for robust brain tumor classification in data-limited medical imaging scenarios.

Methods

The proposed framework combines a ConvNeXt-based convolutional branch for fine-grained spatial feature extraction with a Swin Transformer branch for modeling long-range contextual dependencies. A gate-based fusion mechanism is introduced to adaptively balance the contribution of each feature stream. Additionally, a conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial network (cDCGAN) is employed to generate class-consistent synthetic MRI samples to mitigate data scarcity. The model was evaluated on a public dataset of 7023 MRI images across four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no tumor) under three training scenarios: original, traditionally augmented, and GAN-augmented datasets.

Results

The results demonstrate that the GHCT-Net achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art CNN and Transformer architectures, reaching a classification accuracy of 98.39% on the GAN-augmented dataset. Quantitative analysis, along with confusion matrices, t‑distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) visualizations, and gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability studies, confirms that the model successfully learns discriminative and clinically relevant features.

Conclusion

Combining a gated hybrid CNN-transformer architecture with GAN-based data augmentation provides a highly effective and robust solution for brain tumor classification, particularly in scenarios constrained by limited medical imaging data.

title: Interpreting liver volume changes after rifampicin in healthy volunteers.
abstract: Rifampicin-associated liver volume changes in healthy volunteers provide an opportunity to examine the human relevance of xenobiotic-induced liver growth. This Comment considers three aspects of the clinical analysis relevant to interpreting the observed response. Clarification of whether the volumetric outcomes and choice of normalisation were prespecified, alongside paired treatment effects and confidence intervals, would help establish the basis for inference and assess the response's magnitude and precision. For a small volumetric response, blinded repeat segmentation of existing magnetic resonance images and details of scan timing and pre-scan intake would help assess reproducibility under comparable physiological conditions. Associations between 4β-hydroxycholesterol and liver volume could also be examined using within-participant rifampicin-minus-placebo differences, with appropriate attention to the crossover design and an exploratory interpretation. Most of these suggestions could be addressed through protocol information and existing imaging and crossover data, strengthening interpretation of the human findings and guiding further investigation of pregnane X receptor-mediated liver growth.

title: Prognostic value of dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI and plasma angiogenic markers for survival outcomes in HPV-negative oropharyngeal carcinoma treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy.
abstract: Purpose Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) enables non-invasive assessment of tumour vascularity, while circulating angiogenic factors may reflect tumour-associated angiogenic activity. We investigated whether DCE-MRI perfusion parameters and plasma angiogenic factors measured before and early during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) are associated with survival in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Methods In this prospective single-centre study, 24 patients with locally advanced HPV-negative OPSCC treated with cCRT were analysed. DCE-MRI perfusion parameters (Ktrans, Kep, Ve, iAUC) were analysed at baseline and early intra-treatment (20 Gy), while plasma angiogenic factors (vascular endothelial growth factor [VEGF], connective tissue growth factor, platelet-derived growth factor-AB, angiogenin, endostatin, and thrombospondin-1) were analysed at baseline, early intra-treatment and post-treatment (10-12 weeks). Disease-specific survival (DSS) was assessed using univariable Cox regression (hazard ratios [HRs] per 1-SD) and Kaplan-Meier analysis with false-discovery-rate correction. Results Seven patients died of the index cancer. Higher baseline Ktrans (HR per 1-SD 0.30, p = 0.031) and higher early intra-treatment plasma VEGF (HR 0.37, p = 0.043) were nominally associated with better DSS; VEGF also showed separation in Kaplan-Meier analysis (3-year DSS 92% vs. 36%, log-rank p = 0.016). Effect estimates were similar after exploratory adjustment for tumour volume but attenuated after adjustment for stage. No association remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction, and the early VEGF association partly overlapped with local treatment response. Conclusion In this exploratory analysis, baseline DCE-MRI perfusion (Ktrans) and plasma VEGF showed hypothesis-generating associations with DSS in HPV-negative OPSCC. As no association survived multiplicity correction, these findings require validation in larger independent cohorts.

Purpose

Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) enables non-invasive assessment of tumour vascularity, while circulating angiogenic factors may reflect tumour-associated angiogenic activity. We investigated whether DCE-MRI perfusion parameters and plasma angiogenic factors measured before and early during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) are associated with survival in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC).

Methods

In this prospective single-centre study, 24 patients with locally advanced HPV-negative OPSCC treated with cCRT were analysed. DCE-MRI perfusion parameters (Ktrans, Kep, Ve, iAUC) were analysed at baseline and early intra-treatment (20 Gy), while plasma angiogenic factors (vascular endothelial growth factor [VEGF], connective tissue growth factor, platelet-derived growth factor-AB, angiogenin, endostatin, and thrombospondin-1) were analysed at baseline, early intra-treatment and post-treatment (10-12 weeks). Disease-specific survival (DSS) was assessed using univariable Cox regression (hazard ratios [HRs] per 1-SD) and Kaplan-Meier analysis with false-discovery-rate correction.

Results

Seven patients died of the index cancer. Higher baseline Ktrans (HR per 1-SD 0.30, p = 0.031) and higher early intra-treatment plasma VEGF (HR 0.37, p = 0.043) were nominally associated with better DSS; VEGF also showed separation in Kaplan-Meier analysis (3-year DSS 92% vs. 36%, log-rank p = 0.016). Effect estimates were similar after exploratory adjustment for tumour volume but attenuated after adjustment for stage. No association remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction, and the early VEGF association partly overlapped with local treatment response.

Conclusion

In this exploratory analysis, baseline DCE-MRI perfusion (Ktrans) and plasma VEGF showed hypothesis-generating associations with DSS in HPV-negative OPSCC. As no association survived multiplicity correction, these findings require validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: The Lymphatic System in the Fontan Circulation: Pathophysiology, Imaging and Therapeutic Interventions.
abstract: The Fontan circulation, the definitive palliation for patients with univentricular hearts, produces a unique haemodynamic state characterised by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, reduced cardiac output and the absence of a subpulmonary ventricular impulse. Because lymphatic drainage depends critically on the pressure gradient between the thoracic duct and the systemic veins, this physiology has profound consequences for the lymphatic system. Over the past decade, the lymphatic circulation has moved from being regarded as a passive bystander to being recognised as a central determinant of Fontan failure. Chronic systemic venous hypertension drives lymphatic overproduction and impaired central drainage, leading to progressive lymphatic congestion that manifests as chylothorax, protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), plastic bronchitis, lymphoedema and Fontan-associated liver disease. Advances in magnetic resonance (MR) lymphangiography, in particular dynamic contrast-enhanced MR lymphangiography and T2-weighted MR lymphangiography, now permit direct visualisation of abnormal lymphatic flow and precise planning of image-guided interventions. Percutaneous lymphatic embolisation and thoracic-duct decompression, together with surgical decompression procedures and, ultimately, heart transplantation, have shown clinically relevant efficacy in selected patients with complications refractory to medical therapy. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on the pathophysiology, imaging and treatment of lymphatic complications in the Fontan circulation. Lymphatic involvement is frequent, under-diagnosed, and prognostically important; the integration of advanced lymphatic imaging and the consolidation of expertise in specialised percutaneous lymphatic intervention represent the most relevant advances of the last decade.

title: Evaluation of the relationship between the anatomical and morphometric characteristics of the sphenoid sinus in the paediatric population.
abstract: Objectives The aim was to analyse the morphological characteristics of the sphenoid sinus in the paediatric population and the possible effects of sex and age on the prevalence of pneumatization. Methods Patients in the 0-16 age group were determined as the paediatric group, and patients 16+ years of age were determined as the control group. Sphenoid sinus measurements and pneumatization classification were performed by two maxillofacial radiologists. Sphenoid sinus pneumatizations are divided into three groups: sellar, clival, and lateral. Results Types of right lateral pneumatization show significant differences between age groups (P=0.023). Lat-D type was significantly more prevalent in control group, while Lat-B type was observed only in the paediatric group. Like the right side, left lateral pneumatization types also showed statistically significant differences between age groups (P=0.013). Lat-D type is significantly more common in control group, while Lat-C is more frequently observed in the paediatric group. In terms of symmetry, there is a borderline significant difference between age groups (P≈0.05). While the height of the sphenoid sinus exhibited a weak positive correlation with the length of the optic chiasm (R=0.273, P<0.001), the anteroposterior length and width of the sphenoid sinus both demonstrated moderate positive correlations with the intercarotid distance (R=0.333 and R=0.435, P<0.001). Conclusion Lateral pneumatization type showed significant age-related changes. Optic chiasm length correlated with sphenoid sinus height, while intercarotid distance correlated with both sphenoid sinus anteroposterior length and width.

title: Multiparametric quantitative MRI in knee osteoarthritis: evidence and requirements for interpretation and reporting.
abstract: Quantitative MRI can characterize cartilage and other joint tissues beyond visible structural damage, but its contribution to individual management of knee osteoarthritis remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the evidence needed to interpret quantitative measurements, combine parameters, and report their uncertainty. An initial PubMed search in June 2026 was supplemented on 14 September 2026 by an updated PubMed search and broader Embase and Web of Science searches. Targeted full-text assessment addressed incremental value, outcome timing, validation, and measurement error. Selected development studies found better discrimination with integrated diffusion and relaxation measurements than with individual parameters, whereas other combined imaging models did not improve on simpler comparators. Longitudinal associations were outcome-specific, and independent external validation was limited. Treatment studies showed inconsistent agreement between imaging changes and symptomatic benefit. We propose a five-step interpretation framework that establishes the clinical question, verifies technical adequacy, assesses morphology and comparable reference data, evaluates measurement uncertainty, and separates observations from clinical inferences. Two hypothetical scenarios illustrate its application. Quantitative MRI currently provides its strongest support as a controlled research measurement. Demonstrated reproducibility, an appropriate comparator, and evidence of added decision value are required before a quantitative finding can justify patient-level diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-response claims.

title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18 F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

title: Synovial plica syndromes: a comprehensive overview from embryology to pathology.
abstract: Synovial plicae are folds of synovial tissue in the knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder, representing embryonic remnants of synovial septa. They are usually asymptomatic, but trauma, repetitive microtrauma, or prior surgery can render them thickened and fibrotic, producing pain and mechanical symptoms collectively termed plica syndrome. It is easily overlooked or misdiagnosed because the symptoms are nonspecific and other intra-articular disorders often coexist. This review addresses the embryology, histology, anatomy, clinical presentation, imaging, and treatment of synovial plicae across these joints, with emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. MRI is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating suspected plica syndrome, characterizing the fold and associated abnormalities, and excluding alternative causes of joint pain. Pathologic plicae appear thickened and irregular, with increased signal intensity and frequently associated focal synovitis or adjacent chondral damage. Plica thickness alone has limited diagnostic value, as measurements overlap between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Establishing a diagnosis of symptomatic plica syndrome requires correlation of the imaging findings with the clinical presentation. When joint effusion is absent, magnetic resonance (MR) or computed tomography (CT) arthrography improves delineation of the synovial folds and associated lesions. Plica syndrome occurs most often in young, physically active patients, and management is initially conservative. When symptoms are refractory, arthroscopic resection relieves symptoms, particularly when the plica is the only abnormality and the cartilage is preserved. Most outcome data derive from the knee and the elbow.

title: CT-fibrosis score: development and internal validation for identifying advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: Purpose Advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic and anatomic remodeling beyond the liver. We developed and internally validated an interpretable CT-based score integrating abdominal body-composition and organ measurements and compared it with the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index. Methods We retrospectively studied 151 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASLD (86 advanced [F3-F4], 65 early-stage [F0-F2] fibrosis). Deep learning-based segmentation quantified abdominal adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, bone, liver, and spleen measurements. The CT-Fibrosis Score was developed using repeated (50×) stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with imputation, standardization, and feature selection confined to each training fold and inner 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Performance was based on out-of-fold predictions and compared with FIB-4 using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, age dependence, and ascites. Results Four features were consistently selected: age, bone-to-abdominal-cavity volume ratio, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) density, and spleen index. The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.85). Among 141 patients with an available FIB-4 score, no significant difference was detected between the CT-Fibrosis Score (AUC 0.76) and FIB-4 (AUC 0.79; difference - 0.03, 95% CI - 0.11 to + 0.04; p = 0.37); this comparison was not powered for non-inferiority. Adding the CT-Fibrosis Score to FIB-4 did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.80 vs. 0.79; difference + 0.003, 95% CI - 0.04 to + 0.05; p = 0.90), with the confidence interval excluding an improvement greater than approximately 0.05. Conclusion The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis but did not improve discrimination when added to FIB-4. External validation in an unselected population undergoing CT for non-hepatic indications is required before any opportunistic application.

title: Multimodality imaging of hepatic cystic echinococcosis: diagnostic approach, differential diagnosis, complications, and post-treatment assessment.
abstract: Cystic echinococcosis (CE), caused by the metacestode of Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato, is a zoonosis that remains endemic across the Middle East, the Mediterranean basin, North Africa and South America, and the liver is the organ most frequently involved. Because serological assays are of limited sensitivity and specificity, imaging carries the diagnostic burden: ultrasonography (US) is the cornerstone for initial diagnosis, staging, treatment planning and longitudinal follow-up; computed tomography (CT) best defines anatomical location, vascular relationships, mural calcification and acute complications such as rupture and superinfection; and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) more faithfully reproduces US-defined staging morphology than CT and provides superior soft-tissue contrast for assessing biliary involvement and separating CE cysts from cystic neoplasms. The aim of this pictorial review is fourfold: to illustrate the US, CT and MRI appearance of each World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) stage of hepatic CE and to explain how stage assignment translates directly into a stage-specific treatment decision-anti-parasitic treatment, percutaneous treatment, surgery or watch-and-wait; to present, stage by stage, the hepatic lesions that mimic CE and the findings that discriminate them; to depict the wall signs of the CE cyst that become visible with high-frequency linear transducers, including the three-layered wall, adherent brood capsules and hydatid sand; and to review the imaging of complicated CE together with the expected post-treatment appearance, procedure-related complications and the imaging strategy for detecting recurrence.

title: T2-weighted MRI-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency status in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
abstract: Rationale and objectives The aim of this study was to explore the feasibility of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) - based radiomics in preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), and to establish a non-invasive approach for guiding individualized treatment planning. Materials and methods A total of 133 patients with pathologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent MRI scan (T2WI, T1-contrast enhanced) were retrospectively enrolled in this study. All patients were stratified into HRD-positive and HRD-negative group. These 133 patients (41 in HRD-negative group and 92 in HRD-positive group) were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 93) and a validation set (n = 40) at a 7:3 ratio. Three different models were constructed and evaluated: clinical characteristics only (clinical model); T2WI-radiomics features only (radiomics model); and a combination of them all (combined model). The predictive performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and area under the curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to validate the clinical-radiomic combined model. Results In the training set, the combined model achieved the best performance (AUC = 0.889; all P > 0.05). The radiomics model achieved predictive performance comparable to the clinical model (AUC of 0.762 vs. 0.790; P = 0.676). In the validation set, the combined model performed significantly better than the clinical or radiomics model (AUCs of 0.853 vs. 0.805 vs. 0.706; all P > 0.05). DCA demonstrated that the combined model achieved superior net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the clinical and radiomics models alone. Conclusions Our research demonstrated that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance. It is feasible to apply radiomics to predict HRD status of HGSOC patients, which can further assist clinicians in formulating individualized treatment strategies.

title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

title: Automatic generation of training data from dual-energy CT scans: a new approach to train renal vessel segmentation models.
abstract: Objective To investigate the feasibility of automatic training data generation using virtual non-contrast (VNC) images of dual-energy CT and to evaluate the performance of medical segmentation models trained on auto-generated data. Methods Training images were generated from contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans using VNC algorithm. Corresponding training labels were generated from iodine-density images via intensity thresholding. The paired VNC images and labels constituted the dataset (791 cases in total) for training non-enhanced CT (NECT) segmentation models. We attempted to train segmentation models with VNC images alone, as well as the combination of VNC and real NECT images. Results Models trained with auto-generated data effectively performed renal vein segmentation on NECT images, achieving Dice score of 69.60%. It identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks and 54.5% (6/11) accessory veins in the test set. The models' performance on artery segmentation was not satisfactory, with Dice score of 44.56%. It only identified 41.4% (29/70) artery main trunks and 4.54% (1/22) accessory arteries. However, the combination of generated data and labeled data greatly improved model's artery Dice to 71.23%. Combined model identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks, 98.6% (69/70) artery main trunks, 68.2% (15/22) accessory arteries and 63.6% (7/11) accessory veins. Its accessory artery detection is significantly higher than the model trained with labeled data (15/22 vs. 5/22, p < 0.01), closing the gap with human radiologist (15/22 vs. 18/22, p = 0.250). Conclusion VNC and Iodine-density images can be utilized to automatically generate training data for segmentation models. This pipeline shows promise for training segmentation models on NECT images.

title: Association of Capsular Involvement with Delayed Re-intervention After Splenic Artery Embolization for Blunt Splenic Injury.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether splenic capsule involvement is associated with delayed re-intervention after splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury. Materials and methods This retrospective single-center study included 329 consecutive patients undergoing splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury (2017-2025). Capsule involvement was defined as a laceration reaching the splenic surface with capsular disruption or communication with the perisplenic space on contrast-enhanced computed tomography. The primary outcome was delayed re-intervention. Cox and Firth regression were performed, with interobserver agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa. Results Delayed re-intervention occurred in 26 patients (7.9%) at a median of 6 days; all underwent repeat embolization; none required splenectomy. Twenty (76.9%) were detected on routine surveillance computed tomography without preceding deterioration. Capsule involvement was present in 25 of 26 events. Initial computed tomography showed vascular injury elsewhere in 25 of 26 patients, but neither computed tomography nor angiography showed pseudoaneurysm or active bleeding at the eventual lesion site. Re-intervention occurred in 25 of 245 patients with capsule involvement (10.2%) versus 1 of 84 without (1.2%). Capsule involvement was associated with re-intervention (hazard ratio, 6.82; 95% confidence interval, 1.62-28.74; p = 0.009), but significance was lost after reclassifying two events. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 96.2%, 27.4%, 10.2%, and 98.8%; pre-consensus agreement was 97.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.938). Conclusion Capsule involvement was associated with delayed re-intervention, but the estimate was statistically fragile because only one capsule-negative event occurred. Surveillance-driven, single-center findings are exploratory; external validation is required before changes in surveillance practice. Level of evidence Level 3, prognostic study.

title: ESR Essentials: MRI of the scrotum-practice recommendations by the European Society of Urogenital Radiology.
abstract: While conventional ultrasonography (US) remains the first-line imaging modality for scrotal pathology, multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has emerged as a valuable problem-solving tool for indeterminate US findings. Owing to its superior soft-tissue contrast, functional imaging capabilities, and operator independence, mpMRI allows for the precise localization and characterization of scrotal lesions. This paper from the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group provides a comprehensive, evidence-based overview of scrotal mpMRI for a general radiologist. It details optimized imaging protocols, recommending a standard sequence of T1-weighted, T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and subtracted dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. The article highlights key clinical indications, including the characterization of intratesticular and paratesticular masses, local staging of testicular germ cell tumors, and differentiation between germ cell and sex cord-stromal neoplasms. This paper familiarizes radiologists with normal MRI appearances and MRI findings of common scrotal diseases. Evidence-based recommendations for reporting basic MRI examinations of the scrotum are also provided. The potential of advanced techniques, such as diffusion tensor imaging and proton MR spectroscopy, and the future integration of artificial intelligence and radiomics, are also discussed. We hope the implementation of these recommendations into radiological practice will enhance diagnostic confidence and promote standardized practice in scrotal MRI for radiologists. KEY POINTS: While conventional ultrasound is the first-line modality for scrotal pathology, it can yield inconclusive findings regarding complex mass characterization and local tumor staging. Multiparametric MRI combines anatomical and functional data to accurately characterize scrotal masses, localize impalpable, undescended testes, and provide precise local tumor staging. Scrotal multiparametric MRI serves as a valuable problem-solving tool that enhances diagnostic confidence in sonographically indeterminate cases, prevents unnecessary radical orchiectomies, supports testis-sparing surgery or active surveillance, and standardizes radiological reporting templates to optimize personalized patient management.

title: Reducing operator-dependent variability in liver shear wave elastography through an AI-guided region-of-interest placement pipeline.
abstract: Objectives To develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that automates optimal circular region-of-interest (ROI) placement and the surrounding elastogram box, provides probe-angle/contact guidance, and measures skin-to-capsule distance (SCD) to standardize liver SWE acquisition, aiming to reduce operator-dependent variability. Materials and methods A two-stage pipeline combined SimCLR self-supervised pretraining on 17,441 unlabeled ultrasound images, followed by ENet fine-tuning using 495 annotated images for liver segmentation and 1564 images for poor probe contact detection. Segmentation outputs were combined with constraints on valid liver tissue pixels, axial depth, lateral boundaries, and regions of poor acoustic coupling to generate masks for optimal ROI placement. A distance transformation algorithm then identified optimal ROI coordinates within these masks. An inter-observer reader study assessed AI performance by comparing automated ROI placement, SCD measurements, and probe-angle correction guidance with annotations from expert attending radiologists. Results 18,182 US images from 654 liver elastography examinations in 609 patients (mean age, 52.6 ± 12.95 years; 55.4% male) were acquired from three ultrasound systems. The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance with a Dice coefficient of 0.89, sensitivity of 0.95, specificity of 0.93, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94. The reader study demonstrated significantly higher AI-to-attending radiologist agreement (93.8%) compared to inter-attending agreement for ROI placement (81%). Cohen's kappa agreement between two attending radiologists was 0.25. Conclusion The proposed AI-driven pipeline significantly improved ROI placement consistency and reproducibility, highlighting its potential to enhance clinical reliability in liver fibrosis assessment. Key points Question Operator-dependent variability in region-of-interest (ROI) placement compromises measurement reproducibility in B-mode shear wave elastography. We developed an AI pipeline to place an optimal ROI. Findings The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance of Dice 0.89 (AUC 0.94) and demonstrated higher AI-to-attending agreement (93.8%) than inter-attending agreement (81%) for ROI placement. Clinical relevance By standardizing ROI placement, elastogram box selection, and probe angle/contact guidance, the AI pipeline reduces operator-dependent variability in liver SWE acquisition, supporting more reproducible liver stiffness measurements that could improve fibrosis staging reliability.

title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Objectives The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. Materials and methods This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions. Results Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions. Conclusion IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy. Key points Question Reliable pretreatment tools are needed to identify unresectable HCC patients likely to benefit from TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Findings An integrated MRI-pathology model combining habitat radiomics and deep-learning pathomics predicted treatment response, with validation and testing areas under the curve of 0.878 and 0.875. Clinical relevance The integrated model may support pretreatment response stratification for TACE-based triple therapy and help inform surveillance intensity or alternative treatment considerations, pending prospective validation.

title: A fractal-integrated CT score predicts high-risk pathology and early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a noninvasive CT-based imaging score incorporating fractal analysis to predict high-risk pathological features in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. Materials and methods This retrospective bicenter study included 514 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC who underwent curative resection, divided into training (n = 219), internal validation (n = 94), external validation (n = 100) and outcome datasets (n = 101). The fractal dimension (FD) and lacunarity were extracted from portal venous-phase CT images via box-counting algorithms. Imaging predictors of high-risk pathological features, including high tumor grade, lymphovascular invasion (LVI) and perineural invasion (PNI), were identified by logistic regression and integrated into a comprehensive weighted imaging score. Cox regression analyses were performed to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. Results Patients with high-risk pathological features exhibited greater FD and lacunarity. The final score included six imaging features: necrosis, peripancreatic fat infiltration, venous involvement, regional lymphadenopathy, FD and lacunarity. For any high-risk pathology, the fractal-integrated score achieved AUC of 0.94, 0.88 and 0.84 in the training, internal validation and external validation datasets, respectively. For high pathological burden, the AUCs were 0.92, 0.80, and 0.77. In the outcome dataset, the score was an independent predictor of early recurrence (HR = 2.71; p = 0.004) and improved prognostic discrimination when combined with pathologic predictors. Conclusion This CT-based score, integrating fractal biomarkers, enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative prediction of aggressive pathological features in PDAC and provides incremental value for early recurrence risk stratification. Key points Question Can the fractal-based imaging features be used to predict high-risk pathological features and guide risk stratification for early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)? Findings This CT-based score integrating fractal analysis predicted high-risk pathological features and was independent predictors of early recurrence and provided incremental prognostic value beyond pathologic factors. Clinical relevance This CT-based imaging score may help identify patients at high-risk of aggressive pathology before surgery and may further complement postoperative pathological risk stratification for early recurrence.

title: Evaluating strategies to optimize breast MRI screening: a modeling study of abbreviated protocols, dockable tables, and staffing scenarios.
abstract: Objective MRI is increasingly recommended for breast cancer screening, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. However, widespread adoption is constrained by limited capacity and high costs. This study evaluated how optimized MRI screening workflows could address these barriers through three targeted interventions: an abbreviated scan protocol, dockable MRI tables, and expanded technician staffing. Materials and methods A calculation model was developed to compare seven workflow strategies against the current standard care. Strategies included reducing MRI acquisition time from 13 to 6 min, introducing dockable tables with breast coils, adding a third technician, and combinations thereof. Workflow durations and cost inputs were derived from published literature, hospital data, and expert opinion. Primary outcomes were daily screening capacity, cost per screening, annual screening costs, and staffing requirements for a screening volume of 5500 screening examinations per year. Results After evaluating several optimized workflow strategies, we found that reducing MRI acquisition time increased daily screening capacity from 30 to 47 scans, with associated annual savings of €147,505 (8.4%) and a reduction of 1320 technician hours. Combined strategies integrating reduced scan time, additional technicians, and dockable tables increased the daily capacity from 30 to 67 scans and reduced annual costs by up to €160,557 (9.2%) compared with the current workflow. Conclusions Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scan protocols and dockable tables can substantially increase screening capacity, reduce costs, and technician workload. This would expand access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for (future) capacity problems. Key points Question Which workflow optimization strategies, including abbreviated scan protocols, dockable tables, and additional technicians, offer the greatest capacity and cost benefits for MRI breast cancer screening? Findings Abbreviated scan protocols provide the largest cost savings, while combined workflow changes can substantially increase capacity and still reduce costs. Clinical relevance Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scans and dockable tables can increase screening capacity and reduce costs and technician workload. This expands access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for capacity problems.

title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
abstract: Purpose Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. Methods CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality. Results The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer.

CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality.

The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). title: Opportunistic PSA testing is not the safe alternative : Why Austria's non-policy on prostate cancer screening maximizes harm and forfeits the benefits.
abstract: Austria has never implemented an organized prostate cancer screening program, yet opportunistic PSA testing has been widespread for more than three decades. This has produced the harms of screening without the safeguards of a program: testing outside appropriate age and life-expectancy windows, repeated testing of low-risk men, unnecessary biopsy, overdiagnosis and overtreatment, while generating little systematic information on quality or outcomes. Randomized evidence shows that organized, repeated screening can reduce prostate cancer mortality substantially, whereas opportunistic testing delivers less benefit with more overdiagnosis. Contemporary risk-adapted pathways further improve the balance of benefit and harm: defined start and stop ages, PSA-based risk stratification, MRI before biopsy, targeted biopsy, and active surveillance can reduce unnecessary biopsies and detection or treatment of indolent disease without compromising detection of clinically significant cancer. Europe has therefore moved toward organized, PSA-based screening with MRI as a follow-up test. Austria is now participating in PRAISE-U Plus and has initiated a national multidisciplinary consensus process involving 65 experts from 22 organizations. The policy question is no longer whether Austrian men are being screened-they are-but whether screening remains unstructured or becomes organized, quality-assured and equitable. The evidence supports the latter: invite the right men, stratify risk, biopsy selectively, treat only clinically relevant disease, and measure outcomes systematically.

title: Systemic immune-inflammation index predicts neurological recovery in degenerative cervical myelopathy: a comparative analysis of OPLL and non-OPLL patients.
abstract: To compare systemic inflammatory characteristics between patients with ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) and non-OPLL degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and to evaluate the prognostic value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), alone and in combination with radiological parameters, for postoperative neurological recovery. This retrospective prognostic cohort study included 317 surgically treated patients with DCM (98 with OPLL and 219 without OPLL) with complete 2-year follow-up data. Neurological and clinical outcomes were assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS), Neck Disability Index (NDI), modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score, and mJOA recovery rate; patients were categorized as having favorable recovery (mJOA recovery rate ≥ 50%; n = 231) or unfavorable recovery (< 50%; n = 86). Preoperative hematologic inflammatory indices, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and SII, serum biochemical profiles, surgical characteristics, and cervical radiological parameters were collected. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was used to assess maximum spinal cord compression (MSCC), maximum canal compromise (MCC), transverse area (TA), and compression ratio (CR). Full multivariable logistic regression models identified factors independently associated with favorable recovery. Sensitivity analyses separately adjusted for surgical approach, surgical procedure, and the numbers of decompressed and fused levels. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses assessed discriminative performance and optimal cutoffs. Predictors that remained independently associated with favorable recovery in the full multivariable models were retained, and parsimonious logistic regression models were refitted for ROC analysis, nomogram construction, and internal validation. The combined scores represented weighted linear predictors from the corresponding refitted SII-TA models and were not predicted probabilities. Internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples; calibration was assessed using calibration curves and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical net benefit was evaluated using decision curve analysis. Patients with OPLL had significantly higher white blood cell (WBC) counts and SII values than those without OPLL. In the overall cohort, lower SII and larger TA were independently associated with favorable neurological recovery. A combined predictive score was derived from the refitted parsimonious model as follows: Score = - 0.202 + 5.697 × TA - 0.294 × (SII/100). Score ≥ 0.50 was identified as the optimal cutoff for predicting favorable neurological recovery. ROC analysis further identified cutoff values of SII ≤ 556.5 and TA ≥ 0.405 cm² as predictors of favorable outcomes. Subgroup analyses suggested differing predictor patterns between the OPLL and non-OPLL groups. In the OPLL subgroup, lower SII remained independently associated with favorable neurological recovery, with an optimal cutoff value of SII ≤ 558.4. In contrast, in patients with non-OPLL DCM, a distinct combined predictive score was derived from the refitted parsimonious model: Score = - 0.453 + 5.522 × TA - 0.210 × (SII/100). Score ≥ 0.99 was identified as the optimal cutoff for predicting favorable neurological recovery. Corresponding ROC-derived thresholds of SII ≤ 390.6 and TA ≥ 0.445 cm² were identified for predicting favorable neurological recovery in this subgroup. The association between lower SII and favorable recovery remained significant after separate adjustment for each surgical characteristic. The optimism-corrected areas under the ROC curve were 0.749, 0.711, and 0.722 for the overall DCM, OPLL, and non-OPLL DCM models, respectively; goodness-of-fit tests did not indicate lack of fit, and decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical net benefit. Systemic inflammatory burden, quantified by SII, was independently associated with long-term neurological recovery in patients with DCM. Subgroup analyses yielded different predictor patterns and SII cutoff estimates in the OPLL and non-OPLL groups; however, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external confirmation. Models integrating systemic inflammatory and radiological parameters may assist risk stratification, but their clinical utility should be established in independent prospective cohorts before implementation.

title: Cage rotation and effective rim support are associated with subsidence after TLIF using a single expandable banana-shaped cage design.
abstract: To determine whether postoperative cage obliquity and vertebral rim support are associated with 12-month subsidence after TLIF using a single articulating expandable banana-shaped cage design. We retrospectively reviewed 101 patients (109 levels) treated with an articulating expandable banana-shaped cage. Postoperative CT was used to measure cage obliquity angle and cage-rim contact ratio. Subsidence was defined as ≥ 2 mm at 12 months. Spearman correlations were used to examine relationships between cage obliquity and rim-support metrics. Associations of cage obliquity and cage-rim contact with subsidence were evaluated using separate multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for Hounsfield units. Spatial heatmaps visualized the distribution of anterior rim support, which was further quantified using mediolateral contact metrics. Subsidence occurred in 16 levels (14.7%). Greater cage obliquity angle was associated with subsidence (OR 1.40 per 5°, 95% CI 1.10-1.84, p = 0.004), whereas greater cage-rim contact ratio was inversely associated with subsidence (OR 0.68 per 10%, 95% CI 0.51-0.90, p = 0.008). Cage obliquity was inversely correlated with cage-rim contact ratio (ρ = -0.370; p < 0.001) and mediolateral contact spread (ρ = -0.457; p < 0.001), but not with contact centroid. Fusion, radiographic correction loss, and patient-reported outcomes did not differ significantly by subsidence status. In this single-design cohort, greater residual cage obliquity and reduced cage-rim contact ratio were associated with subsidence, identifying insufficient rotation and reduced effective anterior rim support as potentially modifiable technical factors. These findings provide a rationale for developing and prospectively evaluating intraoperative methods to assess cage rotation and optimize rim support, although the optimal rotational target and its preventive effect require further validation.

title: Probe-mediated subcellular organelles translocation enabled ratiometric quantification of nitroreductase activity and microviscosity for hypoxia imaging and precise tumor delineation.
abstract: Quantitative assessment of hypoxia-induced nitroreductase (NTR) upregulation and pathological viscosity elevation offers a critical diagnostic parameter for precise cancer diagnostics.​ We propose a subcellular organelle translocation strategy for ultrasensitive quantification of NTR/microviscosity and subsequent precise evaluation of tumor hypoxia levels. The constructed NTR-sensitive probe Cy826 releases the fluorophore Cy468 upon NTR catalysis, accompanied by a significant fluorescence turn-on response (21.9-fold enhancement) and subcellular organelle translocation from endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to lysosomes, which effectively reduced local probe accumulation and significantly alleviated the aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) effect and spectral crosstalk in quantification process. The cyclen-based hemicyanine Cy468 is a fluorophore distinct from our previously reported Cy496, with near-infrared (NIR) emission (~ 720 nm), lower logP, and lysosomal rather than mitochondrial targeting. Cy826 displays high sensitivity (LOD = 8.2 ng/mL) and excellent selectivity toward NTR, along with a strong fluorescence enhancement under high viscosity and molecular crowding conditions. The probe also facilitates real-time monitoring of viscosity changes in ER and lysosomes, and dynamically responds to endogenous NTR activity under varying hypoxia levels. Moreover, after administration of Cy826, the considerable tumor-to-background ratio (TBR > 12) enables high-contrast imaging of hypoxic tumors from early to advanced stages with favorable biocompatibility and metabolic characteristics. Our subcellular organelle translocation strategy proposed in this study offers a novel approach to mitigating ACQ effect in quantification assignment, and the high-performance NIR fluorescent probe drafted in this work provides a prospective tool for precise tumor diagnosis and intraoperative navigation via multi-parameter imaging of hypoxic tumor microenvironment.

title: Standard anterior temporal lobectomy using a retractorless technique in patients with drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy: long-term seizure outcomes and predictors of postoperative seizure freedom.
abstract: Background Fixed brain retractors risk focal ischemia and cortical injury. Although retractorless dynamic retraction is established in skull base surgery, its role in epilepsy surgery remains poorly characterized. Objective To evaluate long-term seizure outcomes, safety, and reliability of retractorless standard anterior temporal lobectomy (ATL) in drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE), and identify predictors of seizure freedom. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 42 patients who underwent retractorless standard ATL for drug-resistant MTLE. Dynamic retraction used bipolar forceps and pressure-controlled suction. The primary outcome was seizure freedom (Engel Class Ia) at minimum 24-month follow-up; secondary outcomes were complications and resection adequacy on postoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Results At a mean follow-up of 66.3 months, 69% of patients achieved complete seizure freedom (Engel Class Ia), and 83.3% achieved freedom from disabling seizures (Engel Class I). Postoperative MRI confirmed adequate resection in 95.2% of cases. Complications were uncommon and unrelated to retraction injury. Low preoperative seizure frequency (< 3 seizures/week) was the sole independent predictor of seizure freedom (odds ratio, 24.21; P = 0.026), while higher frequency (≥ 3 seizures/week) was associated with increased recurrence risk (hazard ratio, 7.34; P = 0.042). Conclusion Retractorless standard ATL is safe and effective for drug-resistant MTLE, achieving long-term seizure control while minimizing retraction-associated risks. Preoperative seizure burden was the dominant prognostic marker, supporting early surgical intervention.

Low preoperative seizure frequency (< 3 seizures/week) was the sole independent predictor of seizure freedom (odds ratio, 24.21; P = 0.026), while higher frequency (≥ 3 seizures/week) was associated with increased recurrence risk (hazard ratio, 7.34; P = 0.042).

Conclusion

Retractorless standard ATL is safe and effective for drug-resistant MTLE, achieving long-term seizure control while minimizing retraction-associated risks. Preoperative seizure burden was the dominant prognostic marker, supporting early surgical intervention.

title: DINOv3-SAM: Fusing Semantic and Anatomical Foundation Models for Robust Medical Image Classification.
abstract: Robust medical image classification remains a persistent challenge due to heterogeneous acquisition protocols, label noise, and subtle inter-class variability. In chest radiography, these difficulties are compounded by shortcut learning from non-anatomical artifacts and projection variability, which severely undermine generalization. To address these limitations, we propose DINOv3-SAM, a dual-encoder framework that synergistically integrates complementary visual representations. The architecture combines a self-supervised DINOv3 vision transformer, which captures global semantic context, with the Segment Anything Model (SAM) image encoder, which provides anatomy-aware spatial features. The two feature streams are spatially aligned and adaptively refined through a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), which emphasizes informative channels and diagnostically relevant regions prior to classification. Notably, only the final DINOv3 layers are fine-tuned while SAM remains frozen, yielding a computationally efficient framework with only 5.3 million trainable parameters. We evaluate DINOv3-SAM across five public datasets spanning diverse modalities and diagnostic tasks: pediatric pneumonia classification, cardiomegaly detection, large-scale RSNA pneumonia detection, COVID-19 radiography, and dermatological lesion classification. A unified stratified train/validation/test protocol ensures consistent and fair evaluation across both binary and multi-class settings. Each configuration was trained three times with different random seeds, and comprehensive comparisons against reproduced CNN baselines and published state-of-the-art methods, supported by statistical significance testing, demonstrate improvements across most datasets and metrics. The proposed framework achieves a mean accuracy of 94.94% (±3.06) on pediatric pneumonia, 97.24% (±0.77) accuracy (AUC 0.998 ±0.001) on COVID-19 radiography, and a mean AUC of 0.8705 (±0.0445) on the challenging RSNA benchmark. These results underscore the efficacy of fusing self-supervised semantic representations with segmentation-informed anatomical cues to enhance robustness against dataset bias, acquisition variability, and cross-domain shifts. The proposed approach offers a reliable foundation for multi-dataset and multi-modality medical image classification in research-oriented decision-support systems.

title: Predictive Nomogram for High Ki-67 Expression using Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Identifying reliable prognostic factors for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is challenging, thereby complicating treatment and follow-up decisions. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS)-based nomogram to predict high Ki-67 expression in ccRCC. This retrospective study analysed 312 patients from two centres (training, n = 212; validation, n = 100) who underwent preoperative CEUS. Postoperative pathology confirmed ccRCC. Immunohistochemistry assessed Ki-67 expression and CD34-positive microvascular density (CD34 + MVD). A nomogram was developed using multivariate logistic regression and validated based on the area under the curve (AUC). Predictive performance was compared with tumour-node-metastasis (TNM) staging and World Health Organisation/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grading using the DeLong test. Spearman's correlation coefficients were compared among CD34 + MVD, WHO/ISUP grade, and Ki-67 expression. Significant predictors of high Ki-67 expression included tumour diameter ≥ 3.85 cm (odds ratio [OR]: 1.525, 95% confidence interval: 1.054-2.205), washout time ≤ 34.7 s (OR: 0.942, 95% Cl: 0.911-0.975), and necrosis ≥ 9.158% (OR: 1.105, 95% Cl: 1.021-1.195). The nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.858 (training set) and 0.810 (validation set), outperforming TNM staging (AUC: 0.733) and WHO/ISUP grading (AUC: 0.761). Ki-67 expression correlated negatively with CD34+MVD (r = -0.632) and positively with WHO/ISUP grading (r=0.620), whereas CD34+MVD expression was negatively correlated with WHO/ISUP grading (r = -0.607). The CEUS-based nomogram demonstrated superior predictive accuracy for high Ki-67 expression compared with TNM staging and WHO/ISUP grading, supporting its potential for personalised treatment and more precise follow-up surveillance programmes.

title: Skull-Base Synthetic CT from Brain MRI: Development, Independent-Center Validation, and Radiologist Evaluation.
abstract: We developed and evaluated a deep learning pipeline for skull-base synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generation from routine non-contrast T1-weighted and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), focusing on clinically relevant bony anatomy for neurosurgical and radiotherapy workflows. We retrospectively collected 184 manually registered T1/T2/CT triplets for training and internal validation (166/18 split) and 43 cases from a second center for independent-center validation. A three-dimensional Swin-UNETR generator was trained with bone-weighted multiscale reconstruction, perceptual, and adversarial losses. Two board-certified radiologists independently scored 16 skull-base structures, artifacts, and diagnostic acceptability on raw sCT in Hounsfield units (HU), without histogram matching; this blinded review was the primary endpoint. Acceptability was 76.7% for Rater 1 and 67.4% for Rater 2 (pooled 72.1%, cluster-robust 95% CI 58.5-82.6%), with mean structure scores from 2.67 to 4.85 out of 5. Raw sCT showed limited absolute HU calibration (global MAE 364±50 HU, bone Dice 0.38±0.09 ), with a compressed dynamic range in which air and soft tissue were overestimated and dense bone underestimated; histogram-matched outputs, reported as a secondary analysis, reached bone Dice 0.88±0.03 and bone MAE 26.31±5.03 HU. Halo artifacts were near-universal, and false-canal artifacts occurred in 21-30% of cases. The method shows promise as a radiation-free adjunct for skull-base visualization, but the present results do not support replacing dedicated CT for diagnostic, dosimetric, or physics-based applications.

title: Multi-task Model with​ Peritumoral MRI Radiomics Learning for Breast Cancer Segmentation-Guided Subtype Classification.
abstract: Accurate breast cancer molecular subtype classification is important for treatment planning, but immunohistochemical assessment may be affected by intratumoral heterogeneity and requires invasive tissue sampling. We hypothesize that segmentation-guided learning of tumor-core and peritumoral microenvironment (PTM) MRI features would improve molecular subtype discrimination over tumor-core-only analysis. A transformer-based segmentation network integrates cross-modal and multi-scale features to delineate tumors, after which the predicted masks are used to construct tumor-core and peritumoral inputs for an energy-regularized classification network. On the test cohort, the retrospective single-center study includes 381 patients with histopathologically confirmed breast cancer and corresponding DCE, DWI, T1WI, and T2WI images. The proposed method achieves a Dice coefficient of 88.29%, a Jaccard index of 79.80%, a precision of 91.98%, and a 95HD of 4.03 pixels for tumor segmentation. For molecular subtype classification, it achieves an accuracy of 84.0%, a macro-averaged sensitivity of 85.7%, a macro-averaged specificity of 94.8%, and a macro-averaged F1 score of 83.9%, providing the best overall performance among the evaluated methods. These findings support further evaluation of segmentation-guided multimodal MRI analysis for preoperative molecular subtype assessment.

title: Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Segmentation of Shoulder Anatomy on MRI: A Systematic Review.
abstract: To synthesize the performance and methodological characteristics of fully automated deep learning algorithms for shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. CENTRAL, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception through July 17, 2026. The protocol specified fully automated deep learning-based pixel-wise segmentation of shoulder MRI, an expert-derived MRI-space reference standard, and quantitative segmentation metrics. Two reviewers independently screened records; unresolved disagreements were adjudicated by a senior reviewer. Overlapping datasets were linked during synthesis. Of 354 identified records, 169 duplicates were removed, 185 records were screened, and 53 full-text reports were assessed. Thirty-five reports were included (31 journal articles and 4 full conference papers; 2018-2026). U-Net-based encoder-decoder architectures predominated, with additional region-based, transformer, adversarial, and autoencoder approaches. Dice similarity coefficients ranged from approximately 0.81-0.99 for osseous targets, 0.71-0.99 for shoulder muscles, and 0.58-0.94 for tendon or tear regions; intersection-over-union values for tear or surgical-planning regions ranged from 0.45-0.83. MRI protocols and validation designs were heterogeneous, and most reports described retrospective single-center investigations. Five reports used independent external test sets; several others included multicenter images. Overlapping cohorts precluded a valid pooled participant count. Deep learning achieved high accuracy for shoulder bones and rotator-cuff muscles in selected datasets, whereas tear-region performance was more variable. Multicenter patient-level validation and standardized annotation and reporting are needed before routine clinical deployment.

title: Diffusion Prior-Driven Vision-Language Adaptation for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection.
abstract: Unsupervised medical anomaly detection faces dual challenges of pathological data scarcity and domain gaps when transferring general-purpose vision-language models to fine-grained tasks. This study aims to address the misalignment between global semantic representations and local pathological nuances by proposing a novel hybrid supervision framework. We propose a flexible vision-language adaptation framework in which diffusion-based pseudo-anomaly synthesis serves as an optional training enhancement. For CheXpert and BUSI, region-guided diffusion generates localized pseudo-anomalies to provide additional discriminative supervision. For BrainMRI, the framework is trained exclusively on normal reference images without any synthetic anomaly augmentation, allowing us to assess its effectiveness independently of the diffusion synthesis component. The architecture incorporates a local-enhanced feature rectifier to enhance local textural representation, a zero-initialized hypersphere-aligned residual adapter for stable cross-modal manifold alignment, and a temperature-scaled mapmaker for multi-scale dense anomaly localization. Performance was evaluated across three medical imaging modalities under multiple few-shot configurations. Our method remains highly competitive compared to state-of-the-art approaches in terms of image-level detection and pixel-level localization. On the ultrasound dataset under a 32-shot setting, the framework achieved an image-level area under the curve of 94.2% and a pixel-level area under the curve of 96.6%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework across the evaluated medical imaging modalities under different training configurations. In particular, its competitive performance on BrainMRI without synthetic anomaly augmentation suggests that the vision-language adaptation framework can remain effective when offline pseudo-anomaly generation is unavailable. The code involved in this study is publicly available on website https://github.com/SWLee777/DiffVLA .

title: Propagation of Low-Dose-Induced Noise Characteristics Across Deep Learning Layers in CT Imaging.
abstract: Dose reduction in computed tomography (CT) imaging impacts diagnostic accuracy for human observers and potentially artificial intelligence (AI) systems. As noise propagates through an AI model, its characteristics change, possibly influencing model performance. This study aims to develop a configurable low-dose CT simulation tool in image-space and analyze noise behavior in deep learning (DL) layers. The noise characteristics were quantified using the noise power spectrum (NPS) within homogeneous phantom regions. NPS area under the curve (intensity) and median frequency (texture) were reported. Low-dose CT images were simulated using a custom program that was calibrated for configurable noise intensity and texture. Noise was generated at texture levels. Pre-trained U-Net features were extracted from reference and simulated low-dose images, enabling NPS-based analysis of noise propagation across deep learning layers. NPS from simulated low-dose CT images matched reference NPS for various intensity and texture values. Feature analysis revealed progressive convergence of noise characteristics across deep learning layers, with batch normalization mitigating amplification observed after convolution and ReLU activation. Differences in noise texture between low-dose simulations converge along the U-Net contracting path. The image-space simulation tool offers a viable alternative for researchers lacking access to raw data, supporting future AI-focused dose optimization studies. However, whether these outcomes translate to segmentation performance remains unclear and warrants further investigation.
