title: Diagnostic Performance and Calibration of AI Models for Thyroid Ultrasound Malignancy Classification: From TN5000 to ThyroidXL.
abstract: We evaluated cross-dataset transportability of three frozen encoders for binary benign-versus-malignant thyroid ultrasound classification using expert-defined nodule regions and one external cohort. Logistic regression classifiers using DINOv2, TinyUSFM, and ResNet18 features were developed on 3500 TN5000 images, calibrated on 477 duplicate-clean validation images and tested on 958 images. External evaluation used maximum image scores from 2083 ThyroidXL images in 739 patients with cytological or histopathological outcomes. No external retraining, recalibration or threshold adjustment was performed. Additional analyses evaluated four classifiers, encoder-recommended preprocessing and calibration intercepts and slopes. Internal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were 0.9081 for TinyUSFM, 0.8946 for DINOv2, and 0.8896 for ResNet18. Primary external AUROCs were 0.8464 (95% confidence interval, 0.8164-0.8731), 0.7954, and 0.7833, respectively. Sensitivities at frozen high-sensitivity thresholds were 0.9972, 0.9717, and 0.9887, but specificities were 0.1736, 0.1891, and 0.1373. External calibration intercepts were negative; slopes were 0.891, 0.645, and 0.697. DINOv2 ranked first externally with four of five classifiers. With recommended preprocessing, ResNet18 ranked first numerically (0.8329 versus 0.8214 for DINOv2); their paired difference was inconclusive. Encoder rankings depended on the classifier and preprocessing. These results apply to the three evaluated implementations, not pretraining strategies generally. Transported patient scores overestimated malignancy and had low specificity. Prospective assessment is needed before clinical use.

title: Critical Validation of Deep Learning-Based Cervical Vertebral Fracture Detection on Computed Tomography Localizer Radiographs.
abstract: Localizer radiographs are low-resolution two-dimensional overview images acquired prior to computed tomography (CT) scans. Their automated analysis could support the early detection of cervical vertebral fractures in trauma patients and thus enable immediate adjustment of imaging protocols. This study investigated to what extent deep learning-based methods can reliably detect such fractures on localizer radiographs, with a focus on critically validating model behavior beyond standard performance metrics. On a custom-annotated dataset of 346 trauma patients, two approaches were compared: a full-image binary classification and a two-step pipeline that first localizes the cervical spine and then classifies the cropped region. Model validity was assessed through a permutation test, occlusion testing, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, an analysis of potential confounders, and a subgroup analysis by anatomical fracture location. The full-image classifier formally achieved the highest test-set performance with a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.477, compared with 0.349 for the cervical-spine-level classifier. Our validity analysis indicates that the full-image classifier does not primarily rely on the fracture region itself, rendering it unsuitable for clinical use. This work therefore presents a case study of shortcut learning and illustrates validation methods that may be of value for comparable studies on small datasets with visually subtle targets.

title: The Deep Learning-Based Prediction Method for Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis of Thyroid Cancer Based on Multimodal Data.
abstract: Thyroid cancer is a common malignant tumor worldwide, and there is a risk of misdiagnosis or over-treatment for small-sized thyroid cancer. The key to eliminating this risk lies in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis. The traditional manual prediction methods are not ideal, so this paper proposes an intelligent prediction method based on deep learning. This method is based on common clinical examination data, including ultrasound images, ultrasound image text descriptions, and blood test data. A deep convolutional neural network model is proposed using data from these three modalities as inputs. The model integrates multimodal data features through mean cross-attention and extracts fine-grained classification information from the fused feature map through a bilinear CNN network, demonstrating strong feature discrimination ability. Through collecting data and conducting various experiments, the experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper has good performance in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis, is better than the manual prediction, and has broad application prospects. Future research will continue to strive for data collection, increasing the amount of collected data and improving multi-center representativeness, and enhancing the diagnostic and predictive capabilities of the network model through technological improvements.

title: Data Leakage and Unverified Provenance in Public Brain Tumor MRI Datasets: A Systematic Audit.
abstract: Brain tumor MRI classification studies routinely report accuracies above 99%, yet many public datasets in this domain trace to a few original sources and are often combined or cross-validated without accounting for shared origin. We audited seven brain tumor MRI datasets (34,525 images) for leakage within datasets and overlap between datasets typically treated as independent. Internal leakage was detected with perceptual hashing and rotation-aware structural similarity. Cross-dataset overlap was detected with ResNet-50 embedding similarity, checked against a random-pair baseline, a DenseNet-121 sensitivity analysis, and blinded two-rater review (all 75 sampled above-threshold pairs were true duplicates; 95% CI 95.1-100). A further blinded review just below the threshold found roughly half of the sampled pairs were also duplicates, so reported overlap is a lower bound. True-duplicate leakage between training and evaluation splits occurred in three of four datasets with predefined splits, including a peer-reviewed dataset and one documented as overlap-free. For 14 of 16 dataset pairs, 15.6-99.1% of the smaller dataset's images were automatically matched to the other, including datasets described as collected from named hospitals. In a controlled experiment on the one dataset with patient identifiers, image-level splitting yielded higher accuracy than patient-level splitting (97.10 ± 0.69% vs. 91.82 ± 2.77%; Welch's t-test, p = 0.017), with a 10.1-point drop in meningioma F1. This addresses within-dataset correlation only, so it is a conservative estimate of total inflation. Reported performance warrants cautious interpretation, and tooling for verifying dataset independence is lacking. We propose a checklist for dataset creators and researchers.

title: Observer agreement in sonographic glandular tissue component classification and sonographic breast density assessment: a multi-institutional study.
abstract: Purpose The sonographic glandular tissue component (GTC) is a potential imaging biomarker for stratifying breast cancer risk in women with dense breasts. This study evaluated the reproducibility, reliability, and clinical applicability of GTC classification and GTC-based sonographic breast density assessment in a multicenter observer study. Methods Fifteen readers (nine physicians and six sonographers) from 12 institutions independently assessed 100 paired ultrasound images twice, 1 month apart, with the dataset rearranged for the second reading. GTC was qualitatively classified into four categories according to its estimated proportion within the fibroglandular tissue (FGT): minimal, mild, moderate, and marked; minimal/mild were grouped as low GTC and moderate/marked as high GTC. Sonographic breast density was categorized as sonographic dense breast (high GTC), sonographic non-dense breast (visible fat lobules), or intermediate, with intermediate cases further divided into high or low categories using an FGT-to-FAT (subcutaneous and retromammary fat) ratio cutoff of 1. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement was evaluated using κ statistics. Results Substantial interobserver agreement was observed for the four-class GTC classification, the two-class GTC classification, and sonographic breast density assessment. Intraobserver agreement was moderate for the four-class GTC classification and substantial for the two-class GTC classification and sonographic breast density assessment. The majority-vote sonographic breast density assessment showed substantial agreement with the mammographic ground truth, whereas individual-reader assessments showed moderate concordance with mammographic breast density both overall and in intermediate-density breasts. No significant differences in agreement were observed between physicians and sonographers. Conclusion Substantial interobserver agreement and moderate-to-substantial intraobserver agreement support the reproducibility and reliability of GTC classification and GTC-based sonographic breast density assessment.

title: Accelerated aortic stenosis progression is associated with greater CT-derived extracellular volume.
abstract: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

title: Mask-aware knowledge distillation for low-latency pneumothorax classification in chest radiographs.
abstract: Accurate pneumothorax classification requires strong discrimination with low deployment cost. We developed a mask-aware knowledge distillation framework in which a mask-guided ResNet-50 teacher transferred dynamically annealed logits and lesion-weighted multilevel attention to a MobileNetV3-Small student, while masks and teacher-side components were removed at inference. A fixed stratified 20% SIIM-ACR hold-out set was reserved for testing; the remainder underwent five-fold cross-validation, with PTX-498 positives used only for training augmentation. The Mask-aware KD student achieved a mean validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of [Formula: see text], and the five-model student ensemble achieved a fixed-test AUC of 0.946 (95% confidence interval, 0.935-0.956) versus 0.950 for the teacher ensemble. Validation-selected 90% and 95% sensitivity targets yielded test sensitivities of 0.929 and 0.973. Uniform-attention KD achieved a lower AUC of 0.936. The student ensemble required 5.00 million parameters, 1.49 billion multiply-accumulate operations (MACs), and 51.00-ms single-threaded CPU latency at [Formula: see text]. Training-time lesion guidance enabled numerically similar discrimination with substantially lower inference cost. No independent external validation was performed, and generalizability across institutions, acquisition protocols, portable radiography settings, and patient populations remains uncertain; verified patient-level evaluation remains necessary before clinical translation.

title: Decoding tumor heterogeneity using MRI for predicting response to immune checkpoint inhibitors in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study.
abstract: Tumor heterogeneity hinders accurate prediction of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We developed a habitat model using routine in-phase (IP) and opposed-phase (OP) MRI sequences, which provide complementary structure- and lipid-related information, to predict response to ICI therapy in HCC. This study included 883 HCC patients from six institutions and public databases. We developed habitat, radiomics, peritumoral, clinical, and combined models to predict partial response (PR) in five institutions. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed to evaluate survival differences based on prediction scores. Habitat model interpretability was assessed using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) along with multi-omics and pathological analyses in the public databases and one external institution. The habitat model showed numerically higher AUCs among the independent models, with AUCs of 0.923, 0.918, and 0.897 in the training set and two external validation sets, respectively. The combined model also showed favorable performance with AUCs of 0.959, 0.965, and 0.955, respectively. Calibration curves showed generally close agreement, while decision curve analyses suggested potential clinical net benefit of the habitat and combined models. Patients with higher habitat scores had significantly longer progression‑free and overall survival (all P < 0.05). Exploratory biological analyses showed that the higher habitat score group was associated with enhanced immune activity, downregulated fatty acid-related pathways, and shorter tumor-inflammatory spatial distances. The IP and OP MRI-based habitat model showed potential for treatment-response prediction and prognostic stratification in patients with HCC receiving ICI therapy.

title: CT attenuation changes across freeze-thaw preservation states in donated bodies: a preliminary multi-organ anatomical analysis.
abstract: To establish the thermal preservation state as a critical pre-analytical variable in quantitative post-mortem CT of donated bodies, with the aim of enabling reliable multi-donor comparisons, improving the performance of automated segmentation tools, and providing a translational experimental model applicable to CT-guided thermal interventions. Eight body donors underwent whole-body CT in up to three preservation states: fresh, frozen (- 20 °C), and thawed. CT datasets were automatically segmented using TotalSegmentator in 3D Slicer. Mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values were extracted for major organs and tissue groups. The primary analysis was within-donor: Friedman tests with Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc comparisons in donors with complete data (n = 7), complemented by linear mixed-effects models using all available scans. Freezing produced a consistent reduction in CT attenuation across all soft tissues and muscle, with near-complete recovery after thawing. In the primary repeated-measures analysis, preservation state had a significant effect after FDR correction in six of the nine tissue groups (liver, spleen, brain, aorta, pancreas and muscle; q = 0.023-0.042), but not in kidney, heart or bone. Brain and pancreas showed the strongest effects (Kendall's W = 0.80 and 0.76). In the liver, the median within-donor change was - 59.7 HU at freezing and + 60.3 HU at thawing. Mixed-effects models confirmed a significant reduction at freezing in liver, spleen, brain, kidney, pancreas and muscle (β = -35.1 to -52.7 HU) and no residual difference after thawing in any tissue group. Bone attenuation remained stable across all preservation states. Freeze-thaw preservation systematically alters CT attenuation in soft tissues while minimally affecting bone. Preservation state should therefore be considered a critical pre-analytical variable in quantitative post-mortem CT, particularly for studies relying on automated segmentation, radiomics, and translational applications involving thermal tissue imaging.

title: Integration of weight-bearing computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging for advanced musculoskeletal statistical shape modeling of the foot and ankle.
abstract: Purpose Statistical shape models (SSMs) from three-dimensional (3D) medical imaging describe morphology variation in normal and pathologic anatomy. Within the foot and ankle, weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) is used to characterize skeletal deformity but poorly visualizes soft tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides improved evaluation of soft tissue structures but less accurate bone visualization. This methodologic analysis describes and tests reliability of a novel process to generate SSMs from coregistered MRI and WBCT structures. This method is illustrated via two example models: a combined musculoskeletal model and a distal tibia growth plate model. Methods Bilateral WBCTs and T1-weighted DIXON MRIs of the lower legs were collected from 14 individuals aged 8 to 18 with no prior lower limb surgery in a control group and hereditary neuropathy group. Bones were segmented from WBCT and manually aligned in MRI space. Alignment reliability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Six muscles were segmented semi-automatically and the distal tibia growth plate was manually segmented from MRI. Following cropping, size normalization, and alignment multi-domain SSMs were generated. SSMs were evaluated qualitatively through comparison with expected anatomy and quantitively by calculation of compactness, generalization, and specificity. Results The alignment method demonstrated excellent reliability with an intrarater ICC of 1 and interrater ICC of 0.999. The musculoskeletal model demonstrated expected atrophy in neuromuscular disease and the preliminary growth plate model showed variation in metaphyseal thickness. Both models demonstrated compactness, specificity, and generalization comparable to published SSMs, requiring 11 and 12 modes to account for 95% of population variance. Conclusion This method allows for application of shape modeling to novel questions in musculoskeletal morphology through simultaneous modeling of bone and soft tissue anatomy. Limitations include manual registration and MRI resolution. This analysis presented examples of muscle and growth plate models, but has broader applications in musculoskeletal analysis.

title: Coexistent tracheal bronchus and azygos lobe: surgical planning and operative technique for robotic-assisted right upper lobectomy.
abstract: Tracheal bronchus and azygos lobe are individually uncommon congenital anomalies arising from independent embryological mechanisms. Their simultaneous occurrence is exceptionally rare, with fewer than five cases identifiable in the published literature. We report an adult patient in whom a displaced apical segmental bronchus arising directly from the tracheal wall, a bifid right upper lobe bronchus comprising only the anterior and posterior segmental bronchi, and an associated azygos lobe. Elective robotic-assisted right upper lobectomy was undertaken for a biopsy proven primary lung cancer. Final histopathology confirmed grade 2 adenocarcinoma with clear surgical margins without lymph node involvement. Preoperative three-dimensional reconstruction was helpful for surgical planning and we describe the operative principles required to safely manage this unusual anatomical combination.

title: Deciphering intratumoral heterogeneity: An interpretable radiopathologic framework for lymph node staging in early-stage cervical cancer.
abstract: Preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) informs treatment planning in early-stage cervical cancer (CC). Traditional radiomics (TR) may obscure intratumoral heterogeneity. We developed multiparametric MRI habitat radiomics (HR) for LNM prediction and explored its histopathologic context. Patients underwent radical surgery and lymphadenectomy. Part I comprised 148 training and 63 test patients; Part II comprised 14 for spatially matched histopathology. Intratumoral voxels were clustered into habitats by K-means using T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) signals. The number of habitats was selected using validation AUC. HR/TR scores and clinical-radiological predictors were integrated by logistic regression. AUC and accuracy were compared by DeLong's and χ² tests. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) assessed contributions. Subregion-matched histopathology quantified Ki-67, CD3, CD31, and tumor-stroma ratio (TSR). LNM prevalence was 27.1% (61/225). The four-habitat HR model achieved a test AUC of 0.841 with 14 DWI/CE-T1WI-derived features. Test AUCs for clinical model (CL), TR, and HR + CL were 0.804, 0.784, and 0.890. HR + TR+CL achieved the highest AUC (0.902) and accuracy (87.30%), without a significant AUC difference from HR + CL (P = 0.277). SHAP ranked HR score above clinical lymph-node status, tumor diameter, and TR score. HR-3 exhibited highest Ki67 and lowest TSR, CD3, and CD31; HR-1 had highest TSR and lowest Ki67; HR-2 showed higher CD31 than HR-4. MRI-based HR may support preoperative LNM assessment in early-stage CC, with HR + CL representing a parsimonious candidate model for further evaluation. Spatially matched exploratory histopathology suggests possible regional tissue differences across MRI-defined habitats.

title: Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiling in Moyamoya Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by stenosis and occlusion of the internal carotid artery branches, leading to chronic ischemia and aberrant collateral vessel formation. Despite its clinical significance, the pathophysiology is not fully understood, and identification of MMD-related biomarkers may supplement invasive digital subtraction angiography, the current gold standard for diagnosis, as well as provide additional insights into prognosis and disease progression. High-throughput metabolomics and proteomics offer potential to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify diagnostic markers. Our goal is to systematically review the current literature on metabolomics and proteomics in MMD using high-throughput methods, identify candidate biomarkers, characterize implicated pathways, and assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of molecular signatures. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases through April 13, 2026, for studies analyzing serum or CSF from MMD patients using mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, or immunoassays. Studies were included if they employed case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, or RCT designs in human subjects. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disputes resolved by a third reviewer. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We extracted the top differentially expressed proteins or metabolites, results of any enrichment pathway analyses, and demographics information from each study. From 3071 studies identified, 31 were included after removing 1558 duplicates and excluding 1482 irrelevant studies. Recurrent differentially expressed proteins implicated inflammatory signaling (CRABP-I, PDGF-BB, IL-7, complement proteins), angiogenesis (VEGF, Ang-2, MMP-9), and cytoskeletal remodeling (FLNA, ZYX, keratins), while consistent metabolomic signatures highlighted BCAA elevation, urea cycle disruption, and lipid remodeling. Pathway analyses recurrently implicated immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, cytoskeletal reorganization, hypoxia signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Demographically, cohorts were predominantly adult, East Asian, and bilateral MMD, with a sample-size-weighted mean age of 40.0 years. High-throughput proteomics and metabolomics identified recurring molecular alterations in Moyamoya disease, commonly identifying inflammatory signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and cytoskeletal remodeling as potential pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite predominantly good-quality studies (mean Newcastle-Ottawa Scale 6.77 ± 0.67), major limitations included small sample sizes, single-center designs, and regional specificity. Validation in larger, ethnically diverse, multicenter cohorts is essential before clinical translation of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
abstract: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.

title: Predicting neoadjuvant chemotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer using DCE-MRI and mammographic texture.
abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) kinetic features and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) texture features for predicting pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Additionally, its predictive performance was compared with that of single-modality models. A total of 360 patients with pathologically confirmed TNBC who received NAC between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively and consecutively collected. Patients were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 252) and a validation set (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. Pre-NAC DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features were extracted. After feature selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, DCE-MRI and DBT radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were constructed. A nomogram prediction model was then developed using multivariable logistic regression incorporating clinicopathological and laboratory indicators. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, respectively. These results were subsequently compared with those of a clinical-only model and single-modality combined models. The pCR rates in the training and validation sets were 41.67% and 40.74%, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified Ki-67 proliferation index, maximum tumor diameter, background parenchymal enhancement score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, lactate dehydrogenase level, DCE-Rad score, and DBT-Rad score as independent predictors of pCR (P < 0.05). The dual-modality nomogram achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.784 (95% CI: 0.718-0.851) in the training set and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.644-0.873) in the validation set, outperforming the clinical-only model (0.727), the clinical plus DCE-Rad score model (0.761), and the clinical plus DBT-Rad score model (0.766). Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes. Furthermore, decision curve analysis confirmed the clinical net benefit of the proposed model. The multimodal radiomics fusion model based on DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features effectively predicts pCR following NAC in TNBC patients. Its predictive performance is superior to that of single-modality models. Consequently, this model offers a non-invasive imaging tool for individualized pretreatment efficacy assessment. Nevertheless, further multicenter external validation is required to confirm its generalizability. For now, it should be viewed as a decision‑support aid that informs rather than dictates treatment choices, with specific actionable thresholds to be refined in future prospective studies.

title: Type Vb double common bile duct complicated by gallbladder cancer.
abstract: Double common bile duct (DCBD) is an extremely rare biliary anomaly with subtype-dependent oncological risk. We report a case of DCBD (Choi classification type Vb) complicated by gallbladder cancer. A 75-year-old woman was incidentally found to have a gallbladder fundus tumor on screening ultrasonography. Preoperative imaging suggested gallbladder cancer within clinical T3 or less. Biliary evaluation by magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), drip infusion cholangiography-computed tomography (DIC-CT), and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) confirmed Choi type Vb DCBD without pancreaticobiliary maljunction (PBM). The patient underwent open extended cholecystectomy with a stepwise intraoperative strategy guided by frozen section analysis. Frozen section confirmed adenocarcinoma; as the cystic duct margin was tumor-free, lymph node dissection was limited to the cystic duct nodes without hepatoduodenal ligament dissection. Final pathology: adenocarcinoma (well to moderately differentiated), pT1b, pN0 (0/3), pStage IB (Union for International Cancer Control [UICC] 9th edition), pR0. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 11 and remained recurrence-free at 6 months. To our knowledge, this is the fourth reported type Vb DCBD case in the English-language literature and the first associated with gallbladder cancer. Preoperative evaluation of biliary anatomy, including PBM status, and a stepwise intraoperative approach are essential for safe and oncologically appropriate management.

title: A digital twin roadmap for adult spinal deformity.
abstract: Adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery is a high-risk, high-cost domain in which preoperative planning plays a critical role in determining alignment goals, surgical strategy, and the balance between deformity correction and treatment-related complications, yet decisions still rely heavily on static radiographs, classification systems, and surgeon experience. In parallel, medical digital twins, continuously updated, patient-specific computational models that simulate alternative treatment paths, are emerging in other medical disciplines but have not been formally articulated for ASD. In this narrative review, we adapt the recently proposed five-component medical digital twin framework (patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and synchronization policy) to adult spinal deformity by mapping each component to ASD-specific data sources, computational models, clinical workflows, and validation pathways. We outline how existing tools in ASD, including classification systems, frailty and bone-health metrics, biomechanical modeling, motion analysis, mobile health data, and machine learning risk calculators, can serve as inputs to an ASD digital twin. We highlight priority use cases, such as choosing the magnitude of surgery, bone-health-aware planning, pelvic fixation and rod strategy, and selection among open, hybrid, and minimally invasive approaches, all reframed as comparative simulations with explicit uncertainty bands. Finally, we propose a staged roadmap, from minimal viable twins evaluated via retrospective replay, to shadow-mode deployment, to oversighted clinical pilots, while detailing challenges in data harmonization, model validity, governance, and equity. Rather than claiming that a mature ASD digital twin exists today, this work offers a practical blueprint for how digital twins could evolve into auditable, patient-specific decision-support tools that augment, rather than replace, surgeon judgment in spinal deformity surgery.

title: Determination of total free acids in UiO-66 via extraction-decoupled gas-evolvement headspace detection.
abstract: The accurate quantification of free acidic species occluded within metal-organic frameworks (i.e., UiO-66) is essential for evaluating synthesis completeness, material purity, and post-synthetic processing. In this work, a rapid and automated headspace gas chromatography (HS‑GC) method was developed for the determination of total free acids in MOFs. The strategy couples ultrasound‑assisted methanolic extraction with a selective phase‑conversion reaction: the extracted carboxylic acids react stoichiometrically with bicarbonate in a sealed headspace vial to liberate carbon dioxide, which is then detected by HS‑GC. Under systematically optimized conditions, the method exhibited excellent linearity, high sensitivity with a low limit of detection, and satisfactory precision. Accuracy was confirmed by near‑quantitative spike recoveries and by close agreement with a well‑established spectrophotometric reference method. Leveraging the automated headspace platform, the procedure substantially reduced sample cycle time and enabled high‑throughput operation while markedly decreasing organic solvent consumption relative to conventional wet‑chemical protocols. This approach provides a reliable, efficient, and environmentally favorable tool for routine monitoring of free acid content in MOFs (i.e., UiO-66), facilitating quality control in both laboratory‑scale research and scaled‑up synthesis.

title: Automatic Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics for Differentiating Henoch-Schonlein Purpura Nephritis from IgA Nephropathy in Children: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To assess a noninvasive ultrasound habitat radiomics approach with automatic kidney segmentation for distinguishing pediatric Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis (HSPN) from immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). Materials and methods This retrospective multicenter study included 592 biopsy-confirmed pediatric patients from three centers (HSPN, n = 338; IgAN, n = 254). The development cohort (n = 453) was split into training (n = 362) and internal validation (n = 91) cohorts, and an independent external validation cohort (n = 139) was used for final testing. Kidney regions of interest were automatically segmented using nnU-Net. K-means clustering defined three echogenic habitat subregions, and 408 radiomics features were extracted from the whole-kidney region and habitat subregions. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and three machine-learning classifiers were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was compared with clinical and combined models. Results nnU-Net achieved high kidney segmentation performance, with a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.957 and a mean intersection over union of 0.918 in the independent healthy-child test set. Fifteen radiomics features were retained, including six whole-kidney features and nine habitat-derived features. Logistic regression showed stable performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.806 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.715-0.897) internally and 0.825 (95% CI, 0.758-0.892) externally. The combined model outperformed the clinical model in AUC in both cohorts (0.846 vs 0.717; 0.805 vs 0.733). Conclusion This deep-learning-assisted ultrasound habitat radiomics approach enabled automatic kidney delineation and showed encouraging performance as a reproducible imaging adjunct for differentiating pediatric HSPN from IgAN.

title: Atrophy-Robust Multiclass CNN Segmentation of Brainstem-Related Structures in Neurodegenerative Parkinson Syndromes.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Neurodegenerative Parkinson syndromes show regionally distinct tissue loss involving several brainstem and midbrain structures. Reliable volumetry is constrained by atlas-based segmentation in atrophy-affected brains. We developed a multiclass convolutional neural network (CNN) for the segmentation of 16 brainstem-related regions on routine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 200 manually annotated MRI datasets of patients with Parkinson's disease, atypical Parkinson syndromes, and healthy controls were used for model development and validation. A Deep Neural Patchwork model was trained on 150 datasets and evaluated in an independent test cohort of 50 participants against atlas-based segmentation using the Dice coefficient, 95% Hausdorff distance, and average symmetric surface distances (ASSD). In an extended validation cohort of 264 participants, CNN-derived regional volumes were analyzed across Parkinson's disease, progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). Results CNN segmentation outperformed atlas-based segmentation across accuracy metrics. Overall medians were 0.75 vs 0.33 for Dice, 2.0 vs 5.0 mm for 95% Hausdorff distance, and 0.30 vs 1.02 mm for ASSD. CNN-derived volumetry recapitulated established disease-associated patterns, including predominant mesencephalic, superior cerebellar peduncle, and red nucleus atrophy in PSP and more marked pontine and middle cerebellar peduncle volume loss in MSA. Conclusion The principal contribution of this study is an atrophy-robust multiclass brainstem segmentation framework. This framework may enable anatomically more faithful extraction of quantitative MRI metrics than atlas-based approaches and may reduce contamination from adjacent CSF spaces, particularly in small atrophy-affected structures.

title: Bioelectrical and optogenetic modulation for neuroimmune therapeutics.
abstract: Neuroimmune interactions are emerging as key regulators of inflammation, immunity, immune homeostasis, and disease progression. Neural circuits do not merely sense tissue injury, but also actively shape immune-cell recruitment, cytokine production, vascular function, and organ-level inflammatory outcomes. Here, we overview bioelectrical and optogenetic systems for neuroimmune modulation in diseases via the defined neural and inflammatory pathway. First, we review systemic neuroimmune modulating pathway and local neuroimmune modulators, and identify established neuroimmune molecular interactions in diseases. After that, we explain bioelectrical and optogenetic systems employed to modulate neuroimmune interactions. We evaluate representative studies with advanced delivery systems in consideration of neural target, immune effector, disease-relevant outcome, and safety. Finally, this review highlights both positive and negative clinical evidence of electroceuticals, and ultrasound-mediated and optogenetic systems predominantly in preclinical development. In summary and perspective, we prioritize and discuss the requirements for their further clinical translation. The integration of neural targeting with advanced materials and adaptive gene and drug delivery would be successfully harnessed for programmable therapies to modulate disease-relevant immune circuits without broadly suppressing host defense systems.

title: Optic Disc Features in Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: Spatial Organization and Structure-Function Associations.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether funduscopic features in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) are spatially organized and associated with structural and functional measures at presentation and outcome. Design Cross-sectional and longitudinal secondary analysis of the multicenter, QRK207 NAION treatment trial (NCT02341560). Participants Trial participants with symptomatic NAION and gradable color fundus photographs at enrollment (n=728) and Month 6 (M6; n=547). Methods We quantified hemorrhage, hyperemia, axoplasmic stasis (cotton wool spots/micro-opacities), pallid edema, and chronic changes via manual annotation. Each feature was analyzed both as presence versus absence (prespecified primary) and as burden standardized to disc area (secondary). Peripapillary swelling was graded 0-4 by degree of vessel obscuration. Spatial distribution was mapped using modified Garway-Heath sectors. We assessed associations with VF, OCT-derived swelling, and symptom duration. Main outcome measures Global and sectoral VF sensitivity (average total deviation; avgTD) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at enrollment and M6; OCT-derived peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, peripapillary optic nerve head volume, and rate of ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thinning. Results At enrollment, hyperemic swelling (88.9%) and hemorrhage (79.5%) predominated, and pallid edema was common (27.9%). Acute hyperemia clustered nasally. Hyperemic swelling area correlated with shorter symptom duration (r s = -0.12, p = 0.004). The presence of pallid edema was associated with faster GCIPL thinning (-1.12 vs -0.37 µm/day, p < 0.001), worse enrollment acuity in multivariable models (β = -6.69 letters; p = 0.002), and modestly longer symptom duration (median 11 vs 10 days; p = 0.03). Enrollment features weakly associated with VF but did not predict M6 avgTD. Inferior peripapillary swelling mildly correlated with worse enrollment superior field deviation (r s = -0.27, p < 0.001). At M6, pallor was most prevalent (86.7%), clustered temporally, and was independently associated with worse avgTD (Inferior ONH to superior VF: β=-2.07 dB; p= 0.007). Conclusions Funduscopic features in NAION exhibit distinct, topographically organized spatial and temporal patterns reflecting evolving tissue injury, but have limited standalone prognostic value for long-term visual outcomes. Notably, acute pallid edema is relatively common in NAION.

title: Assessment of sequential distalization with aligners using cone-beam computed tomography merged with intraoral scans.
abstract: Introduction Sequential distalization with clear aligners, supplemented by Class II elastics, is commonly used to treat mild-to-moderate Class II malocclusions. Although favorable clinical outcomes have been reported, the underlying mechanism of tooth movement remains incompletely understood because of the methodologic limitations of conventional analyses. Methods This retrospective study included 30 adults treated with Invisalign sequential distalization combined with Class II elastics. Pretreatment and posttreatment cone-beam computed tomography images and intraoral scans were merged using segmentation and registration software. The fused models were superimposed on stable maxillary structures with computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing software, and the movement of the maxillary first molars was quantified in 3 planes of space using a 3-dimensional coordinate system. Results The mesiobuccal cusp tip of the maxillary first molar moved distally by a mean of 1.75 mm, whereas the mesiobuccal root apex moved distally by only 0.35 mm, representing 69.7% and 27.6% of the planned movement, respectively. The achieved distal crown tipping (7.14°) significantly exceeded the planned value, whereas the mesial-out rotation (8.22°) was only slightly greater than planned. Conclusions In patients treated with sequential distalization and Class II elastics, maxillary first molar distalization occurred primarily through distal crown tipping and mesial-out rotation. Cone-beam computed tomography- intraoral scan fused models enabled precise 3-dimensional assessments of these tooth movements.

title: Offering prenatal CFTR modulators to prevent cystic fibrosis-related organ damage in utero.
abstract: Background CFTR modulator therapy has drastically improved the prognosis and quality of life for those with cystic fibrosis (CF). CF complications begin to manifest in utero, including meconium ileus, and current regulatory approvals for CFTR modulator therapy does not have a pregnancy indication. Despite this, there have been several documented cases of women taking CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with promising results of potential CFTR correction in utero. Objective To report one center's experience offering CFTR modulator therapy to pregnant women for prenatal CF treatment. Study design Eight pregnant women carrying a fetus at risk of having CF were presented with the option of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with extensive counseling on the potential benefits and risks. Records from routine clinical care from prenatal, birth, and perinatal period were collected. Results Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy. Conclusion Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy termination to successful reversal of ultrasound findings suggestive of developing meconium ileus.

title: Rising Prevalence of Metabolic Dysfunction - Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in an urban South Indian screening cohort: a Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
abstract: Purpose Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), redefined in 2023 from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, is highly prevalent globally, but population-level data using 2023 AASLD criteria and FibroScan-based assessment remain scarce in South Asia, particularly among asymptomatic adults undergoing routine health screening. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 1,103 asymptomatic adults (mean age 43.1±12.7 years; 64.1% male) undergoing FibroScan-based Master Health Check-up at a tertiary centre in Chennai, India (2023-2025). MASLD was defined as controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥249 dB/m plus ≥1 cardiometabolic risk factor; fibrosis was assessed by liver stiffness measurement (LSM). Results MASLD was identified in 716 participants (64.9%; 95% CI 62.1-67.7%). Affected individuals were older, had higher BMI, and more frequently had diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia (all p<0.01). In multivariable analysis, age, male sex, BMI, and diabetes were independently associated with MASLD. Notably, 53.4% of cases occurred in adults under 46 years, and 45.3% had normal liver function tests while 31.3% had normal ultrasound, indicating conventional screening substantially underestimates disease burden. Conclusions Nearly two-thirds of asymptomatic urban South Indian adults screened met MASLD criteria, predominantly working-age individuals under-detected by conventional tools. FibroScan-based screening should be considered in preventive health programmes to enable earlier detection.

title: Regional Radiomics Similarity Networks Reveal Specific Brain Morphological Connectivity Patterns in Migraine and Tension-Type Headaches.
abstract: Objective This study investigated structural brain alterations in migraine and tension-type headache using regional radiomics similarity network to characterize disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns. Background Migraine and tension-type headache are the most prevalent primary headache disorders involving central nervous system dysfunction. While functional magnetic resonance imaging has revealed abnormalities, structural changes remain incompletely understood. Regional radiomics similarity network, a novel approach for modeling individualized morphological brain networks, has not been applied in primary headaches. Methods We enrolled 65 migraine patients, 49 tension-type headache patients, and 53 healthy controls. Regional radiomics similarity network was constructed using 88 radiomics features. Regional mean connectivity strength and voxel-based morphometry were compared across groups. Spearman correlation was performed between network measures and visual analogue scale scores. Generative adversarial networks were used for classification. Results Voxel-based morphometry revealed gray matter volume alterations in cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions across the three groups. Regional radiomics similarity network analysis identified distinct morphological connectivity patterns: patients with migraine showed altered connectivity involving frontal, limbic, and subcortical regions, whereas patients with tension-type headache exhibited prominent alterations involving the cerebellum and thalamic-temporal connections. Exploratory partial correlation analyses suggested associations between several altered connections and pain severity. The model achieved 84.31% classification accuracy. Conclusions Regional radiomics similarity network captures disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns beyond conventional structural measurements, providing insights into structural network substrates of primary headaches. This study establishes regional radiomics similarity network as a promising neuroimaging framework for investigating brain structural alterations in migraine and tension-type headache.

title: Prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction measured by cardiac magnetic resonance in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
abstract: Introduction Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an important role in both the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), as it provides information on cardiac function, structure, and tissue characterization. Moreover, it is the gold standard for right ventricular (RV) assessment. However, evidence regarding the prognostic value of RV systolic dysfunction in this population remains limited. Objective To evaluate the prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) measured by CMR in patients with ATTR-CM. MéTODOS: This was a single-center, observational, retrospective cohort study. We included patients from an institutional ATTR-CM registry who underwent CMR within 6 months of diagnosis between 2011 and 2025. Patients with other types of amyloidosis were excluded. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CMR variables were collected. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed according to the presence or absence of RV dysfunction on CMR, defined as RVEF <50%. Univariate and multivariable Cox regression models were performed to identify predictors of the primary endpoint. TAPSE was not included in the multivariable models to avoid collinearity. Resultados A total of 100 patients were included, with a median age of 79 years [IQR 73-84]; 84% were men. Median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% [IQR 42-62], and median RVEF was 48% [IQR 38-57]. Patients with lower RVEF had higher all-cause mortality (log-rank p = 0.008, Figure). In the multivariable model including age, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP, RVEF was independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98; p = 0.002, Table). Conclusiones In our cohort of patients with ATTR-CM, RVEF assessed by CMR was independently associated with all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that RV assessment may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.

title: Impact of BRCA2, BRCA1, and Other Individual Homologous Recombination Repair Alterations on Survival in Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Background and objective The clinical significance of homologous recombination repair (HRR) alterations beyond BRCA2 in advanced prostate cancer is poorly understood. We investigated the association of individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations with outcomes of patients treated with first-line therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Methods Eligible patients from the prospective CAPTURE study underwent somatic/germ line DNA analyses using a next-generation sequencing panel including ATM, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, HDAC2, PALB2, RAD51B, and RAD54L. Association with overall survival (OS) and radiographic progression-free survival was assessed using multivariable Cox regression models comparing individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations to those in patients with BRCA2 alterations or without HRR alterations. Key findings and limitations A total of 1010 patients were included, with BRCA2 and non-BRCA2 HRR alterations found in 122 (12%) and 191 (19%) patients, respectively. BRCA1, ATM, FANCA, HDAC2, CHEK2, CDK12, and BRIP1 alterations were observed in 19 (1.9%), 69 (6.8%), 34 (3.4%), 24 (2.4%), 23 (2.3%), 20 (2%), and 15 (1.5%) patients, respectively. Patients with ATM (hazard ratio [HR] 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.20-2.30; p = 0.002) or CHEK2 (HR 1.71; 95% CI = 1.03-2.90; p = 0.039) alterations showed improved OS compared to patients with BRCA2 alterations, with similar outcomes to patients without HRR alterations. BRCA1 (HR 0.49; 95% CI = 0.30-0.80; p = 0.004), FANCA (HR 0.61; 95% CI = 0.42-0.89; p = 0.011), and CDK12 (HR 0.57; 95% CI = 0.35-0.93; p = 0.025) were associated with worse OS compared to patients without HRR alterations, with similar outcomes to patients with BRCA2 alterations. Conclusions and clinical implications Prognostic associations differ across individual HRR alterations. Although BRCA1, FANCA, or HDAC mutations were associated with a prognosis similar to that associated with BRCA2 alterations, prognosis in patients with ATM or CHEK2 alterations was similar to that in patients without HRR alterations. In the research setting, non-BRCA2 HRR alterations should be analyzed and reported as individual entities whenever possible.

title: An OCT-based Structural Evaluation Framework for Laser-Induced Retinal Lesions in Mice and Exploratory Application Under ALDH2 Modulation.
abstract: Laser-induced retinal injury models require structural assessments that capture lesion heterogeneity. We developed a five-dimensional optical coherence tomography (OCT) framework and explored its application under aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) modulation. Following 532-nm left-eye photocoagulation, mice received dimethyl sulfoxide vehicle, Alda-1, or Daidzin intraperitoneally for seven days. OCT, fundus photography, and fluorescein angiography were performed 24 h after the final dose. The framework integrated morphologic classification, five-domain severity scoring, lesion geometry, layer-specific thickness and normalized area under the thickness-distance curve (AUC), and anatomically matched contralateral comparisons. Thirty-six lesions from nine mice were analyzed. Classification and scoring showed high interobserver agreement (κ = 0.839; intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.925). After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, severity score was the only tested outcome differing significantly among subtypes; eight of 45 structural correlations were significant. In 32 matched pairs, all six thickness comparisons showed significantly lower lesion-eye values. Correlations between local thickness and normalized AUC were significant after contralateral subtraction for outer retinal and outer nuclear layer measurements at the lesion level, whereas absolute correlations were nonsignificant; only the former remained significant at the mouse level. Alda-1 and Daidzin differed in subtype composition. Mouse-clustered models indicated lower scores, greater outer nuclear layer first-point thickness, and larger margin angles with Alda-1, but mouse-level comparisons were nonsignificant. Normalized AUC and its contralateral differences showed no significant treatment differences at either level. This framework integrates qualitative, semiquantitative, and quantitative assessments to characterize OCT-visible structural features in mouse retinal laser injury models.

title: Management of Coronary Calcified Nodules: A Position Statement.
abstract: Coronary calcified nodules are an uncommon but important substrate for acute coronary syndromes, stent underexpansion, and recurrent target lesion revascularization. This consensus integrates pathologic, imaging, prognostic, and interventional evidence to guide practical decision-making. Intravascular imaging is essential for diagnosis, mechanism definition, and procedural optimization. Optical coherence tomography provides superior assessment of cap disruption and thrombus, whereas intravascular ultrasound remains valuable when contrast exposure or lesion crossing limits optical coherence tomography. Treatment should be tailored to lesion crossability, calcium distribution, and the need for mechanical scaffolding. No calcium-modification device or drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon strategy has demonstrated consistent superiority. The proposed type IIa/IIb framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Calcified nodule-related target lesion failure should be managed by correcting the dominant mechanical mechanism before antiproliferative therapy. These recommendations emphasize individualized, imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention and identify priorities for prospective comparative research.

title: Development of an Electronic Clinical Quality Measure for Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality in Diagnostic CT in Adults.
abstract: The Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure is the first automated radiology outcome measure adopted by CMS. We describe its development, specification, calculation, and adoption. Beginning in 2018, the measure was developed under a CMS cooperative agreement following the Measures Management System Blueprint, with oversight from a multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel. ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps. First, the examination is assigned to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification and Current Procedural Terminology codes. Second, size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise are computed from the DICOM dose report and pixel data; because clinical and radiology data reside in separate systems, translation software inside the hospital firewall performs the linkage and calculations automatically. Third, dose and noise are compared with category-specific thresholds derived from a reader study in which 125 radiologists rated the image quality of 734 CT examinations. An examination is out of range if either value exceeds its threshold, and the measure score is the percentage of eligible examinations that are out of range. Testing across 32 facilities in eight health systems confirmed the availability, accuracy, validity, and reproducibility of all data elements, and the National Quality Forum endorsed the measure in 2021. CMS adopted ExRad in 2023 into hospital inpatient, hospital outpatient, and clinician quality reporting programs, with voluntary reporting beginning in 2025. It is the sole outcome measure in the Diagnostic Radiology MIPS (Merit-Based Incentive Payment System) Value Pathway.

title: Dynamic Fractional Myocardial Blood Volume Mapping Using Ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR Multitasking with Subspace Dose Harmonization.
abstract: Background Fractional myocardial blood volume (fMBV) represents the vascular compartment within myocardial tissue and may reflect changes in microvascular status and health. Conventionally derived from multi-dose Modified Look-Locker Inversion (MOLLI) recovery T1 mapping with ferumoxytol, MOLLI-based fMBV requires repeated breath-holds, inter-dose image registration, and static end-diastolic estimates. CMR Multitasking enables free-breathing, non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated imaging and offers a subspace that captures shared motion and contrast dynamics. This subspace representation can be exploited to harmonize multi-dose acquisitions directly in parameter space, enabling motion-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping while reducing reliance on post-hoc image-space registration. Methods Thirteen healthy volunteers (11 females, 28.2±10.0 years) and twelve ischemic heart disease (IHD) patients (1 female, 67.2±7.1 years) underwent multi-dose ferumoxytol imaging at 3.0T using both breath-held ECG-triggered 5(3)3(3)3 MOLLI and free-running 2-dimensional Multitasking T1 mapping sequences. MOLLI-Multitasking agreement was assessed in healthy volunteers; patient data were used for exploratory dynamic fMBV analysis. Multitasking data were harmonized across respiratory- and cardiac-motion subspace dimensions for cross-dose alignment. Pixel-wise fMBV was estimated using a two-compartment water exchange model. fMBV agreement with MOLLI was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Dynamic fMBV changes were also evaluated from the Multitasking data. In IHD patients, fMBV kinetic metrics (upslope and diastolic-to-systolic distribution) for cycle-dependent variation in dynamic fMBV were computed to assess systolic compression and diastolic recoil. Cardiac positron emission tomography (PET) derived perfusion and CMR-derived strain and late gadolinium enhancement served as references. Results In healthy volunteers, Multitasking produced motion-resolved fMBV maps with strong MOLLI agreement (bias -0.11%, p=0.84). Subspace harmonization reduced cross-dose variability and aligned cardiac phases. Healthy subjects showed significant diastolic-to-systolic variation (10.55±2.12% vs. 7.73±2.76%, p=0.0004). In IHD patients, ischemic segments exhibited elevated diastolic fMBV with significant systolic compression (16.36±3.44% vs. 10.01±2.24%, p=0.013), remote myocardium showed similar phasic variation (11.16±0.68% vs. 7.98±0.57%, p<0.0001). At the same time, scar demonstrated reduced fMBV with attenuated modulation (7.74±1.95% vs. 5.59±1.97%, p=0.099). Abnormal dynamic fMBV regions corresponded to PET defects and impaired circumferential strain. Conclusion Ferumoxytol-enhanced Multitasking with subspace harmonization enables free-breathing, cardiac-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping, overcoming practical limitations of MOLLI-derived fMBV. This approach enables non-invasive assessment of dynamic myocardial blood volume across the cardiac cycle, with potential utility for characterizing microvascular function in ischemic heart disease.

title: Performance of artificial intelligence versus clinician left-ventricular segmentation of cardiac MRI for mortality prediction: a retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study.
abstract: Background Ejection fraction, a key measure of cardiac function, is used in health care for clinical decision making and risk stratification. We hypothesised that a deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) segmentation of ejection fraction obtained from cardiac MRI (CMR) outperforms expert clinician segmentation for the prediction of all-cause mortality. Methods In this retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study, we studied a cohort of 27 382 consecutive patients who underwent cardiac MRI (CMR) in the UK and the USA. Patients were referred for CMR from nine hospitals to Barts Heart Centre (BHC), London. Patients were identified from the reporting archive at BHC as having undergone a CMR between Oct 1, 2014 and Dec 31, 2019. A further cohort of patients was also identified from University of Pittsburgh Medical Centre (UPMC), Pittsburgh, PA, USA, as having undergone a CMR between June 1, 2010 and March 31, 2016. Mortality data were obtained from national and local databases. AI segmentation was done on all CMR studies, and Cox proportional hazards models were fitted to compare the prognostic value of AI-measured versus clinician-measured left-ventricular volume metrics. Model fit was compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), discrimination using C indices and the incremental value of AI over clinician segmentation using likelihood-ratio tests of nested models. Findings 27 382 patients received a baseline CMR (26 106 patients from BHC and 1276 from UPMC). The median follow-up was 5·6 years (IQR 4·4-6·9), during which 3458 (13%) of 27 382 patients died. AI ejection fraction showed better model fit (AIC 57 936 vs 58 097, ΔAIC 161 favouring AI) and marginally better discrimination (C index 0·669 vs 0·637; ΔC 0·033 [95% CI 0·026-0·041]). AI ejection fraction significantly improved model fit when added to clinician ejection fraction (χ 2 =168, p<0·0001), with only slight improvement when clinician ejection fraction was added to AI (χ 2 =7·5, p=0·023). After adjustment for age and sex, AI-derived ejection fraction showed better model fit (AIC 55 684 vs 55 742; ΔAIC 59) and had marginally better discrimination (C index of 0·781 vs 0·777; ΔC=0·004 [95% CI 0·002-0·006]). Interpretation AI-derived ejection fraction shows marginally superior prediction for mortality than clinician-derived ejection fraction in patients who had CMR. Findings support the potential utility of AI for first-line ejection-fraction measurement with clinician oversight, although this should be investigated in prospective studies. Funding National Institute for Health and Care Research Clinical Lectureship and the British Heart Foundation Accelerator Award.

title: Retraining-free multi-task MR image restoration using a pretrained diffusion model with Bayesian optimization.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) often requires long scan times, and efforts to shorten scans can lead to image degradation, such as undersampling artifacts, increased noise, and reduced spatial resolution. A restoration framework that can address multiple types of degradation without task-specific retraining would therefore be valuable. In this study, we evaluated whether a pretrained score-based diffusion model combined with Bayesian optimization, termed task guidance design with Bayesian optimization (TGD-BO), could provide retraining-free, multi-task MR image restoration for compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction, super-resolution (SR), and denoising (DN). TGD-BO incorporates data-consistency guidance and gradient guidance into the reverse diffusion process and parameterizes their time-varying strengths using compact low-dimensional B-spline-based guidance schedules. For each task, the schedule was optimized by Bayesian optimization using four paired degraded/reference slices from a single adaptation case, and the resulting task-specific schedule was then applied unchanged to an independent test set. In single-task experiments, TGD-BO improved upon the fixed-guidance diffusion baseline in denoising, compressed-sensing reconstruction, and super-resolution, although the improvement in super-resolution was modest. Compared with task-specific supervised baselines, TGD-BO did not uniformly achieve higher peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) or structural similarity (SSIM); in super-resolution, it showed lower PSNR and SSIM but better perceptual similarity as assessed by learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). In joint-task experiments, schedules optimized directly for DN + CS and DN + SR yielded numerically better image-quality metrics than applying the corresponding single-task schedules. Sensitivity analyses showed that the selected schedule and test performance were unchanged when 1, 4, or 8 slices from the same adaptation case were used, whereas changing the adaptation case substantially affected test performance. These results suggest the feasibility of adapting a single pretrained diffusion prior across multiple MR image restoration tasks through guidance calibration without task-specific weight retraining, while indicating that robustness to adaptation-case selection and computational cost require further investigation.

title: Measurement-derived residual-risk verification through four-way k-space partitioning in self-supervised accelerated brain MRI.
abstract: Self-supervised accelerated MRI reconstruction reduces dependence on fully sampled training targets, but it does not inherently provide a separate basis for verifying whether reconstructed image content remains locally consistent with acquired measurements. We developed a measurement-derived verification framework that partitions acquired k-space into four roles: reconstruction input, self-supervised reconstruction-loss evaluation, residual-risk learning, and reserved verification. Residuals from the reserved measurements were transformed into spatial residual-risk targets using density-compensated adjoint projection, probe-based gain normalization, anatomical support weighting, percentile scaling, and logarithmic compression. Using fastMRI brain multicoil data, we evaluated 201 training, 40 calibration, and 40 AXT2 test volumes, comprising 636 test slices and 999,792 sampled pixels. The primary Full-CNN achieved AUPRC 0.8348, mean absolute error 0.0834, Spearman correlation 0.9389, and AUROC 0.9818. The secondary A4-CNN achieved AUPRC 0.8452 with similar scale and rank agreement. MRI-volume intervals achieved at least 90% sampled-location coverage in 39 of 40 test volumes for both predictors. AUPRC declined and MAE increased with fewer reserved measurements and under AXFLAIR sequence shift. Residual-risk maps showed moderate correspondence with fully sampled reference error and differed from the tested predictive-variance measures. The framework provides a measurement-derived verification layer for assessing local residual inconsistency in self-supervised accelerated MRI without requiring fully sampled development targets.

title: Diffusion tensor imaging and structural MRI reveal early microstructural injury and progressive atrophy of the olfactory bulb in type 1 diabetic rats.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) can detect early olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) rats and to investigate their relationship with structural and histopathological changes. Methods Control and STZ-induced T1DM rats underwent DTI, high-resolution structural MRI and histological examination at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), axial diffusivity (Da), and radial diffusivity (Dr) were measured in the olfactory nerve layer/glomerular layer/external plexiform layer (ONL/GL/EPL), granule cell layer (GCL), and subependymal zone (SEZ). Results Compared to the controls, T1DM rats showed decreased FA and increased MD, Da, and Dr. in the ONL/GL/EPL at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. In the GCL, FA was decreased, whereas Dr. was increased.. No significant diffusion abnormalities were detected in the SEZ. Ultrastructural examination revealed axolemmal disruption, demyelination, reduced axoplasmic content, and axonal vacuolization in the ONL. Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) demonstrated olfactory bulb atrophy as early as 2 weeks, initially involving the GCL and SEZ, with more extensive and regionally heterogeneous atrophy at 12 weeks. Nissl staining confirmed structural atrophy, and increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity supported apoptosis-related tissue injury. STZ-induced T1DM causes early, layer-specific olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities and progressive structural atrophy. Conclusion The differing spatial and temporal distributions of diffusion abnormalities and atrophy suggest that DTI and volumetric MRI capture partially distinct aspects of diabetes-associated olfactory bulb injury. DTI may provide a sensitive, noninvasive approach for detecting early microstructural abnormalities before widespread structural loss develops.

title: NA-DIP: A Noise-Aware Deep Image Prior for Generating Dedicated Brain PET-Quality Images from Whole-Body PET Acquisitions.
abstract: Purpose To generate dedicated brain PET-quality images from routine whole-body PET acquisitions by robustly enhancing the brain region using a noise-aware deep image prior (NA-DIP) approach. Methods NA-DIP integrates anatomy-guided priors derived from patient-specific μ-maps or MR images, a regularization strategy for enhanced denoising, and a variance-based early stopping criterion that adaptively monitors noise without requiring prior noise assumptions. Using noisy PET images as self-supervised targets, the method was first evaluated using simulation data spanning three noise levels to investigate the trade-off between noise suppression and bias. It was then applied to brain images extracted from 90-s-per-bed-position whole-body acquisitions from 15 pediatric FDG-PET studies spanning a broad range of patient demographics, physiological variability, and image noise levels. Using the corresponding 360-s-per-bed-position dedicated brain scans as the reference, NA-DIP-enhanced images were evaluated for noise reduction, standardized uptake value (SUV) accuracy, and image quality in a blinded reader study. Results NA-DIP demonstrated a superior noise-bias trade-off compared with Gaussian filtering and conventional DIP stopping strategies, particularly under high-noise conditions. The inclusion of MR or μ-map guidance further improved performance. Across pediatric patients, NA-DIP-enhanced 90-s images exhibited lower noise than the corresponding 360-s dedicated brain images while showing modest variability in SUV measurements. Blinded readers rated the NA-DIP-enhanced images as comparable to or better than dedicated brain images in most cases. Conclusion NA-DIP enhanced brain PET images from whole-body acquisitions demonstrated good quantitative agreement and image quality comparable to or exceeding the reference, supporting the feasibility of eliminating separate dedicated brain scans.

title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.
abstract: Purpose To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort. Design External validation in a prospective population-based cohort. Participants Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts. Methods We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV). Main outcome measures Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC). Results Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility. Conclusions The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.
