title: Management, Upgrade Rates, and Radiologic Surveillance of Screen-Detected High-Risk Breast Lesions.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the prevalence, upgrade rate, and radiologic surveillance management of high-risk lesions (HRLs) detected at screening mammography in a Dutch breast cancer screening population. Materials and Methods This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included patients recalled from the Dutch breast cancer screening program between January 2009 and July 2019. Incidence rates, diagnostic work-up, radiologic surveillance, and upgrades to (pre)malignancy after surgical excision and during radiologic surveillance were evaluated. Results Among 17 809 recalled patients, 514 patients with a mean age of 58 years ± 8.1 (SD) were diagnosed with an HRL. The incidence rate of HRLs was 0.83 per 1000 screens and 2.89 per 100 recalls. The majority of HRLs consisted of papillary lesions (34.4% [177 of 514]) and atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) (31.1% [160 of 514]). Surgical excision was performed in 233 cases (45.3%), resulting in 58 HRLs (24.9%) being upgraded to (pre)malignancy. Invasive tumors were mainly found in papillary lesions with atypia and ADH. Of patients diagnosed with an HRL, 324 (63.0%) had an indication for radiologic surveillance. Of these, 257 (79.3%) underwent surveillance, with 109 (42.4%) completing the recommended 5-year surveillance trajectory. During surveillance, 26 patients (10.1%) developed a (pre)malignancy. Invasive tumors were more frequently identified among HRLs upgraded during surveillance than among HRLs upgraded after surgical excision (17 of 26 [65%] vs 16 of 58 [28%]; P = .001). HRLs upgraded to invasive cancer were more likely to be triple-negative compared with screen-detected cancers (9.1% [3 of 33] vs 6.6% [215 of 3277]; P < .001). Conclusion Overall, 16.3% (84 of 514) of screen-detected HRLs were associated with a diagnosis of (pre)malignancy after surgical excision or during radiologic surveillance. Completion of the recommended 5-year surveillance trajectory was achieved in fewer than half of patients undergoing surveillance. title: Pancolitis due to Tuberculosis Masquerading as Inflammatory Bowel Disease in a 43-Year-Old Woman: Diagnostic Challenges in a Resource-Limited Setting-A Case Study and Literature Review From Ethiopia.
abstract: Background Gastrointestinal tuberculosis (GI TB) predominantly affects the ileocecal region, making primary colonic involvement exceptionally rare. In TB-endemic, resource-limited settings, differentiating colonic TB from inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-particularly Crohn's disease (CD)-presents a formidable diagnostic dilemma owing to overlapping clinical, radiological, and ileocolonoscopic features, often leading to diagnostic delays, misdiagnosis, and subsequent complications. Initial clinical presentation treatment and diagnostic re‐evaluation In May 2026, a 43-year-old Ethiopian woman presented to Jimma University Medical Center with a 10-month history of progressive colicky abdominal pain, chronic watery diarrhea, postprandial nonbilious vomiting, and significant weight loss. Prior empirical regimens of antihelminthic agents and broad-spectrum antibiotics administered at peripheral health facilities yielded no clinical improvement. Initial laboratory workup revealed microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin: 8.5 g/dL), a significantly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (92 mm/h), hypoalbuminemia (2.8 g/dL), and a normal carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level (4 ng/mL). Ileocolonoscopy demonstrated superficial ulceration involving the ascending colon and hepatic flexure in a continuous form with numerous inflammatory polyps, and a small deep ulceration at the terminal ileum. Initial histopathology demonstrated chronic active inflammation without evidence of malignancy or granuloma formation. With a presumed diagnosis of CD, treatment was initiated with prednisolone and azathioprine, which might have contributed to the suspected deterioration of the clinical condition, warranting re-evaluation with contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated diffuse, long-segment circumferential wall thickening involving the terminal ileum, the entire colon, and the rectum, alongside pericolic fat stranding, a mesenteric phlegmon, and multiple necrotic mesenteric lymph nodes, with the largest measuring 2 × 3 cm with peripheral rim enhancement. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the necrotic lymph nodes revealed epithelioid granulomas and characteristic caseous necrosis. With the above evidence, terminal ileitis and pancolitis due to TB were considered, immunosuppressive medications were discontinued, and standard antituberculosis therapy (2RHZE/4RH) was promptly initiated. The patient started to experience clinical improvement, achieving full resolution of her constitutional and abdominal symptoms and gaining weight at 1 month of follow-up. Conclusion Diagnosing GI TB-especially in atypical sites such as the colon-presents a critical challenge in resource-limited, TB-endemic settings, where differentiating it from IBDs, especially CD, is vital to prevent severe complications from inappropriate therapy. To avoid misdiagnosing GI TB as IBD (which risks disseminated infection from immunosuppression) or IBD as TB (which worsens bowel stricture, fistulae, and perforation), clinicians must perform mandatory pretreatment TB screening using radiologic, immunologic, molecular, and culture modalities before initiating immunosuppressive agents. Furthermore, diagnostic accuracy requires obtaining deep submucosal biopsies during ileocolonoscopy to detect characteristic granulomatous lesions if present. Finally, when an empirical anti-TB trial is necessary, it must be strictly time-limited and followed by objective re-evaluation at 8 weeks-including repeat endoscopy and biopsy-rather than relying solely on clinical symptomatic improvement.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. Methods This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome. Results Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979]; P =0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes ( P =0.115). Conclusions Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

title: The Association of MRI-Derived Tissue Bridge Morphometrics with Baseline Impairment and Recovery in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Subanalysis of the RISCIS Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Early prognostic biomarkers are essential to optimize treatment and trial design in spinal cord injury (SCI). The Riluzole in SCI Study (RISCIS), a multicenter randomized controlled trial, provided evidence on secondary analyses that riluzole improved functional recovery in acute cervical SCI. The current analysis uses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess lesion and tissue bridge morphometrics against baseline impairment, functional recovery, and treatment response in RISCIS participants. In this preplanned ambispective subanalysis, 24 participants underwent T2-weighted MRI for acute cervical SCI together with neurological and functional assessments to 12 months. A subset also had diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), used to extract fractional anisotropy (FA) values. Segmentation with the Spinal Cord Toolbox (v7.2) gave ventral, dorsal, and total tissue-bridge widths and lesion volume and length. Associations with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) grade, upper extremity motor score (UEMS) and total motor score (TMS), lower extremity motor score (LEMS), light touch and pinprick sensory scores, Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) domains at baseline and follow-up were analyzed with regression models adjusted for age and sex. Overall recovery across TMS, SCIM, and SF-36 Physical Component Summary was analyzed with an O'Brien-style global statistical test (GST). Interactions tested whether bridge metrics modified riluzole's effect. At baseline, greater ventral ( β = 9.65, p = 0.017) and total ( β = 6.16, p = 0.021) tissue-bridge widths were associated with higher TMS, and ventral width with higher UEMS ( β = 6.61, p = 0.010). Larger dorsal (odds ratio [OR] = 21.92, p = 0.013), ventral (OR = 4.91, p = 0.049), and total (OR = 3.70, p = 0.019) bridges corresponded to less severe baseline AIS grade. Pinprick scores increased with ventral ( β = 26.56, p = 0.020) and total ( β = 17.50, p = 0.023) bridge width, and light touch scores increased with total bridge width ( β = 16.22, p = 0.045). No imaging metric was associated with LEMS. These individual-metric associations were nominally significant but did not survive correction. In GST analyses, larger ventral ( T = 4.63, p = 0.012, p '= 0.048) and total ( T = 4.30, p = 0.019, p '=0.048) bridges predicted greater overall recovery; both remained significant after correction and were stable across sensitivity analyses. Ventral and total bridge width showed nominally significant interactions with riluzole treatment for upper-limb motor recovery. Exploratory DTI findings were inconclusive and sensitive to individual observations: both the FA-recovery association and the observation of poor outcome despite a preserved tissue bridge rested on a single participant. Overall, we found that midsagittal tissue-bridge width measured ∼72 h after injury from standard-of-care T2-weighted MRI was associated with baseline injury severity and multidomain functional recovery, at a timepoint substantially earlier than the 1 month at which tissue bridges have previously been quantified. Because edema may obscure lesion margins this early, acute bridge widths may underestimate spared tissue resolvable later. The treatment-interaction observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective confirmation. These findings support MRI-derived tissue bridges as candidate biomarkers for prognostication and enrichment of neuroprotective trials in SCI.

Interactions tested whether bridge metrics modified riluzole's effect. At baseline, greater ventral (β = 9.65, p = 0.017) and total (β = 6.16, p = 0.021) tissue-bridge widths were associated with higher TMS, and ventral width with higher UEMS (β = 6.61, p = 0.010). Larger dorsal (odds ratio [OR] = 21.92, p = 0.013), ventral (OR = 4.91, p = 0.049), and total (OR = 3.70, p = 0.019) bridges corresponded to less severe baseline AIS grade. Pinprick scores increased with ventral (β = 26.56, p = 0.020) and total (β = 17.50, p = 0.023) bridge width, and light touch scores increased with total bridge width (β = 16.22, p = 0.045). No imaging metric was associated with LEMS. These individual-metric associations were nominally significant but did not survive correction. In GST analyses, larger ventral (T = 4.63, p = 0.012, p'= 0.048) and total (T = 4.30, p = 0.019, p'=0.048) bridges predicted greater overall recovery; both remained significant after correction and were stable across sensitivity analyses. Ventral and total bridge width showed nominally significant interactions with riluzole treatment for upper-limb motor recovery. Exploratory DTI findings were inconclusive and sensitive to individual observations: both the FA-recovery association and the observation of poor outcome despite a preserved tissue bridge rested on a single participant. Overall, we found that midsagittal tissue-bridge width measured ∼72 h after injury from standard-of-care T2-weighted MRI was associated with baseline injury severity and multidomain functional recovery, at a timepoint substantially earlier than the 1 month at which tissue bridges have previously been quantified. Because edema may obscure lesion margins this early, acute bridge widths may underestimate spared tissue resolvable later. The treatment-interaction observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective confirmation. These findings support MRI-derived tissue bridges as candidate biomarkers for prognostication and enrichment of neuroprotective trials in SCI.

title: A review of medical image segmentation research based on bibliometrics.
abstract: BackgroundMedical image segmentation is a fundamental step in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning, and its research landscape has expanded rapidly with the advancement of artificial intelligence. A systematic bibliometric overview of this field is therefore needed to clarify its intellectual structure and emerging trends.ObjectiveTo provide a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the global research landscape, developmental trends, collaboration networks, and emerging hotspots in the field of medical image segmentation over the past decade.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was performed on 21,437 publications related to medical image segmentation, indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2016 to 2025. The analysis systematically examined publication outputs, country-level contributions, author collaboration networks, journal distributions, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.ResultsThe annual publication count increased remarkably from 25 in 2016 to 5,207 in 2025. China contributed the largest share with 11,556 publications, followed by the United States (3,272) and India (1,924). Core researchers formed stable intra-team collaborations, though inter-team cooperation remained limited. Keyword and citation analyses identified deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Transformers, U-Net, and their variants as dominant methodological themes. Case studies on skin and lung segmentation revealed differential research attention and international collaboration patterns across anatomical targets. A historical trajectory analysis showed methodological evolution from traditional image processing to fully convolutional networks and U-Net, and subsequently to hybrid architectures integrating attention mechanisms and Transformers.ConclusionMedical image segmentation has experienced substantial growth, driven by deep learning innovations. Future research may increasingly focus on multimodal foundation models capable of generalizable segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios. This bibliometric review offers researchers a valuable reference for understanding the intellectual structure and frontiers of the field.

title: Tractography-Based Insights into Neuroplasticity and Clinical Heterogeneity in Parkinson's Disease Subtypes.
abstract: Parkinson's disease shows substantial heterogeneity across motor, cognitive, and non-motor domains, reflecting variable patterns of neurodegeneration and compensation across distributed brain circuits. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) tractography enables pathway-specific characterization of white-matter alterations and provides a framework for linking clinical subtypes to tract-level patterns that may be obscured by skeleton-based or connectomic averaging. Here, we synthesize white-matter evidence across motor, cognitive, genetic, and prodromal dimensions of PD heterogeneity, using tractography as an organizing framework within a broader dMRI and multimodal context. We review diffusion approaches ranging from diffusion tensor imaging to free-water, neurite, and fixel-based models. We distinguish pathway reconstructions from other diffusion and imaging analyses and consider how complementary approaches inform, but do not uniquely determine, interpretations of degeneration and subtype-specific neuroplasticity. Emerging methods, including harmonization pipelines, radiomic tractometry, and machine learning classifiers, may further improve tract-level sensitivity and reproducibility. Cognitive subtypes illustrate how posterior association and limbic tract degeneration, together with cholinergic and noradrenergic dysfunction, shape clinical progression. Integrating tractography with molecular, genetic, functional, and clinical markers may support subtype-specific biomarkers for risk stratification, prognosis, and targeted neuromodulation or rehabilitation strategies, although longitudinal and external validation is required before routine use.

title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.
abstract: Background Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency. Case description We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder. Conclusion Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

title: Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy Versus Percutaneous Endoscopic Interlaminar Discectomy for Highly Migrated Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Comparative Study With Quantitative MRI-Based Decompression Analysis.
abstract: Study designRetrospective comparative cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare the perioperative, clinical, and radiographic outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) and percutaneous endoscopic interlaminar discectomy (PEID) in the treatment of highly migrated lumbar disc herniation (HMLDH).MethodsA total of 128 patients with single-level HMLDH who underwent UBE (n = 63) or PEID (n = 65) between June 2022 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. All patients completed a minimum follow-up period of 2 years. Perioperative variables, complications, and reoperation events were analyzed. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Radiographic decompression was quantitatively assessed using the postoperative dural sac cross-sectional area (DSCA) expansion rate measured on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).ResultsCompared with PEID, UBE was associated with a significantly shorter operative time, less endoscopic hemostasis time, and lower fluoroscopy time. Intraoperative blood loss was lower in the PEID group. Early postoperative back pain was significantly lower in the PEID group, whereas no significant between-group differences were observed in long-term VAS or ODI outcomes. The overall complication rate was significantly lower in the UBE group. In addition, UBE achieved a significantly greater DSCA expansion rate and a lower rate of residual disc fragments than PEID.ConclusionUBE and PEID achieved comparable long-term clinical outcomes in patients with HMLDH. UBE demonstrated advantages in perioperative efficiency, radiographic decompression, and reduced radiation exposure. Furthermore, UBE was associated with a lower overall complication rate, primarily attributable to a lower incidence of postoperative nerve root irritation.

title: Influence of dominant sequence artifacts on generative AI for virtual contrast-enhancement in breast MRI.
abstract: Background Virtual contrast-enhanced (vCE) breast MRI is a deep learning approach for generating contrast-like images from non-contrast acquisitions. As diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) has emerged as a major contributor to enhancement synthesis, understanding the influence of DWI-related image artifacts is important for the robustness and potential clinical implementation of AI-based contrast-free imaging approaches. We evaluated the robustness of a pix2pix-based vCE synthesis model to artifact-contaminated DWI during training and inference. Materials and methods This IRB-approved, retrospective study included 1,974 multiparametric breast MRI examinations (mean age: 49 years) acquired with two clinical routine 3T MRI scanners (2017-2022). High b-value (b = 1500 s/mm 2 ) DWI images were automatically classified for high-intensity (HI) and low-intensity (LI) artifacts using a pretrained neural network. A pix2pix 2D-GAN was trained either after excluding artifact-affected slices (vCE-clean) or using all available slices (vCE-all). Performance was evaluated using image similarity metrics, lesion-based analysis, reader assessment, and correlation of artifact scores with reconstruction errors. Results Excluding artifact-affected slices during training resulted in a small but statistically significant increase in whole-image structural similarity index (SSIM) with small effect size (vCE-all 0.843 ± 0.034; vCE-clean 0.849 ± 0.031, p < 0.001, d av = 0.20). However, lesion-based metrics and qualitative ratings of lesion enhancement and image quality were comparable between models. During Inference, strong LI DWI artifacts were associated with higher lesion-based errors. Conclusion Controlling for artifacts on diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) during vCE training only minorly influenced technical metrics but not perceived image quality/lesion enhancement. In contrast, severe signal-loss artifacts during inference impaired local performance, highlighting the importance of image quality control during potential deployment.

title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
abstract: Background and aims Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated. Results Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50). Conclusion The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

title: Computed tomography anatomy of the pony thorax and abdomen and an example of a clinical application.
abstract: Background In veterinary medicine, computed tomography (CT) is a valuable diagnostic tool that provides detailed cross-sectional images with higher contrast resolution than conventional radiography. However, owing to the large body-size of horses, CT has been primarily limited in equine veterinary practice to imaging of the head, neck, and extremities, as imaging studies of the thoracic and abdominal cavities are not possible with standard gantry size in medium-to-large horses. In this study, we aimed to characterise the normal thoracic and abdominal anatomy of ponies using CT and to describe an example of the potential clinical applications of abdominal CT. title: Quantitative imaging-pathology correlation in nodular fasciitis and diagnostic discrimination from sarcoma.
abstract: Objectives To investigate associations between key magnetic resonance imaging features of nodular fasciitis (NF) and quantitative histopathologic biomarkers, and to evaluate whether their integration provides complementary information for differentiating NF from soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in diagnostically equivocal settings. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 128 patients with NF and 133 with STS who underwent preoperative 3-T MRI between May 2023 and June 2025. Two blinded musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated predefined imaging features, including fascial tail sign, T2 heterogeneity score, enhancement pattern, perilesional edema, and mean/minimum apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Histopathology quantified cellular density, collagen content, and myxoid degeneration. Imaging-pathology correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis and multivariable regression. Diagnostic performance of MRI-only, pathology-only, and combined models was evaluated using logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), area under the curve (AUC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation. Results T2 heterogeneity correlated positively with myxoid degeneration (ρ = 0.52) and negatively with collagen content (ρ = -0.28) (p < 0.001). Mean ADC correlated inversely with cellular density (ρ = -0.63, p < 0.001). Mean ADC was significantly higher in NF than STS (p < 0.001). The combined model outperformed MRI alone (AUC, 0.96 vs 0.89) and demonstrated greater net clinical benefit. Bootstrap validation confirmed stable performance (mean AUC, 0.960; 95% confidence interval, 0.938-0.978). Conclusion Imaging features of NF were associated with underlying stromal and cellular substrates. Integrating imaging features with quantitative pathology biomarkers may support radiology-pathology concordance assessment in selected diagnostically equivocal cases. Key points Question How can we improve radiology-pathology concordance and reduce interpretative variability for NF cases presenting with suspicious, diagnostically equivocal magnetic resonance imaging findings? Findings T2 heterogeneity and diffusion measurements are associated with stromal composition and cellularity, while predefined MRI features demonstrated substantial-to-excellent inter-reader agreement. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

title: AI-accelerated compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon MRI: prospective validation of image quality and preliminary assessment of staging accuracy versus contrast-enhanced CT.
abstract: Objectives To prospectively validate an AI-accelerated MRI protocol combining L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon cancer staging, compared with contrast-enhanced CT (CECT). Materials and methods This single-center study (August 2022-April 2024) enrolled 132 patients with pathologically confirmed colon cancer who underwent both 3.0-T non-contrast MRI and CECT within 1 week. Patients unable to complete an MRI were excluded. MRI sequences included T1- and T2-weighted imaging and diffusion-weighted imaging. Image quality was assessed using a 4-point Likert scale, alongside quantitative analysis of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and edge rise distance (ERD). Surgical pathology correlation was available for 33 cases. Five radiologists independently reviewed the images. Results Among 153 matched examination pairs from 132 patients (mean age, 58 ± 11 years), AI-MRI outperformed CECT in both qualitative and quantitative measures. MRI yielded higher image quality scores (4 [IQR 3-4] vs. 3 [IQR 3-3]), improved CNR (5.5 [IQR 4.2-7.0] vs. 1.3 [IQR 0.7-2.2]), and reduced ERD (1.6 mm [IQR 1.2-2.8] vs. 3.7 mm [IQR 2.8-5.0]). MRI provided superior peritoneal sharpness (75.8%) and colonic wall visualization (100%), and superior or equivalent tumor conspicuity (92.2%) and nodal assessment (86.9%), whereas CECT demonstrated better artifact control (45.1%). In preliminary analyses, MRI achieved higher T-staging accuracy (78.8% vs. 30.3%) and N-staging specificity (93.3% vs. 13.3%). Conclusion The AI-accelerated MRI protocol significantly outperformed CECT in image quality and preliminary staging accuracy for colon cancer evaluation while eliminating radiation exposure. Key points Question Can an AI-accelerated MRI protocol provide superior image quality and staging performance compared with contrast-enhanced CT, which has limited diagnostic accuracy for colon cancer staging? Findings AI-accelerated MRI using L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction achieved superior image quality and higher preliminary staging accuracy than contrast-enhanced CT. Critical Relevance Statement AI-accelerated MRI improves image quality and staging confidence without radiation exposure, supporting its potential to enhance preoperative assessment and clinical decision-making in colon cancer.

title: Deep learning-based quantification of CT changes after 1 year of pirfenidone treatment as a prognostic marker in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the prognostic value of changes in deep learning-based CT quantification following 1 year of pirfenidone treatment in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Materials and methods This study included patients with IPF who received at least 1 year of pirfenidone between September 2009 and March 2022 at two hospitals. The extent of normal lung and fibrosis (sum of reticular opacity and honeycombing) was quantified on baseline and 1-year follow-up chest CT scans using a deep learning-based tool, and the changes were calculated. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or lung transplantation; the secondary outcome was a ≥ 10% absolute decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) occurring after the 1-year follow-up. Associations between changes in CT quantification and these outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression analyses. Results A total of 436 patients (341 men; mean age, 69.8 years) were included. Greater preservation of normal lung extent over 1 year was associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) per 5% increase: 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.85, 0.96; p < 0.001), whereas increases in fibrosis extent were associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR per 5% increase: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.06, 1.27, p = 0.002). Regarding the secondary outcome of ≥ 10% absolute FVC decline, only the change in fibrosis extent remained a significant predictor (adjusted HR per 5% increase: 1.26, 95% CI: 1.09, 1.45, p = 0.001). Conclusions Changes in deep learning-based CT quantification results over 1 year of pirfenidone treatment demonstrated significant prognostic value in patients with IPF. Key points Question Disease progression and mortality in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) continue to occur unpredictably beyond 1 year of pirfenidone treatment. Findings Changes in deep learning-based quantification of normal lung and fibrosis extent after 1 year of pirfenidone treatment were significant prognostic predictors. Critical relevance statement Incorporating 1-year changes in deep learning-based CT quantification improves prognostication of mortality, lung transplantation, and lung function decline, supporting more individualized risk stratification in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Diagnostic performance benchmarks of MRI for prostate cancer: a large-scale cohort study of 33,759 patients.
abstract: To evaluate the real-world diagnostic performance of PI-RADS for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) across large-scale worldwide cohorts. This multicenter observational study included 20,429 patients from nine Chinese institutions and a published worldwide meta-analysis dataset comprising 13,330 patients for comparison. All PI-RADS assessments were extracted from original MRI reports produced by clinical radiologists as part of standard diagnostic workflows. Summary receiver operating characteristic curves were constructed using a bivariate random-effects model, and center-level areas under the curve (AUCs) were pooled via random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses were conducted. PI-RADS exhibited overall discriminatory performance for csPCa across nine Chinese cohorts comparable to the META results from 70 studies, though significant inter-center variation was observed. Using a PI-RADS ≥ 3 threshold, pooled sensitivity was 92.6% and specificity was 51.5%. At a PI-RADS ≥ 4 threshold, pooled specificity improved to 78.1%, with a sensitivity of 81.5%. The overall diagnostic performance was consistent across thresholds: The summary ROC (SROC) AUC was 0.903 for PI-RADS ≥ 3 and 0.826 for PI-RADS ≥ 4 in detecting csPCa at the meta-analysis level. Subgroup analyses indicated better performance among older patients (≥ 70 years) and those with higher PSA levels (> 20 ng/mL). PI-RADS v2.1 outperformed v2 or earlier versions in most clinical scenarios. This large-scale real-world study provides critical multicenter evidence supporting the use of PI-RADS in clinical practice worldwide, while also revealing substantial variability in scoring and diagnostic performance across institutions. The findings offer an evidence-based overview of PI-RADS implementation in China and worldwide, highlighting both its utility and inconsistencies. Question What are the real-world PI-RADS diagnostic performance benchmarks for clinically significant prostate cancer detection across diverse Chinese multicenter institutions versus global data? Findings PI-RADS demonstrated good overall performance (SROC AUC 0.903 at a threshold of ≥ 3), with superior discriminatory ability in older patients, higher PSA levels, and v2.1 users. Critical relevance statement This article critically assesses substantial inter-institutional heterogeneity in PI-RADS performance, highlighting that pooled estimates should not replace local calibration and that regionally adapted implementation strategies are essential for advancing clinical radiology practice.

title: Feasibility of one-stop multi-energy dynamic photon-counting perfusion CT for resectable HCC evaluation: lesion detection and histopathological correlations.
abstract: To assess the feasibility of one-stop multi-energy dynamic volume perfusion photon-counting CT (VP-PCCT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) evaluation, including lesion detection and correlations with histopathology. From July 2024 to June 2025, 407 participants with suspected malignant liver lesions prospectively underwent VP-PCCT, and 177 patients with pathology-confirmed HCC who received three-phase energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) were retrospectively enrolled for comparisons of image quality and lesion detectability. Single-phase images reconstructed from VP-PCCT perfusion datasets were compared with EID-CT. Perfusion parameters were analyzed between groups stratified separately by histological grade and microvascular invasion (MVI), and logistic regression was employed to identify independent indicators. Ninety-two participants [median age, 62 years (IQR, 53-69); 76 males] with pathology-confirmed HCC were included in the VP-PCCT group and matched with 92 in the EID-CT group. Compared with EID-CT, 40-keV VP-PCCT provided comparable image quality for HCC and vessels with a similar tumor detection rate but a lower radiation dose. title: Time-dependent diffusion MRI in determining mismatch repair status of endometrial cancer.
abstract: Objectives Mismatch repair (MMR) proteins are important in determining therapeutic strategy in endometrial cancer (EC). We investigated the role of microstructural parameters derived from time-dependent diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (td-dMRI) in differentiating MMR status of EC. Materials and methods This prospective single-center study enrolled patients with suspected EC who underwent preoperative td-dMRI. Tumors were classified as MMR-deficient (dMMR) and MMR-proficient (pMMR) by immunohistochemistry. The microstructural parameters, including intracellular volume fraction ( vin ), cell diameter ( d ), cellularity ( ρ ), extracellular diffusivity ( Dex ), and water exchange rate constant ( kin ), were derived by fitting td-dMRI data with three methods (IMPULSED, JOINT, and EXCHANGE), together with the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Differences in these microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR EC were compared. The diagnostic performances were evaluated by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Eighty-two patients (17 dMMR, 61.8 ± 10.1 years and 65 pMMR, 58.6 ± 11.8 years) were recruited. dMMR EC exhibited higher vin , ρ and lower Dex , ADC values than pMMR EC (p ≤ 0.003). IMPULSED and JOINT demonstrated higher AUCs than conventional ADC (p = 0.025 and 0.046, respectively). The combined selected microstructural parameters ( vin and Dex ) derived from JOINT achieved an AUC of 0.903; JOINT demonstrated superior parametric stability and marginally better calibration than IMPULSED. Conclusion In this exploratory study, td-dMRI discriminated between dMMR and pMMR ECs, providing information on the intricate microscopic organizational structures in tumors. The microstructural parameters may serve as a promising method to improve the diagnostic efficacy of diffusion-weighted MRI in differentiating MMR status of EC. Key points Question There remains an unmet need for noninvasive, preoperative tools to assess DNA MMR status in EC. Findings td-dMRI showed significant differences in microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR tumors. Relevance statement td-dMRI shows potential as a noninvasive imaging approach for preoperative assessment of MMR status in EC and may support individualized treatment planning.

title: Patient-specific biophysical AI-powered modeling for predicting RFA volumes in HCC.
abstract: Objectives To clinically evaluate a fully automated, artificial intelligence-powered, patient-specific biophysical model for predicting radiofrequency ablation (RFA) volumes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and to compare its performance with manufacturer-provided ablation estimates. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 96 RFA procedures in 65 HCC patients treated using a single ablation with a cluster needle. Tumors, needle position, and postablation zone were manually segmented on periprocedural computed tomography. Liver parenchyma and vascular structures were automatically extracted using deep learning. A graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated biophysical model simulated heat transfer, vascular heat-sink effects, and tissue necrosis using patient-specific anatomy and procedural data. Correlations between ablation volume manually segmented and clinical or anatomical parameters (ablation time, ablation tip temperature, tumor-capsule distance, vessel proximity, type, and diameter) were assessed. Model-predicted volumes were compared with ground truth and manufacturer estimates using relative volume difference (RVD) and volume similarity. Results Final ablation volumes showed wide variability (7.9-78.8 cm³) and were not correlated with any individual clinical or anatomical parameter (Pearson r - 0.02 to 0.29). Across 94 evaluable cases, simulated and ground-truth volumes were similar (p = 0.165), while manufacturer estimates significantly overestimated ablation volume (p < 0.001). The model achieved a median RVD of 0.39 (interquartile range 0.24-0.57), significantly lower than the manufacturer's algorithm (1.04; 0.64-1.61). Incorporating patient-specific ablation time further improved accuracy. Simulation was fast (0.45 s per second of ablation on GPU). Conclusion A fully automated, patient-specific biophysical model substantially improves RFA ablation volume prediction in HCC compared with manufacturer approximations, supporting its potential role in personalized treatment planning and outcome standardization. Key points Question In patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, can a fully automated, AI-powered, patient-specific biophysical model predict radiofrequency ablation volume more accurately than manufacturer-provided estimates? Findings A fully automated, AI-powered biophysical model integrating patient-specific anatomy and vasculature predicted RFA volume significantly better than manufacturer estimates (median relative volume difference (RVD) 0.39 versus 1.04). Relevance statement Accurate ablation volume prediction could support personalized radiofrequency ablation (RFA) planning, reduce reliance on operator experience, and standardize treatment margins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), potentially improving local tumor control and reducing recurrence in cirrhotic patients undergoing thermal ablation.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques. Materials and methods A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques. Results Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts. Conclusion Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention. Key points Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

title: Central and peripheral Neurolymphomatosis, a rare involvement of DLBCL on PET/CT.
abstract: In this paper we present two rare cases of patients suffering from diffuse large B-cell lymphoma initially treated with chemotherapy. During follow-up, they presented with central and peripheral neurological symptoms, respectively. On PET/CT, intense uptake of FDG was seen indicating neurolymphomatosis. Because of the localization it was not possible to take a biopsy for histological examination, but clinicians relied on imaging, clinical course and laboratory tests for a final diagnosis. Both patients died shortly after this examination underlining the poor prognosis of neurolymphomatosis.

title: Smartwatch-based pelvic tracking system for augmented reality navigation in total hip arthroplasty: a preliminary clinical study.
abstract: Background Accurate assessment of pelvic orientation is essential for acetabular cup placement during total hip arthroplasty (THA). Conventional pelvic tracking systems generally rely on dedicated tracking hardware and optical tracking infrastructure. We developed a smartwatch-based pelvic tracking system integrated with an augmented reality (AR) navigation platform and evaluated its preliminary clinical performance. Methods This retrospective study included 30 hips of 27 consecutive patients who underwent primary THA using a smartwatch-based pelvic tracking navigation system between May 2025 and April 2026. The system utilizes a commercially available smartwatch fixed to the iliac crest as a pelvic tracking device and communicates orientation information to a smartphone-based AR navigation platform via Bluetooth. Acetabular cup orientation was evaluated using postoperative CT. Absolute radiographic inclination (RI) and anteversion (RA) errors were calculated as absolute differences between the final intraoperative navigation measurements and postoperative CT measurements. Results The mean absolute RI error was 2.8° ± 2.1°, and the mean absolute RA error was 3.6° ± 2.2°. Postoperative CT measurements were within 5° of the final intraoperative navigation measurements for RI and RA in 86.7% and 70.0% of hips, respectively. Navigation was successfully completed in all 30 hips, with no conversion to a backup technique. Additional bench testing demonstrated reproducible smartwatch reattachment and reduction of time-dependent relative orientation differences following FPP invocation. Conclusions This study demonstrated the feasibility of integrating a commercially available smartwatch into a pelvic tracking system for THA navigation. The smartwatch-based pelvic tracking platform achieved a preliminary range of cup-positioning accuracy without requiring continuous optical visualization of a pelvic reference marker while utilizing a compact and widely available consumer wearable device. This study represents the first step toward wearable-device-based navigation in arthroplasty.

title: Redefining the EPCAM Phenotype: Deletion Architecture Determines Lynch Syndrome Cancer Risk.
abstract: Purpose To characterize the cancer phenotype and clinical presentation across molecularly distinct EPCAM deletion subgroups and determine how the phenotype varies with MSH2 involvement. Methods We retrospectively evaluated 662 unrelated probands undergoing hereditary cancer multigene panel testing (MGPT) with isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions (n = 22), isolated EPCAM 3' deletions (n = 96), contiguous EPCAM full-gene deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 64), contiguous EPCAM 3' deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 116), MSH2 gross deletions (n = 155), and MSH2 nonsense/frameshift (ns/fs) variants (n = 209). Lynch syndrome (LS)-associated cancer prevalence, tumor spectrum, and PREMM5 scores were compared across cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression estimated cancer-specific associations relative to a MGPT-negative reference cohort. Results Isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions, comprising 18.6% of observed isolated EPCAM deletions, were not significantly associated with LS-associated cancers. The LS-associated cancer prevalence was 13.6% in this cohort, compared with 54.6% with isolated EPCAM 3' deletions and 64.1%-72.2% in MSH2 -involving cohorts ( P < .001). title: LC-WGS-based Chromosomal Instability Analysis of EUS-FNA Specimens for Diagnosing Solid Pancreatic Lesions.
abstract: Background Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) is widely used to obtain tissue for the diagnosis of solid pancreatic lesions, but indeterminate or inconclusive pathology remains challenging. This study evaluated low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (LC-WGS)-based chromosomal instability (CIN) analysis as a salvage diagnostic strategy for EUS-FNA specimens. Methods Patients with solid pancreatic lesions undergoing EUS-FNA were prospectively enrolled. Genomic DNA from FNA specimens was analyzed by LC-WGS, and CIN results were classified as positive or negative using a prespecified threshold. Diagnostic performance was assessed against a composite reference standard. Results The analysis included 51 patients. Conventional pathology showed a sensitivity of 55.3% and an accuracy of 66.7%. The patients were classified into three groups: Salvage, defined as indeterminate, suspicious, or nondiagnostic initial pathology (n = 12); Malignant Control, defined as final malignant diagnosis with conclusive initial pathology (n = 26); and Benign Control, defined as final benign diagnosis with benign initial pathology (n = 13). The CIN analysis achieved a sensitivity of 81.6%, a specificity of 92.3%, an accuracy of 84.3%, a positive predictive value of 96.9%, and a negative predictive value of 63.2%. In the Salvage group, CIN correctly identified malignancy in 9 of 12 unresolved cases. Combining CIN with pathology increased sensitivity to 86.8% and accuracy to 88.2%. Conclusion An LC-WGS-based CIN analysis may provide complementary molecular information for solid pancreatic lesions with nondefinitive EUS-FNA pathology.

title: Klippel-Trenaunay Syndrome Prenatal Diagnosis: Two Case Reports and a Review of the Literature.
abstract: BACKGROUND Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is an exceedingly rare congenital disorder attributed to a sporadic mutation in the PIK3CA gene, which impairs normal blood and lymphatic vessel development. The syndrome is classically defined by a triad of congenital features: cutaneous port-wine stains, venous malformations, and progressive limb hypertrophy. Prenatal recognition of KTS is uncommon, and its sonographic features can overlap with other congenital vascular anomalies, making early diagnosis challenging. CASE REPORT This report reviews 2 cases of prenatally diagnosed KTS at our institution. In both fetuses, prenatal ultrasound demonstrated marked swelling and thickening of the soft tissues within the right thigh. Within these hypertrophic soft tissues, tortuous and dilated arterial and venous channels were visualized; some veins exhibited a honeycomb-like structural pattern. Color Doppler imaging revealed abundant intralesional blood flow signals. Following induced abortion, gross anatomical examination of both fetuses disclosed reddish skin discoloration over the right lower extremity. The diagnosis of KTS was established based on concordant prenatal ultrasound findings and post-abortion macroscopic anatomical evaluation. CONCLUSIONS The diagnostic cornerstone of prenatal KTS lies in the sonographic detection of disproportionate soft-tissue and bony overgrowth accompanied by characteristic vascular malformations. It is equally imperative to rigorously differentiate these ultrasound findings from those of other overgrowth syndromes and vascular anomalies, and to assess for potential severe complications that may affect perinatal prognosis. An accurate prenatal diagnosis, coupled with multidisciplinary perinatal management involving obstetricians, geneticists, and neonatal specialists, is essential for optimizing pregnancy counseling and improving overall clinical outcomes.

title: Resolution of Severe Jaundice Following Hepatic Artery Infusion of Bevacizumab and 5-Fluorouracil With Oral Regorafenib in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer：A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatic artery infusion (HAI) chemotherapy has been established as an indispensable treatment for hepatic metastatic colorectal cancer (CRLM), particularly in patients with multiple lesions. CASE REPORT We report the case of a patient diagnosed with liver metastasis from sigmoid colon cancer. The patient underwent hepatic segmentectomy and resection of the colon lesion in April 2019, following 8 cycles of systemic chemotherapy. After 4 postoperative courses of chemotherapy, the patient was monitored with regular follow-up. However, by November 2021, the patient had experienced 2 episodes of hepatic lesion recurrence and received late-line chemotherapy, combined with transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) and radiotherapy. In April 2024, the patient presented with severe jaundice, with total bilirubin (TB) up to 204 μmol/L (≈12 mg/dL), and concurrent abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple hepatic lesions without evidence of biliary obstruction. After thorough discussion, shared decisionmaking led to the initiation a treatment regimen consisting of HAI with fluorouracil and bevacizumab, along with regorafenib. Because the bilirubin level decreased the next morning after the first infusion, additional cycles were performed, and subsequent arteriography showed a gradual transition from diffuse neoplastic abnormal staining to normal vascular patterns, and the liver lesions were significantly reduced in size. CONCLUSIONS Given the patient's poor adherence to regorafenib and its low late-line efficacy reported in the literature, we believe that HAI likely contributed more significantly to this case. While regorafenib's contribution cannot be fully excluded, this case shows that patients with heavily pretreated CRLM accompanied by jaundice can tolerate HAI of bevacizumab and fluorouracil.

title: From Hunterian to Hunterian: the posterior malleolar fracture.
abstract: Background The posterior malleolar fracture (PMF) is now understood through three-dimensional imaging and mechanism-based classification, yet this understanding is not new. We argue that its central mechanism (rotation of an axially loaded talus within the ankle mortise) was inferred by Bonnin three-quarters of a century ago, obscured by an era of radiographic, size-based description, and later confirmed and made visible by computed tomography (CT). This continuity is frequently overlooked in the wider literature. Methods We present a narrative review of the primary historical literature alongside contemporary CT-based and cadaveric studies. Results Bonnin's cadaveric experiments showed that a rotating, axially loaded talus behaves as a wedge within the mortise, splitting the posterior tibial margin (the injury we now term a rotational pilon fracture) and he held that damage to the plafond, not the size of the fragment, determined the prognosis. Attention later shifted to the proportion of articular surface involved - a quantity poorly measured on radiographs and divorced from mechanism. CT has since reintroduced the mechanism in living patients: the Mason-Molloy classification describes three pathomechanical types that confirm and refine Bonnin's observations, and management has moved from size thresholds to classification-guided fixation. Conclusions Bonnin and Mason, two Hunterian Professors separated by more than half a century, performed essentially the same investigation with the tools available to them and reached the same conclusion. Recognising that the modern classification visualises a mechanism Bonnin had already inferred (rotation of a loaded talus) restores a continuity the wider literature has largely missed.

title: [Modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea].
abstract: Objective: To explore the feasibility, safety and efficacy of modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy in the treatment of specific types of obstructive sleep apnea（OSA）. Methods: The clinical data of 28 OSA patients with Friedman type Ⅱ or Ⅲ and mandibular micrognathia admitted to Foresea Life Insurance Guangzhou General Hospital and its collaborating institutions from January 2021 to December 2024 were collected and analyzed. All patients underwent modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy, and corresponding auxiliary procedures were combined according to the obstruction level: modified uvulopalatopharyngoplasty（UPPP） was added for patients with tonsillar hypertrophy or palatopharyngeal plane stenosis, lingual tonsillectomy for those with lingual tonsillar hypertrophy, and midline glossectomy or radiofrequency ablation of the tongue for those with significant tongue hypertrophy and retraction. Preoperative three-dimensional reconstruction of maxillofacial CT combined with Mimics software was performed for surgical planning to determine the parameters of double trapezoidal osteotomy（height: 14-16 mm, upper width: 20-22 mm, lower width: 23-25 mm）. During the operation, osteotomy, advancement（about 12 mm） and "Z"-shaped titanium plate fixation were completed according to the plan. Postoperative follow-up was conducted regularly to evaluate the efficacy. Results: All 28 operations were performed uneventfully, with an operation time of（95±15） minutes and intraoperative blood loss of（50±10） mL. Postoperatively, 6 patients had mild mental swelling and ecchymosis, which subsided spontaneously 3-5 days after surgery; 3 patients had transient numbness of the lower lip（in the distribution area of the mental nerve）, and the sensation recovered within 1 month after surgery; 2 patients had mandibular midline fracture and mild loosening of bone fragments due to forceful mouth opening and teeth clenching 3 days after surgery, which healed after fixation with dental arch guide plate for 3 months by the department of stomatology without affecting the final efficacy. All patients were hospitalized for 5-7 days after surgery and discharged uneventfully, without serious complications such as massive postoperative hemorrhage, dyspnea, surgical site infection, or titanium plate loosening. At the 6-month follow-up, the average snoring VAS scores before and after surgery were 7.75±1.82 and 3.61±1.75, respectively, and the average ESS scores were 9.93±4.97 and 5.54±3.09, respectively, with statistically significant differences（ P <0.05）. Comparison of polysomnography results before and after surgery showed that the average AHI was（47.87±26.33） events/h and（20.89±18.35） events/h, respectively, with a statistically significant difference（ P <0.01）, and the average AHI decreased by 56.36% after surgery compared with before surgery. The lowest oxygen saturation was（72.29±12.64）% before surgery and（83.50±7.93）% after surgery, with a statistically significant difference（ P <0.01）. Facial evaluation at 6 months after surgery showed that the appearance of mandibular retrognathia was significantly improved in 26 patients（76.5%）. Conclusion: Modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy, fixed by tenon-and-mortise, yields high stability and a low complication profile. It can effectively enlarge the retroglossal airway, ameliorate obstructive sleep apnea（OSA） symptoms, optimize facial contour, and improve patient satisfaction simultaneously. This procedure holds high clinical application value for patients with Friedman type Ⅱ or Ⅲ（non-very severe） OSA associated with mandibular micrognathia. For patients with severe OSA, combined multi-level surgery or noninvasive ventilation therapy is required. Rigorous patient selection and exclusion of very severe cases are the keys to ensuring the success rate of treatment.

title: [Evaluation of airway obstruction and surgical outcomes in OSA patients with small tonsils through drug-induced sleep endoscopy].
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the upper airway obstruction patterns in obstructive sleep apnea（OSA） patients with tonsils of grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° using drug-induced sleep endoscopy（DISE）, and to analyze the outcomes of DISE-guided surgery. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on OSA patients with grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° tonsil size treated between 2017 and 2020. Obstruction characteristics were recorded according to the VOTE classification based on DISE. The characteristics of upper airway obstruction were compared across subgroups stratified by OSA severity and tongue base position（grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° : low-grade tongue base collapse; grade Ⅲ°-Ⅳ°: high-grade tongue base collapse）. Patients who underwent DISE-guided surgery and completed follow-up were further enrolled to assess surgical efficacy and identify factors affecting postoperative outcomes. Results A total of 112 patients were included in the DISE analysis, including 30 patients with low-grade tongue base collapse and 82 with high-grade tongue base collapse. Retrovelar obstruction had the highest prevalence（66.7% to 84.1%） among all obstruction sites. The proportion of oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse increased with the severity of OSA. Forty-five patients completed surgery and follow-up. Surgery was performed according to DISE-based surgical planning. The surgical success rate in the low-grade tongue base collapse group（76.9%） was higher than that in the high-grade tongue base collapse group（52.9%）, but the difference was not statistically significant（ P =0.259）. Postoperative AHI and percentage of time with oxygen saturation below 90% were significantly lower in the low-grade tongue base collapse group（ P <0.05）. Among patients with complete concentric collapse of the retrovelar space（CCC） or complete oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse（O）, the surgical success rate was 81.8% in the low-grade tongue base collapse group versus 50.0% in the high-grade tongue base collapse group（ P =0.193）. Among 6 high-grade tongue base collapse patients presenting with isolated CCC/O who underwent velopharyngeal surgery combined with partial glossectomy, 4 were effective（66.7%）; all 3 patients who underwent velopharyngeal surgery alone were ineffective. Conclusion The velopharyngeal region is the primary site of obstruction in OSA patients with grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° tonsils and merits careful consideration during surgical planning. Patients with a low-grade tongue base collapse achieve better responses to DISE-guided surgery. For patients with high-grade tongue base collapse and CCC/O collapse subtype, combining tongue base surgery with velopharyngeal surgery may improve surgical outcomes.

Patients who underwent DISE-guided surgery and completed follow-up were further enrolled to assess surgical efficacy and identify factors affecting postoperative outcomes.

Results

A total of 112 patients were included in the DISE analysis, including 30 patients with low-grade tongue base collapse and 82 with high-grade tongue base collapse. Retrovelar obstruction had the highest prevalence（66.7% to 84.1%） among all obstruction sites. The proportion of oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse increased with the severity of OSA. Forty-five patients completed surgery and follow-up. Surgery was performed according to DISE-based surgical planning. The surgical success rate in the low-grade tongue base collapse group（76.9%） was higher than that in the high-grade tongue base collapse group（52.9%）, but the difference was not statistically significant（P=0.259）. Postoperative AHI and percentage of time with oxygen saturation below 90% were significantly lower in the low-grade tongue base collapse group（P<0.05）. Among patients with complete concentric collapse of the retrovelar space（CCC） or complete oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse（O）, the surgical success rate was 81.8% in the low-grade tongue base collapse group versus 50.0% in the high-grade tongue base collapse group（P=0.193）. Among 6 high-grade tongue base collapse patients presenting with isolated CCC/O who underwent velopharyngeal surgery combined with partial glossectomy, 4 were effective（66.7%）; all 3 patients who underwent velopharyngeal surgery alone were ineffective.

Conclusion

The velopharyngeal region is the primary site of obstruction in OSA patients with grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° tonsils and merits careful consideration during surgical planning. Patients with a low-grade tongue base collapse achieve better responses to DISE-guided surgery. For patients with high-grade tongue base collapse and CCC/O collapse subtype, combining tongue base surgery with velopharyngeal surgery may improve surgical outcomes.

title: Adversarial robustness of deep learning-based thyroid nodule segmentation in ultrasound.
abstract: Deep learning-based segmentation models are increasingly integrated into clinical imaging workflows, yet their robustness to adversarial perturbations remains incompletely characterized, particularly for ultrasound images. We evaluated adversarial attacks and inference-time defenses for thyroid nodule segmentation in B-mode ultrasound. Two black-box adversarial attacks were developed: (1) Structured Speckle Amplification Attack (SSAA), which injects boundary-targeted noise, and (2) Frequency-Domain Ultrasound Attack (FDUA), which applies bandpass-filtered phase perturbations in the Fourier domain. Three inference-time mitigations were evaluated on adversarial images: randomized preprocessing with test-time augmentation, deterministic input denoising, and stochastic ensemble inference with consistency-aware aggregation. Experiments were conducted on a U-Net segmentation model trained on cine-clips from a database of 192 thyroid nodules. The baseline model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.76 (SD 0.20) on unperturbed images. SSAA reduced DSC by 0.29 (SD 0.20), from 0.76 to 0.47, while maintaining high visual similarity (SSIM = 0.94). FDUA resulted in a smaller DSC reduction of 0.11 (SD 0.09), from 0.76 to 0.65, with lower visual fidelity (SSIM = 0.82). Against SSAA, all three defenses significantly improved DSC after correction, with deterministic denoising showing the largest recovery (+0.10, p < 0.001), followed by randomized preprocessing (+0.09, p < 0.001), and stochastic ensemble inference (+0.08, p = 0.002). No defense achieved statistically significant improvement against FDUA, although recall consistently improved at the cost of reduced precision. The tested inference-time defenses therefore partially mitigated spatial-domain perturbations, whereas statistically significant DSC recovery was not demonstrated against frequency-domain perturbations, highlighting attack-specific challenges in adversarial robustness evaluation.

title: Enhancing medical image segmentation with HCE-Net: A heterogeneous feature collaborative extraction network.
abstract: Medical image segmentation occupies a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Conventional segmentation techniques struggle to accommodate the intricate representational attributes of medical images, while prevailing deep learning segmentation models predominantly adopt homogeneous single encoders and linear feature fusion paradigms, thereby exhibiting inherent limitations in contextual modeling, fine-grained feature excavation, and contour segmentation accuracy. To address such dilemmas, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Collaborative Feature Extraction Network (HCE-Net). Establishing a dual-path heterogeneous encoding architecture, this network excavates complementary feature representations in a parallel manner. An Orthogonal Fusion Module (OFM) is elaborately devised to integrate Sobel edge priors with multi-scale convolutions, enabling the precise capture of edge and contour characteristics. A Diversified Receptive Field Module (DFM) is constructed to consolidate multi-scale detail manifestations and preserve global contextual cues. Furthermore, Adaptive Aggregation Connection (AAC) is embedded within skip connection branches to supplant conventional simplistic concatenation, efficaciously mitigating the technical bottleneck of heterogeneous feature fusion. Comparative experiments conducted on three publicly accessible medical datasets, encompassing dental radiographs, pulmonary CT scans, and retinal vascular images, demonstrate that HCE-Net substantially elevates segmentation accuracy, enhances boundary integrity, and ameliorates the general robustness of the model. It manifests distinguished application prospects across diverse medical image segmentation scenarios.

title: Clinical outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation stratified by paraspinal muscle degeneration: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate pain and functional outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH) stratified by preoperative paraspinal muscle degeneration, and to examine whether degeneration grade was associated with 2-year outcomes. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 129 patients with single-level LDH who underwent surgery between December 2021 and December 2023 and had complete preoperative, 1-month, 6-month, and 2-year follow-up data. Two blinded spine surgeons independently graded bilateral multifidus fatty infiltration from 0 to 4 on axial T2-weighted MRI at the mid-disc level; linearly weighted kappa was 0.967(95% CI, 0.937 to 0.989). Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using covariate-adjusted patient-level random-intercept mixed-effects models with degeneration grade treated as a categorical factor, followed by adjusted 2-year regression and post hoc sensitivity analyses. Results Of 136 screened patients, 129 were included after excluding 2 with incomplete records and 5 lost to follow-up. The cohort included 64 men and 65 women, with a mean age of 57.36 ± 11.63 years; grades 0-4 included 13, 25, 33, 32 and 26 patients, respectively. All grades improved substantially. In covariate-adjusted mixed models treating grade as a factor, the grade effect was significant for back pain VAS (P < 0.001), leg pain VAS (P = 0.010), and ODI (P < 0.001). The time-by-grade interaction was nominally significant for leg pain VAS (P = 0.036) but not after false-discovery-rate adjustment (q = 0.053), and not significant for back VAS and ODI. Each one-grade increase was associated with higher 2-year back pain VAS (β = 0.114, 95% CI, 0.001 to 0.227, P = 0.048) and ODI (β = 1.001, 95% CI, 0.168 to 1.833, P = 0.019), but not leg pain VAS. Conclusions Fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery was associated with substantial pain relief and functional improvement across all multifidus degeneration grades. More severe degeneration showed modest prognostic associations with residual back pain and disability, but the estimated effects were smaller than published minimal clinically important differences. These findings should inform cautious counseling and hypothesis generation rather than be used as a standalone surgical decision rule.

title: Literature Review of the Utility of Ultrasound for Adolescent and Child Ankle Injuries.
abstract: Pediatric posterior ankle pain is a common and challenging presentation due to the complex anatomy and a broad differential diagnosis that includes apophysitis, tendon injuries, fractures, impingement syndromes, infection, and inflammatory arthropathies. Initial evaluation typically consists of physical examination and radiographs, which are often inconclusive and may result in delayed diagnosis, repeat imaging, and/or prolonged immobilization. Magnetic resonance imaging is the gold standard for most of these injuries, but it is expensive and logistically difficult for the pediatric population. A rapid, accessible, and cost-effective imaging modality is needed to improve early detection and management. This review evaluates the role of ultrasound in assessing posterior ankle pathology in pediatric patients. Ultrasound demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy in identifying Achilles tendon tears and differentiating partial- from full-thickness injuries while also assisting in treatment decision making through dynamic tendon gap assessment. It is recommended in several studies for evaluating Achilles tendinopathy and may have predictive value for future symptoms. Emerging evidence supports its adjunctive role in Sever disease and posterior ankle impingement syndrome as well. For osseous and infectious conditions, ultrasound can identify findings suggestive of calcaneal stress fractures, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. Although magnetic resonance imaging remains the gold standard for these diagnoses, ultrasound improves the detection of joint effusions and synovitis and enhances the accuracy of diagnostic joint aspirations. Overall, ultrasound is a dynamic, radiation-free modality that serves as a powerful adjunctive tool in evaluating pediatric posterior ankle pain.

title: YOLOv11-based segmentation of vitiligo lesions using standardized clinical photography.
abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a YOLOv11-based deep learning framework that automatically segments vitiligo lesions in standardized clinical photographs captured under controlled conditions, enabling reproducible lesion quantification across longitudinal visits. Methods Standardized photographs from 18 patients were acquired at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months under controlled imaging conditions, including fixed lighting, camera settings, and color calibration. Images underwent preprocessing involving resizing, color and illumination normalization, noise reduction, and geometric standardization. Expert dermatologists generated binary lesion masks that were used as ground truth for training a one-stage YOLOv11 segmentation model. Model performance was evaluated using patient-wise data splits and 5-fold cross-validation. Results The proposed model achieved 95 % accuracy, 92 % precision, 89 % recall, 90 % F1-score, with mAP@0.5 values of 0.878 (bounding box) and 0.892 (mask) from precision-recall analysis. Qualitative review indicated consistent segmentation quality across follow-up visits and moderate illumination variations, though formally stratified quantitative analysis by visit was not performed in this study. Visual assessment demonstrated close agreement between predicted and expert-annotated lesion boundaries, with minor under-segmentation observed mainly in low-contrast peripheral regions. Conclusions Standardized clinical photography combined with a YOLOv11-based segmentation framework enables reliable vitiligo lesion delineation and has potential for integration into quantitative disease monitoring and clinical decision-support systems.
