title: Current findings, application, and diagnosis of magnetic resonance imaging in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder within the motor neuron disease (MND) spectrum, characterized by progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. The clinical phenotype ranges from pure motor syndromes to forms with cognitive and behavioral impairment, and the pathological burden extends beyond the motor system. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, supported by electrophysiology and exclusion of mimics. Therefore, objective imaging biomarkers are urgently needed. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used as an auxiliary and differential diagnostic tool in ALS. T1- and T2-weighted imaging can assess cortical thickness, gray matter atrophy, and signal changes. Diffusion tensor imaging probes white matter microstructure. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy detects neurochemical alterations. Resting-state functional MRI assesses functional connectivity and network organization. Susceptibility-weighted imaging is sensitive to iron and calcium deposition. Ultra-high-field MRI provides higher resolution and improved metabolite quantification. This critical review summarizes current findings on MRI in ALS, but importantly organizes the evidence by the specific question being addressed: pathological/histological correlates, diagnostic or discriminatory performance, and clinical associations with phenotype, severity, progression, and prognosis. We also discuss major limitations, including methodological heterogeneity, limited standardization, small and clinically heterogeneous cohorts, frequent use of healthy rather than disease controls, and scarce multicenter validation. Although advanced MRI has revealed robust group-level alterations, none of these techniques has yet become established in routine clinical diagnosis of ALS. We, therefore, distinguish promising research findings from validated clinical biomarkers and outline priorities for future translation.

title: Association between medial meniscus extrusion and joint effusion persistence at 1 month in knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: [Purpose] Joint effusion is common in knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and contributes to functional limitations and disease progression. Persistence at 1 month is clinically relevant, as it may predispose patients to long-term effusion; however, the associated intra-articular lesions remain unclear. We aimed to identify intra-articular lesions associated with effusion persistence at 1 month using ultrasonography (US) for effusion quantification and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for lesion assessment. [Participants and Methods] This retrospective cohort study included 57 patients with medial compartment KOA and joint effusions. Joint effusion was quantified as the suprapatellar pouch distance (SPP-d) by US at baseline and 1 month. Baseline intra-articular lesions were graded using the MRI Osteoarthritis Knee Score. Participants were classified into persistent (SPP-d ≥4 mm) and non-persistent (SPP-d< 4 mm) effusion groups at 1 month. Binary logistic regression identified lesions independently associated with persistence. [Results] The persistent effusion group (n=40) showed a significantly higher medial meniscus extrusion (MME) score than the non-persistent effusion group (n=17) at baseline. In multivariable logistic regression, the MME score was independently associated with effusion persistence (odds ratio, 6.42; 95% confidence interval, 1.95-21.1). [Conclusions] MME is independently associated with joint effusion persistence at 1 month.

title: Aptamer Interfaces for Serum-Based Gastric Cancer Detection: From Molecular Recognition to Clinical Decision
abstract: Gastric cancer is the fifth most commonly diagnosed malignancy and the fifth leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and it remains lethal chiefly because it is detected late. Endoscopic screening demonstrably works where it is deployed at scale, but endoscopy cannot be extended to the several hundred million people who would need it; a blood test that stratifies risk before endoscopy is therefore the only realistic route to population-level early detection. Aptamers-short, chemically synthesizable nucleic acid ligands-are attractive recognition elements for such a test, and more than a decade of work has produced hundreds of aptasensors that detect gastric cancer serum markers with impressive analytical sensitivity. Almost none has reached clinical use. Here we argue that this impasse is not a problem of affinity, nor of limit of detection, but of interface design. We resolve aptamer-based serum diagnostics into four coupled interfaces-molecular recognition, the serum matrix, signal transduction and clinical evidence-and show that each has been optimized locally while the constraints they impose jointly have been ignored. We then specify a reference architecture and a minimum evidence standard for a gastric cancer serum aptamer test, and identify the five measurements that would move the field from demonstration to deployment.

title: NeuroTürkNet: A Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework for Brain MRI Tumor Classification and Localization
abstract: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) presents challenges for computational tumor classification and localization because tumor appearance and surrounding anatomy vary across examinations. This work presents NeuroTürkNet, a two-stage prototype that combines a custom convolutional neural network (CNN) for four-category image classification with a YOLOv8n model for tumor-region localization. Input MRI images were resized to 640 × 640 pixels and processed using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) and bilateral filtering. The classification dataset comprised 3,264 publicly sourced images, and the localization dataset comprised 5,858 annotated images. The CNN was trained with Adam optimization, class weighting, and validation-based learning-rate scheduling; the YOLOv8n component was trained separately and applied to images classified as tumor-bearing. In the detailed test results reported for the classifier, accuracy was 90.84%, precision 90.87%, recall 90.84%, F1-score 90.80%, and ROC-AUC approximately 0.99. The localization component reported an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.81, a best mAP@50 of 0.88, and best precision of 0.85. A graphical prototype supports MRI upload, visualization of predicted regions, and PDF output. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed computational workflow on the datasets described, but they do not establish clinical diagnostic validity. Independent validation and a complete audit of dataset partitions are needed before medical deployment.

title: Beyond the Dedicated Suite: A Practical Review of Shared Imaging Platforms for Precision Interventional Pulmonology
abstract: Background: Advanced interventional pulmonology (IP) increasingly depends on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and hybrid imaging workflows for the diagnosis and management of intrapulmonary lesions. However, globally, many IP teams still lack a dedicated pulmonology procedure suite in their institution and instead perform cases in rooms originally designed for cardiovascular, neurovascular, interventional radiology, or surgical use. Methods: This review evaluates ceiling-mounted single-plane systems, floor-mounted systems, older and newer biplane angiography suites, robotic CBCT hybrid operating room systems and mobile CBCT systems and their suitability for IP procedures. Results: Based on available literature and institutional experience, ceiling-mounted single-plane systems may offer ergonomic advantages for bronchoscopic IP because they preserve head-side access and procedural ergonomics. Floor-mounted systems remained usable, particularly in older institutions, but could restrict airway-side positioning. Biplane-suite capabilities varied by system generation and configuration; some newer configurations provided CBCT and overlay functions that may facilitate pulmonary workflows. Robotic hybrid systems may provide broad procedural flexibility for complex and combined procedures but require greater institutional support. Mobile CBCT systems represented a practical entry strategy for centers without dedicated infrastructure, while conventional multidetector CT remained valuable for selected percutaneous interventions. Successful adaptation across all platforms depended on room layout, workstation capability, team familiarity, anesthesia support, and multidisciplinary collaboration. Conclusions: Advanced IP programs can be developed without a purpose-built pulmonology suite. Careful adaptation of existing imaging environments may allow centers to expand precision bronchoscopic and percutaneous capabilities according to local resources and workflow realities.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Longevity Research: From Molecular Clocks to Interventional Geroscience
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the scale, resolution, and modalities through which biological aging can be estimated, but evidence that these estimates are valid intervention targets or surrogate endpoints remains limited. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed-indexed literature identified through documented PubMed and Consensus searches in October 2026, plus a separate search of primary US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) documents. No protocol was registered, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were not searched, and screening was by a single reviewer. We distinguish four biomarker properties: chronological-age estimation, prognostic association, responsiveness to intervention, and validated surrogacy. Deep-learning clocks across epigenomic, proteomic, retinal, electrocardiographic, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities report low chronological-age error, and several show prognostic associations with mortality, but calibration was rarely reported in the records reviewed and head-to-head comparisons with mortality-trained clocks in the same cohort were uncommon. Randomized trials show that responsiveness is clock-specific: in the CALERIE trial, caloric restriction slowed DunedinPACE but did not significantly change PhenoAge or GrimAge, and effect sizes were small. Machine learning has accelerated senolytic and mTOR-pathway candidate nomination, and a generative-AI-designed TNIK inhibitor reached phase 2a in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, an age-related disease indication rather than an aging indication. Coverage of the twelve hallmarks of aging by AI studies is uneven: epigenetic alteration and cellular senescence are best represented, whereas autophagy, proteostasis, genomic instability, and telomere attrition are thinly represented. Constraints include reliability, tissue specificity, confounding by ancestry and social factors, the gap between prediction and causation, and the absence, in the primary documents consulted, of a pathway that accepts a biological-age measure as a surrogate endpoint. We propose an evidence ladder and a translational chain for appraising AI-derived aging biomarkers and set out priorities for 2026-2030.

title: Uncertainty-Guided Dynamic Pseudo-Label Enhancement for Semi-Supervised Left Atrial Segmentation
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common atrial-origin arrhythmia. Left atrial image segmentation is critical for timely diagnosis and intervention. The traditional manual annotation is inefficient and inconsistent. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has thus become a practical way to alleviate the annotation bottleneck in medical imaging. Existing SSL segmentation methods still suffer from fixed confidence thresholds, accumulated pseudo-label noise, and insufficient local perturbations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a semi-supervised medical image segmentation method based on uncertainty-guided dynamic pseudo-label enhancement. This method dynamically adjusts the confidence threshold to better adapt to the dynamic characteristics of data distribution and feature changes. And it introduces an uncertainty-guided region mixing (UMIX) module, which uses prediction entropy to identify high uncertainty regions and achieves data enhancement through cross-sample feature replacement. UniMatch serves as the backbone, with strong and weak perturbations applied at both image and feature levels to enable more effective supervised learning and improve segmentation. The proposed method was compared against competing methods on two public datasets. Through comparative experiments with other methods on two public datasets, together with ablation studies, we validated the superior performance of the proposed method in image segmentation tasks and the effectiveness of its individual components.

title: Aptamer-Based Screening and Detection of Serum Biomarkers for Lung Cancer
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and most patients are still diagnosed after symptoms appear, when curative treatment is no longer possible. Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces mortality in high-risk smokers, yet uptake is low, eligibility criteria exclude the large never-smoker populations of East Asia, and false-positive findings generate downstream harm. A blood test that could triage who needs imaging, or rule out disease in indeterminate nodules, would therefore have substantial clinical value. Aptamers - short single-stranded oligonucleotides selected in vitro and produced by chemical synthesis - are attractive as the recognition layer of such a test because they can be generated against native membrane proteins and glycans, are thermostable and can be labelled site-specifically at low cost. Here we review the serum biomarker landscape in lung cancer, the chemistry that makes aptamers usable in serum, the selection strategies that now deliver picomolar binders within days, and the transduction architectures that convert binding into a clinical readout. We argue that analytical sensitivity is no longer the limiting factor: the field’s bottleneck has moved upstream to matrix-adapted affinity and downstream to prospective, blinded validation.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of CT Image Segmentation for Liver Cancer Screening Using Artificial Intelligence (1998--2026): A Review
abstract: Liver cancer is a global challenge, with increasing mortality rates. This article presents a detailed bibliometric analysis of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) methods to segment CT images and, subsequently, screen for liver cancer. We analyzed 2029 articles indexed in the recognized Scopus database, which covers the period between 1998 and 2026 (data collected on July 25, 2026), using a bibliometric analysis and visualization software called VOSviewer, in combination with complementary network analysis methods to explore co-occurrence networks, authors' scientific performance, and influence on citations. Major findings include the identification of researchers, research organizations, and countries contributing to the development of AI-based liver cancer screening techniques, with China, India, and the United States being the main contributors. Similarly, our study highlights the most influential publications and journals in this field, and also the accelerated increase in research output after 2019, mainly supported by deep learning algorithms. Five thematic clusters emerged from keyword co-occurrence analysis: clinical and radiomic evaluation, deep learning-based CT segmentation, quality imaging and contrast-enhanced imaging, neural networks, and AI applications in MRI-based oncology imaging. The analysis also highlights gaps in the existing and burgeoning literature for future investigations, most notably explainable AI, integration of multimodal imaging data, and testing in large-scale clinical settings.

title: Algorithm-based diagnosis and targeted epidural blood patch for spontaneous intracranial hypotension: a case report from a Vietnamese tertiary center
abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) is an increasingly recognized disorder caused by spinal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. Although characteristic brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings may suggest the diagnosis, precise localization of the leak often requires advanced imaging techniques. Reports describing the application of contemporary SIH diagnostic algorithms in Southeast Asia remain limited. Case presentation A 40-year-old Japanese woman presented with severe orthostatic headache and vertigo after heavy lifting and excessive neck rotation. Brain MRI demonstrated diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement, venous sinus engorgement, and brain sagging, yielding a Bern SIH score of 7 and indicating a high probability of spinal CSF leakage. Whole-spine MRI revealed a spinal longitudinal epidural CSF collection extending from T1 to T12. Based on the positive SLEC pattern, prone dynamic CT myelography was performed and identified a thoracic ventral dural tear at the T2 level. Targeted epidural blood patching was subsequently performed using 4 mL of autologous blood. Follow-up MRI demonstrated marked reduction of the epidural fluid collection and re-expansion of the thecal sac. The patient experienced gradual clinical improvement and was discharged with significant symptom relief. Conclusions This case illustrates the clinical value of a structured multimodality imaging approach for SIH, integrating the Bern SIH score, whole-spine MRI, and dynamic CT myelography to guide targeted treatment. Accurate leak localization enabled successful targeted epidural blood patching and favorable clinical recovery. Furthermore, this report demonstrates the feasibility of implementing advanced SIH diagnostic and interventional techniques in a Vietnamese tertiary-care hospital.

title: Histopathological alterations of deep cervical lymph nodes in Alzheimer's disease and their association with cognitive decline
abstract: Abstract Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive and functional decline with amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau pathology. In addition to abnormal protein aggregation, impaired clearance of brain-derived solutes through glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic pathways may contribute to disease progression. Deep cervical lymph nodes (DCLNs), as major downstream lymphoid structures of central nervous system drainage, may provide a peripheral histological window into the brain-cervical lymphatic axis. However, whether human DCLNs undergo histopathological remodeling in AD and whether such changes are clinically relevant remain unclear. Methods DCLNs were obtained from 66 participants, including 59 patients with moderate-to-severe AD and 7 cognitively unimpaired controls. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was used to assess lymph node morphology and germinal center (GC) abundance. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to evaluate Aβ, tau, alpha-smooth muscle actin (alpha-SMA), CD31, and LYVE-1. Cognitive and functional status were assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB), and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) scores. AD patients were stratified by GC abundance using a cutoff of 4 GCs. Multivariate logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, decision curve analysis, and 6-month postoperative follow-up were performed. Results DCLNs from patients with AD showed histopathological remodeling, including reduced GC abundance, structural disruption, fibrosis-related stromal changes, altered vascular and lymphatic marker expression, and detectable Aβ and tau immunoreactivity. Compared with patients with > 4 GCs, those with ≤ 4 GCs had worse baseline cognitive and functional status, including lower MMSE scores and higher CDR-SB and ADL scores. In multivariate analysis, higher alpha-SMA mean fluorescence intensity was associated with a lower likelihood of preserved GC abundance, whereas higher MMSE score was associated with preserved GC abundance. Patients with > 4 GCs also showed greater improvement in MMSE, CDR-SB, and ADL scores at 6 months postoperatively. Conclusions Human DCLNs exhibit histopathological remodeling in AD. Reduced GC abundance is associated with greater clinical impairment, fibrosis-related remodeling, and poorer 6-month postoperative improvement, suggesting that DCLN histopathology may have potential clinical and prognostic relevance in AD.

title: Teleophthalmology for preventable blindness screening in semi-urban primary care: a cost-effectiveness study from Brazil
abstract: Abstract Background Visual impairment from preventable causes remains a critical public health challenge in Brazil, where over 34% of the population has never undergone ophthalmic examination and specialist access is severely maldistributed. Diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, and cataract are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet systematic screening in primary care remains rare in semi-urban municipalities. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a teleophthalmology-based active screening pathway versus the standard Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) passive referral pathway, assessed acceptability among professionals and patients, and estimated quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained through early detection. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted across eight Primary Health Care Units in a semi-urban municipality in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil (October 2025–March 2026). A total of 1,290 patients aged 50 years or older and/or with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were screened using a portable non-mydriatic fundus camera with remote specialist reporting assisted by artificial intelligence (AI)-based segmentation. A two-arm decision tree compared intervention costs (bottom-up micro-costing) against standard pathway costs (SIGTAP 2024/SISREG 2024) from the public payer perspective. The primary effectiveness measure was time to diagnosis. A QALY scenario analysis was performed using Brazilian-validated utility coefficients. Acceptability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUScale; n = 13 professionals) and the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire – Brazil (TUQ-Brazil; n = 99 patients). Results Of 1,290 patients, 41.79% had abnormal findings and 2.32% had ungradable images. Mean time to diagnosis was 1.26 days versus 83 days via standard referral. Cost per detected case was R$50.64 versus R$70.82, a reduction of 28.5%. Teleophthalmology was absolutely dominant across all sensitivity scenarios. A QALY analysis (n = 376) yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of –R$4,330/QALY, well below the SUS threshold (~ R$132,000/QALY). Professionals rated the platform 90.96 ± 5.91 (SUScale; “Excellent”). Patients reported a mean TUQ-Brazil score of 6.61 ± 0.32 out of 7.00, with 93.9% willing to reuse the service. Conclusions Teleophthalmology demonstrated absolute dominance over standard SUS referral in both cost-effectiveness and QALY analyses, delivering earlier diagnosis at lower cost. High bilateral acceptability supports scalability within the SUS, and these findings offer actionable evidence for policymakers considering portable fundus camera integration into semi-urban primary care networks.

title: Development and internal validation of a CSF-free machine-learning model to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis from HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 encephalitis
abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis (ICI-iE) is difficult to distinguish from herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and its work-up includes invasive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing. We evaluated whether a model excluding CSF features could achieve discrimination similar to a CSF-inclusive model and support triage before lumbar puncture. Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

title: Portable Spectrophotometric Olive Oil Quality Analysis System Integrated with Oxidative Stress-State Modeling
abstract: Abstract Olive oil quality control requires analytical methods that distinguishes authentic extra virgin olive oil from lower-grade or adulterated oils while simultaneously monitoring oxidation, phenolic depletion, and storage-related deterioration. Conventional reference techniques such as gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and standardized wet-chemistry assays remain essential for confirmatory analysis, yet their cost, infrastructure needs, and sample-processing demands limit continuous use at farms, mills, warehouses, and retail inspection points. Here we present a full research framework for a portable spectrophotometric olive oil quality analysis system that integrates ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, near-infrared spectroscopy, chemometric calibration, edge-machine-learning classification, and oxidative stress-state modeling. The system is designed to quantify quality indicators such as free acidity, peroxide value, conjugated diene/triene absorbance, phenolic depletion, pigment degradation, and adulteration-associated spectral deviation without relying on destructive laboratory workflows. The research develops the platform as an analytical chemistry and embedded diagnostic system rather than as a simple consumer sensor. The designed instrument combines controlled optical illumination, wavelength-resolved detection, temperature-compensated sample handling, onboard preprocessing, encrypted data storage, and cloud-supported model governance. The biochemical model links spectral behavior to triglyceride structure, oleic-linoleic acid balance, phenolic antioxidant buffering, radical propagation, hydroperoxide accumulation, aldehyde formation, and the degradation of chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments during light or heat exposure. The computational model couples standard normal variate correction, derivative spectroscopy, principal component analysis, partial least squares regression, support vector machines, random forests, gradient boosting, and uncertainty-aware edge inference. A validation strategy is applied using authenticated extra virgin, virgin, refined, and pomace oils; controlled adulteration series with sunflower, soybean, canola, palm, and refined olive oils; and accelerated storage experiments under oxygen, heat, and light stress. Expected outputs include rapid screening of authenticity, estimation of regulatory quality parameters, early detection of oxidative instability, and generation of traceable reports for producers, inspectors, and supply-chain actors. The framework is aligned with international olive oil quality concepts while emphasizing that portable spectroscopy is best positioned as a high-throughput screening and decision-support layer rather than a replacement for legal confirmatory testing.

title: Hybrid U-Net Model with Transformer-Enhanced Skip Connections for Abdominal Organ Segmentation in Laparoscopic Images
abstract: Abstract The organ Segmentation in surgical images plays a crucial role in computer-assisted diagnosis and robotic surgeries, yet it faces challenges like class imbalance, occlusions, and computational constraints. In order to overcome these challenges, we propose an architecture which uses asymmetric multi-scale transformer along with the attention-gated skip connections in U-Net Model to efficiently segment abdominal organs. Our proposed architecture allows efficient extraction of local features and modelling of global contexts. We also propose a hybrid loss function by combining Lovasz-Softmax loss and sparse categorical cross-entropy loss, which helps in overcoming class imbalance in the training process and improving performance on the minor classes. Our proposed method attains a mean precision of 0.9667, mean recall of 0.9432, mean dice of 0.9522, mean IoU of 0.9150, and mean HD95 of 0.4704 on all 13 classes of the CholecSeg8k dataset, which makes it better than the state-of-the-art techniques.

title: Explainable AI-Based Pulmonary Nodule Classification from Computed Tomography Images with an End-to-End Clinical Decision Support Interface
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) imaging is critical for reducing lung cancer mortality. Although deep learning-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have demonstrated promis-ing diagnostic performance, their widespread clinical adoption has been impeded by two persistent limitations: the absence of visual explainability and the lack of deployable end-to-end interfaces that integrate prediction, explanation, and clinical workflow. This paper presents an explainable, end-to-end CAD system for pulmonary nodule classification that addresses both shortcomings. The proposed system employs a transfer-learned ResNet-50 architecture, fine-tuned on 2,372 balanced CT patches extracted from the publicly available LUNA16 dataset. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is integrated into the inference pipeline to generate per-prediction heatmaps that visually localize the discriminative regions driv-ing each classification decision. The complete system is deployed as a production-grade web application featuring a FastAPI backend and a React frontend, complete with authentication and database persistence. On a held-out test set of 356 samples, the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 90.45%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 89.89%, F1 score of 90.40%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9615. A confidence-based abstention mechanism returns an “Inconclusive” verdict for predictions below a 60% probability threshold, reducing the risk of unreliable automated decisions. Rather than claiming state-of-the-art raw accuracy, this work’s principal contribution is demonstrating that competitive classification performance, real-time visual explainability, and a fully deployed, browser-accessible clinical interface can be integrated into a single reproducible, open-source system, contributing a practical baseline for future hospital validation studies.

title: Multiparametric CEST MRI–Guided Intranasal Theranostic Liposomes for Quantitative Biodistribution and Response Prediction in Glioblastoma
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) treatment is limited by the blood-brain-barrier(BBB) and lack of non-invasive methods to track drug delivery and therapeutic response simultaneously. We developed a theranostic strategy utilizing multiparametric chemical exchange saturation transfer(CEST) MRI to guide the nose-to-brain delivery of mucus-penetrating liposomes encapsulating gemcitabine and iohexol(1:1; Gem/Ioh-Lipo). These multiple CEST contrast indicated drug-specific signals (gemcitabine 2.4 ppm, iohexol 4.3 ppm and liposome − 3.5 ppm), demonstrating that > 70% intranasal dose reached the frontal cortex from the olfactory bulb.Importantly, CEST at 4.3 ppm strongly correlated with tumor response(R² > 0.9), indicating the prognostic value of image-guidance. Another CEST contrast (APTw at 3.5 ppm) indicated the tumor response, intranasal Gem/Ioh-Lipo produced an 8.6-fold tumor volume reduction versus drug-free liposomes (P < 0.0001). Controls showed a 55.9% increase in APTw signal in tumor (P < 0.005), indicating increased cellularity and proliferating cells, which were absent in treated animals. This CEST MRI-guided theranostic strategy enables non-invasive, real-time quantification of drug biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy for GBM, enabling precise treatment evaluation.

title: Machine learning implementation for host-based infectious disease diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Host-based diagnostics coupled with machine learning may support faster discrimination of infectious states and reduce unnecessary antimicrobial treatment. We reviewed recent studies that applied machine-learning methods to clinical patient data for pathogen detection, infection classification, or closely related host-response diagnosis. Eligible infection targets included bacterial and viral infections, bacterial-versus-viral classification, and syndrome-based presentations such as sepsis. Malaria was included when evaluated within a mixed febrile cohort. Searches were conducted of four literature databases spanning January 2020 through August 2025. Of 144 retrieved records, 51 passed an initial host-diagnostics screen and 21 articles met the final eligibility criteria. The included articles covered structured clinical variables, gene or molecular-expression measurements, medical imaging, physiological signals, and microscopy. For the quantitative model-class comparison, we extracted 54 evaluations belonging to four machine-learning classes: random forest (23), neural network (17), support vector machine (9), and logistic regression (5). Less frequently evaluated approaches, including gradient boosting, decision trees, naive Bayes, and k-nearest neighbors, were summarized descriptively. Model performance could not be compared directly because input modalities, cohort composition, preprocessing, validation strategies, hyperparameter selection, and reported endpoints varied substantially. Accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were the dominant performance measures. Among the 54 focal-class evaluations, 14 reported accuracy alone, 20 reported AUC alone, and 20 reported both. Only 16 evaluations reported additional measures such as sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, or Matthews correlation coefficient. Imaging studies generally favored neural-network approaches, whereas molecular-expression studies frequently used random forests. However, the evidence did not support a universally optimal model.

title: Characterizing the Spatiotemporal Boundaries of Functional Ultrasound for Brain Decoding
abstract: Abstract Functional ultrasound imaging (fUS) measures task-associated changes in cerebral blood volume (CBV) with fine spatial sampling and rapid acquisition, supporting functional mapping and brain-signal decoding. As an indirect measure of neural activity, fUS-CBV signals are shaped by neurovascular coupling and vascular dynamics, which influence the spatial and temporal stimulus information available for decoding. Consequently, the functional distinctions accessible in fUS-CBV signals require characterization under controlled experimental conditions. Here, controlled whisker stimulation in awake, head-fixed mice was used to characterize these decoding-relevant response properties. Whisker identity and number, stimulation duration, and inter-stimulus interval were systematically varied. All-whisker stimulation produced contralaterally dominant responses in the primary somatosensory barrel field and ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus. Different whisker inputs were associated with distinguishable cortical response distributions, while stimulation involving more whiskers produced broader representative activation patterns. Across durations of 0.5–10 s, brief stimulation generated measurable stimulus-associated signals, and response magnitude, persistence, and spatial distribution varied with stimulus duration. For paired 2-s stimuli, trial-level separability was already high at the shortest tested 1-s gap, corresponding to a 3-s onset-to-onset spacing, and reached 100% at gaps of 3 s or longer. Building on the experimentally characterized spatiotemporal response properties of fUS-CBV signals, a proof-of-concept modeling and decoding framework was developed, comprising cross-animal spatial prediction, classification of short versus long stimulation from S1BF ΔCBV time courses with known stimulus onset, and modeling of paired-event separability. Together, the results show that fUS-CBV signals retain structured spatial and temporal information about controlled sensory input after neurovascular transformation. These measured response properties characterize the spatiotemporal boundaries within which neural activity can be reliably distinguished using fUS-CBV signals, providing constraints for the development of fUS-based decoding models and the design of stimulation paradigms suitable for reliable fUS decoding.

title: Development of a Deep Learning Model Integrating Computed Tomography Images and Blood Data for the Diagnosis of Acute Cholecystitis
abstract: Abstract Background In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model for the diagnosis of acute cholecystitis (AC) using non-contrast CT images and clinical data. Methods This retrospective study included 197 patients (100 AC, 97 non-AC) treated between January 2016 and December 2025 at a single center. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 139) and test (n = 58) datasets. Three models were constructed: an imaging-based deep learning model, a clinical data-based machine learning model, and a hybrid machine learning model integrating deep learning-derived imaging features with clinical data. CT images were preprocessed, and gallbladder regions were segmented. Clinical variables included white blood cell counts and levels of C-reactive protein and liver function markers. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Statistical comparisons were performed using Welch's t-test and Chi-square test. Results The imaging-based model achieved accuracy 0.741, precision 0.703, recall 0.867, specificity 0.607, F1 score 0.776, and AUC 0.863. The blood-based model achieved accuracy 0.914, precision 0.931, recall 0.900, specificity 0.929, F1 score 0.915, and AUC 0.946. The hybrid model showed the highest performance, with accuracy 0.931, precision 0.882, recall 1.000, specificity 0.857, F1 score 0.938, and AUC 0.996. Conclusions A hybrid model integrating CT imaging and clinical data improved diagnostic performance for AC compared with single-modality models.

title: CBCT-based three-dimensional morphometric analysis of the upper airway and its influencing factors in skeletal Class II average-angle patients across different bone ages
abstract: Abstract Objective Previous studies have largely treated skeletal Class II patients as a homogeneous group for overall analysis, without fully accounting for subgroup differences in vertical facial patterns or variations in developmental timing. Consequently, a systematic understanding of the associations between upper airway morphology, hyoid position, and craniofacial morphology remains insufficient, which limits the formulation of precise clinical intervention strategies. This study aims to analyze the three-dimensional morphological changes of the upper airway and their associated influencing factors in skeletal Class II average-angle patients, stratified by cervical vertebral bone age staging, so as to provide evidence for the development of stage-specific orthodontic treatment strategies. Methods A total of 205 skeletal Class II average-angle patients were enrolled and divided into four groups (T1–T4) according to cervical vertebral bone age staging. Upper airway morphology, hyoid position, and craniofacialparameters were assessed using cone-beam CT (CBCT) three-dimensional reconstruction combined with Dolphin and WinCeph software. Inter-group comparisons were conducted using analysis of variance (ANOVA). Spearman correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were used to identify independent predictors of upper airway morphology. Results In females, total upper airway volume and nasopharyngeal volume increased significantly at stages T2 and T4, whereas palatopharyngeal and laryngopharyngeal volumes showed significant increased only at stage T4 ( P < 0.05). In males, significant volumetric increments across all airway segments were observed predominantly at stages T3 and T4 ( P < 0.05). Multiple regression analysis revealed that in females, the positive predictors of total upper airway volume included bone age stages T2 and T4, Mx'-Mx, H-RGn, and H-CVP. In males, the positive predictors comprised bone age stage T3, H-RGn, and H-CVP. Conclusion Upper airway volume in skeletal Class II average-angle patients exhibits a sex-dimorphic developmental pattern across bone age stages. Females display a biphasic growth pattern with leap-like increases at T2 and T4, whereas males demonstrate a steady and pronounced growth spurt from T3 to T4. Hyoid position parameters (H-RGn and H-CVP) consistently emerge as key determinants of upper airway volume, while the contribution of jaw morphology—primarily maxillary width—varies by gender.

title: Analysis of Influencing Factors and Development of a Clinical Prediction Model for Postoperative Visual Improvement Prognosis in Patients with Age-Related Cataract
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To identify independent factors associated with postoperative visual improvement after phacoemulsification combined with intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in patients with age-related cataract (ARC) and to develop an interpretable individualized clinical prediction nomogram for preoperative risk stratification. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 1,847 eyes with ARC who underwent phacoemulsification combined with IOL implantation. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors associated with postoperative visual improvement. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling with 1,000 iterations. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA), and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) value analysis. Results: Age, severity of preoperative visual impairment, fundus lesions, axial length, and keratometric value (K-value) were identified as independent predictors of postoperative visual improvement. The prediction model demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78–0.89) in the training cohort and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.70–0.86) in the validation cohort. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis revealed that age contributed most significantly to the model prediction. A visual nomogram was subsequently developed to provide individualized risk estimation. Conclusion: The nomogram incorporating five independent predictors demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability for predicting postoperative visual improvement in patients with ARC. This model may serve as a practical tool for preoperative risk assessment, individualized patient counseling, and doctor–patient communication.

title: Complex Müllerian Duct Anomaly Presenting as a Rare OHVIRA Variant: Clinical and Surgical Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Background Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Agenesis (OHVIRA) syndrome, also referred to as Herlyn–Werner–Wunderlich syndrome, is an uncommon congenital anomaly of the genitourinary tract characterized by uterine malformations, an obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal agenesis. Atypical variants add further complexity, often posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 14-year-old girl presenting with primary amenorrhea and cyclical abdominal pain. Imaging revealed a bicornuate unicollis uterus with hematometrocolpos, absent left kidney, and a grossly dilated ectopic right ureter. Intraoperatively, the cervix was rudimentary and hypoplastic, precluding fertility preservation. A complete hysterectomy with right ureteric reimplantation was performed using the Politano–Leadbetter technique. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient experienced complete resolution of symptoms at follow-up. Discussion This case demonstrates an atypical variant of Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Agenesis (OHVIRA) syndrome, characterized by bicornuate uterus, rudimentary cervix, segmental vaginal atresia, unilateral renal agenesis, and ureteric malpositioning. Such complex anomalies underscore the limitations of current classification systems and emphasize the importance of detailed anatomical description. Magnetic resonance imaging remains the diagnostic gold standard, while multidisciplinary planning is crucial for tailoring management to individual patients. When reconstructive options are not feasible, definitive surgical intervention is often required to achieve symptom relief and prevent long-term morbidity. Conclusion Atypical variants of OHVIRA syndrome underscore the importance of integrating embryological understanding, systematic renal screening, and collaborative surgical planning. Early recognition and tailored intervention are critical to achieving symptom relief and preventing long-term morbidity.

title: Benign Struma Ovarii Presenting as a Large Multicytic Ovarian Mass: Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Struma ovarii is a very rare form of ovarian teratoma with thyroid tissue present in the ovarian mass. A struma ovarii is categorised based on 50% or more of solid tissue being thyroid tissues. This particular entity can be an adult teratoma with distinct diagnostic challenges by virtue of its peculiar features, including thyroid hormone production. The tentative diagnosis is examined in a perimenopausal woman, with long-standing lower abdominal distention. Case Presentation: A 42-year-old woman, with a parity of 4 presented with a two-year history of intermittent episodes of dull lower abdominal pain associated with a feeling of a mass descending across her abdomen. This was associated with episodes of nausea, occasional vomiting, and dyspareunia for about five months. The patient also had irregular heavy menstrual periods for a similar duration. History did not reveal any signs of hyperthyroidism, Abnormal Uterine bleeding nor urinary tract symptoms. On physical examination, a firm, immobile, well-defined suprapubic mass was noted. Evaluation with abdominopelvic ultrasound showed a large, complex left adnexal cystic lesion with multiple septations. The patient was taken up for an exploratory laparotomy. Intraoperatively, a large, tortuous, multi cystic mass and highly vascularized, arising from the left ovary was found, and a left salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed a multicystic ovary with solid areas that contained seromucinous fluid and hemorrhage. Histological verification was made by the demonstration of ovarian tissue containing 80–90% benign thyroid follicles of varied sizes lined with cuboidal epithelium; with foci of calcification; and no evidence of malignancy. The patient made an uneventful postoperative recovery Conclusion Struma ovarii is tough to diagnose because it mimics so many other conditions and rarely causes thyroid symptoms. In women of reproductive age who have complex ovarian masses, it’s worth keeping in mind, even if their thyroid tests are normal. The only way to be sure is to look at the tissue under a microscope after surgery, which, for benign cases, also solves the problem.

title: Pretreatment Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Risk Marker for Brain Metastasis in Patients with Stage I–III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Receiving Definitive Thoracic Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background Brain metastasis (BM) represents a major pattern of distant failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following definitive thoracic radiotherapy (RT). Systemic inflammation plays a critical role in tumor progression and the metastatic cascade. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for predicting the occurrence, cumulative incidence, and temporal dynamics of brain metastasis in patients with Stage I–III NSCLC receiving definitive thoracic RT. Methods A total of 138 patients with pathologically confirmed Stage I–III NSCLC who received definitive-intent thoracic RT (60–66 Gy) between 2014 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Pre-treatment hematological parameters were obtained within two weeks prior to any oncological intervention. Time-dependent Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the dynamic predictive performance of baseline NLR. Independent predictors of brain failure were identified using cause-specific Cox proportional hazards regression, accounting for death as a competing risk. A pre-specified sensitivity analysis was restricted to Stage III patients (n = 108) with mandatory baseline and routine follow-up brain MRI. Results Over a median follow-up of 28.0 months, 40 patients (29.0%) developed BM. Median baseline NLR was significantly higher in patients who developed BM compared to those who did not (3.21 vs. 2.22; p < 0.001). Time-dependent ROC analysis at 28 months yielded an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.79, with an optimal NLR threshold of 2.26 (sensitivity: 91.7%, specificity: 54.6%). Multivariable cause-specific Cox regression demonstrated that higher continuous baseline NLR was independently associated with an increased hazard of BM (HR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.48–2.12; p < 0.001), alongside adenocarcinoma histology (HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 1.41–6.24; p = 0.004). In the Stage III sub-cohort sensitivity analysis, continuous baseline NLR maintained its independent prognostic significance (HR: 1.74, 95% CI: 1.44–2.09; p < 0.001). High baseline NLR (> 2.26) was significantly associated with a higher cumulative incidence of BM (Gray’s test p < 0.001), inferior overall survival (median 34.0 vs. 65.0 months; p = 0.015), and worse progression-free survival (median 18.0 vs. 42.0 months; p = 0.006). Baseline PLR was not significantly associated with BM (p = 0.136). Conclusions Continuous baseline NLR serves as a readily accessible, independent biomarker for predicting the risk and accelerated onset of brain metastasis in patients with NSCLC undergoing definitive chemoradiotherapy. Baseline NLR may aid in risk-stratified neuro-radiological surveillance protocols.

title: Airway Fire During Left Pneumonectomy: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background. Intraoperative airway fire is extremely rare yet potentially fatal, and an oxygen-filled tracheal tube is a major risk factor. Fire during pneumonectomy—in which the airway is simultaneously the operative field, the sole ventilatory route, and the conduit for combustion—is uniquely hazardous. We describe such a case and analyze its mechanism, management, and prevention. Case presentation. A 70-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a long history of smoking underwent thoracoscopic resection of a centrally located left-lower-lobe squamous cell carcinoma. During left pneumonectomy, while the left main bronchus was being divided with monopolar electrosurgery, sudden flame and smoke indicated combustion of the double-lumen tube, which was judged nonventilatable and urgently changed to a single-lumen tube. Before chest closure, bronchoscopy showed red, edematous mucosa with diffuse black carbonized deposits over the carina and both main bronchi; four intraoperative lavage passes were performed, and three further passes were carried out intermittently while the patient remained intubated in the intensive care unit. He was extubated on the first postoperative day, developed transient atrial fibrillation on the second, and was discharged on the seventh. Histopathology confirmed keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (pT4N2M0, stage IIIB). Conclusions. Recognition of the fuel–oxidizer–ignition triad, and preventive measures adopted before and during bronchial division, are essential. Once a fire occurs, immediate cessation of oxygen, rapid re-establishment of a ventilatable airway, aggressive bronchoscopic saline lavage, glucocorticoid pulse therapy, and supportive postoperative care together supported a favorable outcome; at follow-up the patient had completed five cycles of chemotherapy, with intermittent cough and sputum production and hoarseness attributed to unilateral vocal cord paralysis, but remained able to carry out the activities of daily living without clinically significant laryngotracheal stenosis.

title: Preoperative Risk Stratification of Lymph Node Metastasis in cT1 Lung Adenocarcinoma Using CT Radiomics and Habitat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is important for risk stratification and surgical planning in patients with cT1 lung adenocarcinoma. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a multi-regional computed tomography (CT) radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information for preoperative prediction of LNM. Methods A total of 172 patients with cT1 invasive lung adenocarcinoma from one institution were retrospectively included and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 120) and an internal validation cohort (n = 52). An independent cohort of 63 patients from a second institution was used for external validation. Radiomic features were extracted from the intratumoral region, a 3-mm peritumoral region, and two habitat subregions generated using K-means clustering. After feature selection, a multi-regional radiomic signature (Radscore) was constructed and combined with preoperative clinical variables using logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Nineteen radiomic features were retained in the final radiomic signature. In the internal validation cohort, the clinical, radiomic, and combined models achieved AUCs of 0.758, 0.844, and 0.852, respectively. Using a prespecified training-derived threshold of 0.4036, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 65.0%, specificity of 87.5%, and NPV of 80.0% in the internal validation cohort. In the independent external cohort, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (95% CI: 0.731–0.930), with an accuracy of 77.8%, sensitivity of 77.3%, specificity of 78.0%, PPV of 65.4%, and NPV of 86.5%. The Radscore was significantly associated with IASLC pathological grade and visceral pleural invasion (both P < 0.001). Conclusions The multi-regional CT radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information demonstrated good discrimination for preoperative LNM risk stratification in cT1 lung adenocarcinoma and maintained stable performance in an independent external cohort. The model may provide complementary quantitative information for preoperative risk assessment, although further prospective validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Hierarchical transfer learning and region of interest standardization for bone age assessment in Thai children
abstract: Abstract \normalfont\unboldmath Bone age assessment (BAA) from hand radiographs is routinely used to evaluate child growth and endocrine disorders, but manual atlas-based reading is slow and reader-dependent, while deep learning models trained on large international datasets may lose accuracy in other populations. We developed a population-specific AI framework for BAA in Thai children. It combines ROI standardization using contrast enhancement, automatic hand detection, and segmentation with an EfficientNetB7 regression model trained through hierarchical transfer learning. The model first learned skeletal-maturity representations from the public RSNA and DHA datasets and was then fine-tuned on Thai hospital data. On a held-out Thai test set excluded from BAA training and validation, hierarchical adaptation achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.64 months (RMSE, 5.85 months; \((R^2=0.98)\)), compared with 5.73 months for pooled training and 7.60 months for the public-only baseline. The full preprocessing pipeline also reduced downstream MAE relative to raw radiographs. It met the predefined detection-and-segmentation processing criterion for all evaluated RSNA and DHA images; however, this finding represents processing completeness rather than independent quantitative validation of segmentation accuracy. Among GP, TW, and a hybrid strategy using TW when applicable and GP outside the validated TW3-RUS range, the hybrid produced the lowest point-estimate MAE, although its advantage over TW was small. Grad-CAM provided exploratory evidence of attention to anatomically relevant regions but also identified localized or non-skeletal attention. Improved RSNA hand ROI annotations are released to support future research.

title: Third ventricle width on routine MRI is associated with processing speed in multiple sclerosis: a single-centre retrospective observational study
abstract: Abstract Background: Cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), and slowed information processing is among its most frequent manifestations. Although brain volumetry can quantify atrophy, automated volumetric tools are not universally available in routine practice. We investigated whether third ventricle width (3VW), a simple linear measure obtainable on conventional MRI, is associated with standardised Symbol Digit Modalities Test performance. Methods: This single-centre retrospective observational study included 100 adults with MS assessed in routine care between 2021 and 2023. Current MRI was acquired within one month of cognitive testing. A neuroradiologist blinded to cognitive results measured 3VW three times at the foramen of Monro, and the mean value was analysed. The primary analysis examined the association between current 3VW and age-standardised SDMT performance (SDMT-SD) using Spearman correlation with false-discovery-rate correction. Post hoc multivariable linear-regression sensitivity analyses adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates. MRI measurements approximately 3, 5 and 10 years earlier and analyses of SDMT impairment were exploratory. Results: Twenty-five participants (25%) met the prespecified definition of SDMT impairment (SDMT-SD ≤ -1). Current 3VW was inversely associated with SDMT-SD (rho = -0.556, 95% CI -0.678 to -0.404; q = 2.28 × 10⁻⁸). The association persisted in a fully adjusted linear-regression sensitivity model including age, sex, education and EDSS (β = -0.232 SDMT-SD units per 1-mm greater 3VW, 95% CI -0.391 to -0.074; p = 0.0045). Excluding 14 records previously labelled as CIS produced similar results. Analyses of prior MRI showed associations in selected subgroups but were limited by non-random availability of earlier scans. Conclusions: Greater third ventricle width on routine MRI is associated with worse processing-speed performance in MS. Because it is rapid to obtain and widely accessible, 3VW may serve as a simple imaging marker that prompts cognitive assessment when volumetric tools are unavailable. It should not replace cognitive testing or volumetric MRI, and predictive thresholds require prospective external validation.

title: Noncontrast Multiparametric MRI Adds Value to Preoperative Peritoneal Cancer Index Assessment in Pseudomyxoma Peritonei: Comparison with Contrast-enhanced CT
abstract: Abstract Purpose To compare noncontrast multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) for agreement with intraoperative peritoneal cancer index (PCI) and detection of key imaging features in pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP). Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 40 patients with pathologically confirmed PMP who underwent cytoreductive surgery and preoperative mpMRI and CECT in 2024. Intraoperative PCI across 13 abdominopelvic regions served as the reference standard. Total PCI agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland–Altman 95% limits of agreement (LoA), with analyses stratified by PCI (≤ 20 vs > 20). Regional agreement and sensitivities for key imaging features were also compared. Results Forty patients (median age, 60 years; 25 women) were included. mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative total PCI than CECT (ICC, 0.98 vs 0.90; difference, 0.08 [95% CI: 0.05, 0.15]), with narrower LoA (7.1 vs 19.1 points). Agreement remained greater with mpMRI for PCI ≤ 20 (ICC, 0.91 vs 0.58) and PCI > 20 (ICC, 0.95 vs 0.74). mpMRI showed higher regional agreement in 11 of 13 regions after multiple-comparison correction. mpMRI had higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites (100% vs 61%; P = 0.002) and intralesional septation (95% vs 37%; P = 0.002), whereas CECT had higher sensitivity for intralesional calcification (100% vs 0%; P = 0.021). Conclusion Noncontrast mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative PCI than CECT and higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites and intralesional septation, whereas CECT better detected intralesional calcification.

title: Chemical Composition of Radiolucent Urinary Stones: A Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy Study
abstract: Abstract Background Radiolucent urinary stones are commonly presumed to represent uric acid calculi; however, the chemical composition of these stones may be heterogeneous. Accurate characterization of stone composition may provide clinically relevant information for understanding stone pathogenesis and optimizing individualized management. This study aimed to determine the FTIR-based chemical composition of radiolucent urinary stones and evaluate its association with demographic and clinical characteristics. Methods This cross-sectional study included 43 patients with radiolucent urinary stones who underwent percutaneous nephrolithotomy or endoscopic lithotripsy at Razi Hospital, Rasht, Iran. Retrieved stones were analyzed using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Stone composition was classified based on comparison of overall spectral patterns with reference spectra. Associations between stone composition and demographic characteristics, body mass index, stone size, medical history, dietary pattern, urine culture results, and history of urinary tract infection were assessed. Results Mixed stone compositions were identified in 60.5% of specimens, while pure uric acid stones accounted for 14.0%. The most frequent FTIR-based classification was uric acid plus calcium phosphate (53.5%), followed by pure calcium oxalate (25.6%). Overall, uric acid-containing compositions were identified in 74.4% of specimens. Age was significantly associated with stone composition (p = 0.048), with uric acid plus calcium phosphate becoming more frequent among older patients. No significant associations were observed between stone composition and sex, BMI, stone size, previous medical history, dietary pattern, urine culture results, or history of urinary tract infection. Conclusion Radiolucent urinary stones in this cohort demonstrated substantial compositional heterogeneity and should not be assumed to represent pure uric acid stones based solely on radiographic appearance. FTIR analysis identified frequent uric acid-containing mixed compositions, particularly uric acid plus calcium phosphate. These findings highlight the value of direct stone composition assessment in radiolucent calculi and support further investigation using larger cohorts with detailed metabolic evaluation to clarify the mechanisms underlying mixed stone formation.

title: A MobileNetV2-Based Boundary-Aware Improved DeepLabv3+ Network for Gastrointestinal Endoscopic Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Objective: Gastrointestinal endoscopic lesion segmentation is challenging because lesions often exhibit substantial variations in morphology and size, blurred boundaries, small foreground regions, and complex mucosal background interference. This study proposed an improved DeepLabv3+ segmentation model that integrates a lightweight backbone, cascaded multi-scale contextual modeling, and boundary-aware auxiliary supervision to improve automatic lesion segmentation in endoscopic images. Methods: DeepLabv3+ was used as the baseline framework. The original feature extraction backbone was replaced with MobileNetV2 to reduce model complexity while extracting both low-level spatial details and high-level semantic features. The ASPP module was redesigned as a cascaded multi-scale atrous convolution module to enable feature reuse among branches with different dilation rates. In the low-level feature pathway, a boundary attention module was introduced to enhance contour-related responses according to a predicted boundary probability map. During training, boundary targets were automatically generated from ground-truth masks, and the model was optimized using a combination of cross-entropy loss, Dice loss, and boundary BCE loss. The dataset included 1,445 gastrointestinal endoscopic images with pixel-level labels, of which 1,300 were used for training and 145 for testing. F1-score, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and IoU were used for evaluation. Results: The complete model achieved an F1-score of 0.878, sensitivity of 0.860, specificity of 0.995, accuracy of 0.990, and IoU of 0.784 on the test set. Compared with the original DeepLabv3+ baseline, IoU increased from 0.755 to 0.784. Compared with SegNet, the best-performing competing model, the proposed model improved IoU by 0.040. Ablation experiments demonstrated that both the cascaded ASPP module and the boundary attention branch contributed to performance improvement. Conclusion: The proposed improved DeepLabv3+ model effectively integrates multi-scale semantic information and low-level boundary details, achieving favorable segmentation performance for gastrointestinal endoscopic lesions. This method has potential value for lesion localization, contour delineation, and quantitative analysis in computer-assisted endoscopy.

Compared with the original DeepLabv3+ baseline, IoU increased from 0.755 to 0.784. Compared with SegNet, the best-performing competing model, the proposed model improved IoU by 0.040. Ablation experiments demonstrated that both the cascaded ASPP module and the boundary attention branch contributed to performance improvement.

Conclusion:

The proposed improved DeepLabv3+ model effectively integrates multi-scale semantic information and low-level boundary details, achieving favorable segmentation performance for gastrointestinal endoscopic lesions. This method has potential value for lesion localization, contour delineation, and quantitative analysis in computer-assisted endoscopy.

title: Impact of Epicardial Adipose Tissue on Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Coronary computed tomography Angiography-Based Imaging Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to explore the association between epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume quantified by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and prognosis in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Patients and methods: In this retrospective study, 119 HFrEF patients undergoing CCTA between January 2022 and December 2023 were enrolled. EAT volume were semi-automatically quantified using CCTA sequences. The primary endpoint was the composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure rehospitalization during follow-up. Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier analyses assessed the association between EAT volume and events. Conventional and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were used to evaluate predictive performance, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated. Results Over a median 649-day follow-up, 50 patients (42.0%) experienced endpoint events. Compared with patients without endpoint events, those with endpoints had lower EAT volume (56.55 ± 21.33 cm³ vs. 74.64 ± 25.19 cm³, P < 0.001) and higher EAT density (-72.94 ± 6.80 Hounsfield Units vs. -76.61 ± 5.07 Hounsfield Units, P = 0.002). Multivariate regression analysis showed that EAT volume was an independent prognostic predictor in HFrEF patients; lower EAT volume was associated with poorer prognosis, with a determined cut-off value of 65.53 cm³. Subgroup analysis revealed that patients with lower EAT volume combined with lower body mass index had the poorest prognosis compared with other subgroups. Conclusion In patients with HFrEF, EAT volume is an independent prognostic predictor with moderate predictive value, and its cut-off value may provide additional information for clinical management.

title: Three-dimensional visualisation combined with intraoperative ultrasound in laparoscopic hepatectomy for complex hepatolithiasis: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objective Complex hepatolithiasis remains challenging for laparoscopic hepatectomy. Three-dimensional visualisation technology (3DVT) alone is limited by its static, preoperative nature, whereas intraoperative ultrasound (IOUS) lacks a global anatomical overview, and quantitative evidence for their synergistic benefit remains insufficient. This propensity score-matched (PSM) retrospective cohort study evaluated whether combined 3DVT and IOUS navigation improves perioperative safety and long-term outcomes compared with conventional two-dimensional imaging in patients with complex hepatolithiasis. Results Among 180 patients who underwent laparoscopic hepatectomy between January 2020 and December 2025, 66 matched pairs were analysed. The combined-navigation group had significantly shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss and lower conversion and transfusion rates than the control group (all P < 0.05). The one-stage stone clearance rate was 100.0% versus 90.9% (P = 0.028), and the overall postoperative complication rate was 3.0% versus 18.2% (P = 0.009). Over a mean follow-up of approximately 37 months, the stone recurrence rate was 1.5% versus 10.6% (P = 0.039), with significantly better recurrence-free survival (log-rank P = 0.039). Combined navigation was an independent protective factor for postoperative complications (OR = 0.313, 95% CI 0.107–0.915; P = 0.034).

title: Influence of body composition on survival in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis: a clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram development and validation
abstract: Abstract Background Bone metastasis (BM) reduces survival in breast cancer (BC) patients. Altered body composition is prognostic but poorly captured by conventional models; radiomics enables precise CT-based quantification. This study aimed to determine the influence of body composition on survival in BC patients with BM and to develop and validate a comprehensive web-based nomogram. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 197 breast cancer patients with bone metastasis at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute & Hospital, Tianjin, China, between January 2010 and December 2017. Another 38 patients from January 2012 to December 2016 in P.A. Hertsen Moscow Oncology Research Center, Moscow, Russia, as the external validation cohort to test the nomogram. The radiomics score for predicting survival was established by using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression. The Kaplan-Meier method was used for survival analysis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was used to construct a clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram based on clinicopathologic and radiomics features of body composition. A clinicopathologic web-based nomogram was also established. Receiver operating characteristic curves and internal validation cohort were used to evaluate aforementioned nomograms. We verified the clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram model using the external validation cohort. Results The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed the 1-year survival in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis in construction cohort was 81.9%, the 3-year was 48.6%, the 5-year was 19.6%. Body composition was proved to be significantly correlated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients with bone metastasis. Eight variables were selected into the clinicopathologic-radiomic model: radscore, bone CT-value, bone metastasis location, pathology subtype, brain metastasis, ALP, Ca and TMI. The clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram was satisfactory with the C-index of 0.82, which was higher than the clinicopathologic model (C-index was 0.71). The AUCs of clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram in 1-, 3-, 5-years were internally validated (82.3%, 91.1% and 82.9%, respectively) and externally validated (85.1%, 84.3% and 67.7%, respectively). Conclusions Body composition was significantly associated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients with bone metastasis. Individualized rehabilitation training and nutritional support intervention should be encouraged for the patients. The established clinicopathologic-radiomic nomogram was an effective tool for prognostic prediction, and could help clinicians make personalized clinical decisions.

title: Individualized Structural Brain Deviations in Bipolar I Disorder: a Normative Modeling Study of 4 660 ENIGMA Participants
abstract: Abstract Bipolar disorder (BD) is a prevalent psychiatric condition characterized by marked clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity. Prior neuroimaging studies have used case-control comparisons yielding small to moderate effect sizes for group differences. Large and diverse samples are needed to map heterogeneity within BD. Here, we used individualized brain morphometry deviations derived from normative modeling for three MRI-based measures (regional cortical thickness, regional surface area, and subcortical volumes). We applied this approach to a large international sample of 4 660 individuals (1 145 with bipolar I disorder and 3 515 healthy controls) from the ENIGMA Bipolar Disorder Working Group consortium (age range = 8–80, female = 53.15%) and examined the distribution of deviations within the bipolar disorder group, differences between healthy controls and individuals with bipolar disorder, and associations between neuroanatomical deviations and clinical variables. We found that individuals with bipolar disorder showed a higher proportion of localized extreme deviations, notably negative cortical thickness deviations in regions consistently reported as thinner in prior studies (the left superior frontal gyrus, bilateral inferior frontal gyrus (pars opercularis), left precuneus) and subcortical volume negative deviations in the left hippocampus. In addition, ROI-level deviations in the left middle temporal gyrus and the left inferior temporal gyrus were associated with longer illness duration. This is the largest study to date exploring individualized deviations as neuroanatomical features associated with bipolar disorder. Our findings suggest that neuroanatomical heterogeneity is a core feature of bipolar disorder, with preferential left-lateralized cortical-hippocampal involvement pointing to spatially structured heterogeneity.

title: DSPAN: Dual-domain structure-aware adversarial learning with physics-inspired consistency for low-dose CT denoising
abstract: Abstract Background Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but increases noise and artifacts that can obscure low-contrast anatomy. We developed the Dual-domain Structure-Preserving Adversarial Network (DSPAN) to improve LDCT image fidelity. Methods DSPAN combines a ResNet-based generator with dual-domain structure-aware attention and coupled gradient- and frequency-consistency learning. We used five-fold patient-level cross-validation on all 10 patients in the 2016 NIH-AAPM-Mayo Clinic Low Dose CT Grand Challenge dataset. Each fold included seven training patients, one validation patient for checkpoint selection, and two test patients. Every patient was tested once. Slice-level measurements were averaged within each patient, and performance was summarized descriptively across the 10 patients. No null-hypothesis tests were performed. Results DSPAN achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio of 40.2105 ± 1.6183 dB, structural similarity of 0.9424 ± 0.0220, and root mean squared error of 2.5359 ± 0.5303 in 8-bit-equivalent units. It had the best mean value for all six evaluated image-quality metrics. Compared with DU-GAN, mean peak signal-to-noise ratio increased by 0.1505 dB and root mean squared error decreased by 0.0410. Module ablation showed a 1.0662 dB mean peak signal-to-noise ratio gain over ResNetGAN alone. Conclusions Combining structure-aware attention with gradient and frequency consistency improved internal image-quality performance in this 10-patient dataset. External validation and diagnostic reader studies are needed to establish generalizability and clinical relevance.
