title: Comprehensive Treatment of a Patient with Osteogenesis Imperfecta and Congenital Hemivertebra: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder characterized by extreme bone fragility, making the surgical management of associated severe scoliosis exceptionally challenging due to the high risk of instrumentation failure. The coexistence of OI and a congenital hemivertebra in a single patient is exceedingly rare and further complicates spinal deformity correction. We report the case of a 17-year-old boy with OI who presented with progressive, severe thoracolumbar scoliosis and worsening lumbar pain. Imaging revealed major Cobb angles of 85° and 95°, a fully segmented L3 hemivertebra, and markedly reduced bone mineral density with a total lumbar Z-score of –5.8. To optimize surgical safety and outcomes, a comprehensive, multidisciplinary treatment strategy was implemented. This included preoperative halo-gravity traction to improve spinal flexibility and alignment, alongside bisphosphonate therapy to enhance bone mass. The patient underwent a posterior L3 vertebrectomy and spinal fusion from T4 to S1. Postoperative radiographs demonstrated satisfactory deformity correction. Although asymptomatic pedicle screw breakage was observed at the 6-month follow-up—highlighting the immense biomechanical stress posed by the inherent bone fragility in OI—the patient maintained stable spinal alignment without significant loss of correction at 12 months. This case underscores that while meticulous perioperative optimization (including traction and pharmacological therapies) combined with advanced surgical planning can achieve successful deformity correction in patients with OI and congenital scoliosis, continuous long-term monitoring remains vital due to the persistent risk of hardware fatigue. Trial registration Not applicable. This study is a case report and not a clinical trial.

title: Development and internal validation of a CSF-free machine-learning model to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis from HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 encephalitis
abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis (ICI-iE) is difficult to distinguish from herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and its work-up includes invasive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing. We evaluated whether a model excluding CSF features could achieve discrimination similar to a CSF-inclusive model and support triage before lumbar puncture. Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

title: Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich Syndrome Complicated by Right Ectopic Atrophic Kidney: A Case Report from a Primary Hospital
abstract: Abstract Background Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS), also termed obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA), is a rare congenital Müllerian duct anomaly frequently accompanied by structural abnormalities of the ipsilateral kidney and ureter. Owing to its nonspecific clinical features, which often overlap with common acute abdominal conditions such as pelvic inflammatory disease and appendicitis-HWWS is frequently misdiagnosed or missed in primary healthcare settings, particularly among post-menarchal adolescents with atypical symptoms. This case report presents a 9-year-old girl with HWWS and ipsilateral ectopic atrophic kidney associated with an ectopic ureteral orifice, and discusses the diagnostic reasoning, stepwise imaging strategy, and multidisciplinary management experience gained at a primary hospital. Case presentation: A 9-year-old girl presented with intermittent lower abdominal distending pain for 15 days. Menarche had occurred four months earlier; menses were irregular, without cyclic dysmenorrhea or vaginal purulent discharge. Initial pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a mixed echogenic pelvic mass and absent right kidney. Subsequent contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI and CT urography (CTU) confirmed the diagnosis of type I HWWS, characterized by uterus didelphys with double cervix, right vaginal atresia with hematometra and hematocolpos, and a right ectopic atrophic kidney with an ectopic ureteral orifice. After multidisciplinary consultation involving gynecology, urology, and general surgery, the patient underwent combined hysteroscopic resection of the right vaginal oblique septum, laparoscopic resection of the ectopic right kidney and ureter, and cystoscopy. The intraoperative course was uneventful. Postoperative anti-infective therapy and vaginal care were provided; the patient recovered satisfactorily and was discharged on postoperative day 10 without abnormal vaginal discharge. Conclusion HWWS exhibits heterogeneous and often atypical manifestations in adolescent girls. Primary-care physicians should maintain a high index of suspicion and adopt an integrated genitourinary diagnostic mindset. A stepwise imaging strategy combining ultrasonography, MRI, and CTU can significantly improve early recognition. Combined minimally invasive surgery under multidisciplinary collaboration is safe and feasible, and may serve as a useful reference for the management of complex congenital genitourinary malformations in primary hospitals.

title: CINet: Communication-aware Inter-modality Network for Distributed Multi-Modal MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Abstract AI-enabled medical imaging is increasingly moving toward distributed acquisition, computing, and inference, where information required by a downstream task may reside at different nodes. In multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction, this situation arises when a fully sampled auxiliary contrast is not locally available but can provide complementary information for reconstructing an undersampled target contrast. Existing methods generally assume direct access to the auxiliary modality and therefore do not consider the communication constraints involved in transferring such information between distributed nodes. To address this problem, we propose the Communication-aware Inter-modality Network (CINet) for distributed multi-modal MRI reconstruction, which jointly considers auxiliary representation transmission and cross-modal reconstruction under communication constraints. Specifically, a Task-Oriented Communication Encoder reweights multi-scale auxiliary features and generates compact representations under a prescribed communication budget. The resulting representations are transmitted through a noisy channel, and a Target-Conditioned Selective Fusion module selectively incorporates the received auxiliary information according to the current target representation. CINet thus coordinates compact auxiliary information transmission with its downstream utilization for target reconstruction. Experiments on multi-modal prostate MRI demonstrate that CINet achieves competitive or superior reconstruction performance under different undersampling patterns and acceleration factors while preserving local structural details. Further evaluations under varying communication budgets and channel signal-to-noise ratios characterize the communication--reconstruction trade-off under different transmission conditions.

title: CTA-Based 3D Thrombus Radiomics and Machine Learning for Differentiating Stroke Etiology in Acute Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and evaluate machine learning models integrating three-dimensional (3D) thrombus radiomic features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) with clinical variables to differentiate large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA) from cardioembolism (CE) in patients with acute middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Materials and Methods: This retrospective two-center study included 453 patients with acute MCAO who underwent endovascular treatment (EVT). The 3D thrombus region was segmented on preoperative CTA, and radiomic features reflecting intensity, texture, and morphology were extracted. Multiple machine learning models integrating radiomic and clinical variables were developed using the training cohort and evaluated in a held-out test cohort. Discrimination, calibration, SHAP-based interpretability, feature importance, and decision curve analysis were assessed. Results: Among the evaluated models, the random forest (RF) model showed competitive performance in the held-out test cohort, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.822, sensitivity of 0.867, and the lowest Brier score (0.171) among the evaluated models. Both clinical and 3D thrombus radiomic features contributed to model predictions. Intraprocedural tirofiban use, admission LDL-C level, sex, admission NIHSS score, and selected thrombus texture and morphological features were important predictors. Decision curve analysis indicated positive net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05–0.60. Conclusion: Three-dimensional thrombus radiomics from routine preoperative CTA combined with clinical variables may help differentiate LAA from CE in acute MCAO. The interpretable RF model may serve as a complementary tool for acute-phase stroke etiological assessment.

title: Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty With Dual Mobility Cup for Neglected Non- Traumatic Dislocation Following Conversion Long Stem THA After Failed Intertrochanteric Fracture Fixation: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Conversion total hip arthroplasty (THA) following failed internal fixation of proximal femoral fractures is technically challenging and is associated with an increased risk of complications, including postoperative instability.¹˒² Dual mobility constructs have been increasingly used in revision THA to improve stability and reduce the risk of recurrent dislocation.⁴˒⁵ Case presentation We report the case of a 62-year-old South Asian female who presented with chronic pain and inability to walk following neglected non-traumatic dislocation of a previously operated left long-stem total hip replacement. She had initially sustained a left intertrochanteric femur fracture following a slip and fall at home, which was treated with open reduction and internal fixation using an angle blade plate. Following implant failure, she underwent conversion to an uncemented long-stem THA. Within two weeks, she developed spontaneous anterior dislocation of the prosthetic hip without trauma. Closed reduction under anaesthesia was attempted but failed, and she subsequently had persistent pain, functional limitation, and inability to bear weight. Imaging demonstrated a dislocated prosthesis with extensive fibrosis and pseudo-acetabulum formation. Revision THA was performed using an extended trochanteric osteotomy for removal of the existing femoral stem, an uncemented long diaphyseal-fitting revision femoral stem, and a cemented dual mobility acetabular cup. Cerclage wiring was used to provide additional support. The hip was stable intraoperatively, and postoperative rehabilitation was initiated. The patient achieved full weight-bearing mobilisation with a walker from postoperative day 2, with satisfactory postoperative radiographs and significant relief of pain. Conclusion Neglected prosthetic hip dislocation following conversion THA after failed fracture fixation presents a complex reconstructive challenge because of altered anatomy, fibrosis, pseudo-acetabulum formation, and compromised soft tissues.¹˒² Revision THA using an uncemented long revision stem combined with a cemented dual mobility acetabular component can provide a stable reconstruction in such high-risk cases.⁴˒⁶ Dual mobility articulation should be considered in revision THA when there are significant risk factors for instability.⁴˒⁵˒⁷

title: Base deficit and triage, not blood ethanol, predict poor outcome after acute alcohol ingestion: a 10-year cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Clinicians often anchor on the blood ethanol concentration when judging the severity of acute alcohol ingestion, yet its prognostic value is uncertain. We compared the blood ethanol concentration with routinely available markers of physiological derangement for predicting a poor outcome in emergency department (ED) patients with acute alcohol ingestion. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults (≥ 18 years) presenting to a tertiary ED between September 2014 and September 2024 with a blood ethanol concentration > 10.1 mg/dL; co-ingestions and toxic-alcohol exposures were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of intensive care unit (ICU) admission and/or all-cause mortality at 30 days or 6 months. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC); independent predictors were identified by multivariable logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation. Analyses were repeated after stratification by presentation type (trauma versus non-trauma). Results Of 2,460 patients (85.4% male; median age 35 years), 90 (3.7%) had a poor outcome. Blood ethanol did not discriminate poor outcome overall (AUC 0.527), whereas base deficit (0.783), bicarbonate (0.768), lactate (0.730) and admission glucose (0.690) discriminated moderately to well. Base deficit performed similarly in non-trauma (0.790) and trauma (0.770) strata. Among non-trauma presentations, patients with a poor outcome had a lower median ethanol concentration (129.9 versus 185.2 mg/dL; p = 0.021). A model combining red triage, base deficit and pathological computed tomography achieved an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.874. Conclusions In ED patients with detectable ethanol, the ethanol concentration is a poor predictor of poor outcome, whereas base deficit, lactate, admission glucose and red triage are stronger, readily available markers. Risk stratification should rest on physiological and structural assessment rather than the toxicological level.

title: Deep Feature Selection and Multi-Sparsity Functional Connectivity Networks for Autism Classification
abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with heterogeneous alterations in functional brain organization, making reliable neuroimaging-based characterization difficult. We developed a framework combining deep feature selection with multi-sparsity functional connectivity networks to identify discriminative connectivity patterns and classify ASD. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 871 participants in the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I dataset (403 ASD and 468 typically developing controls) were analyzed. Pearson correlation networks were constructed across 111 regions and thresholded at multiple sparsity levels. Deep feature selection identified stable connections across training folds, while nested cross-validation selected the optimal sparsity level and evaluated a linear support vector machine. The framework achieved 86.2\% accuracy, 88.8\% sensitivity, 84.0\% specificity, and an area under the curve of 91.6\%. Discriminative connections were concentrated in frontal, occipital, and parietal regions, including the superior frontal gyrus and lateral occipital cortex. These findings show that combining feature selection with multi-sparsity connectome analysis can improve the identification of reproducible autism-associated connectivity patterns. The results should be interpreted as research-level classification rather than a clinical diagnostic test and require independent external validation.

title: Radiomics-based detection of lateralization in primary aldosteronism: a multicenter study
abstract: Abstract Purpose : To investigate whether adrenal CT radiomics can distinguish unilateral from bilateral primary aldosteronism (PA), focusing particularly on inter-lateral asymmetry of radiomic features. Methods: Patients were selected from the multicenter Spanish SPAIN-ALDO registry and included if adrenal computed tomography (CT) imaging and definitive subtype classification by adrenal venous sampling were available. Portal-phase CT scans from 33 patients (66 adrenal glands; 22 unilateral and 11 bilateral PA) were centrally analyzed. Adrenal glands were segmented independently by two radiologists. Radiomic features underwent reproducibility filtering (ICC ≥0.75), redundancy reduction, and bootstrap-based stability selection. Patient-level lateralization was primarily assessed using inter-lateral asymmetry indices, with repeated stratified cross-validation and balanced logistic regression. Results: Two reproducible radiomic features—GLSZM small zone emphasis and GLSZM gray-level non-uniformity—showed consistent discriminatory signals for unilateral versus bilateral PA. Radiomics based on inter-lateral asymmetry achieved an AUC of 0.681, increasing to 0.733 when systolic blood pressure was added to the model. At the individual-gland level, Compactness2 and maximum 3D diameter were selected. Radiomics alone achieved an AUC of 0.660 for identifying the aldosterone-producing gland, with no improvement from adding clinical variables. Morphological features showed excellent interobserver reproducibility. Conclusions: In this multicenter exploratory cohort, reproducible adrenal CT radiomic features demonstrated a potential signal for PA subtype classification. Inter-lateral radiomic asymmetry combined with systolic blood pressure showed the highest point-estimate performance for distinguishing unilateral from bilateral PA, while radiomics alone performed similarly for identifying the aldosterone-producing gland. These findings warrant validation in larger independent cohorts .

title: A Stacking Fusion Model Integrating MRI Radiomics and Deep Learning for Prediction of Occult Lymph Node Metastasis in Cervical Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background To develop and validate a stacking model integrating MRI-based radiomics and deep learning model outputs for the preoperative prediction of occult lymph node metastasis (OLNM) in early-stage cervical cancer (CC), and to explore its potential complementary value in preoperative risk stratification. Methods This dual-center retrospective study included 392 patients with early-stage CC. Radiomics features were extracted from preoperative T2WI-FS and DWI sequences, and feature selection was conducted using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression to construct the radiomics model. Deep learning models, including 2D-DL and multichannel 2.5D-DL, were developed separately for T2WI-FS and DWI sequences based on the ResNet50 architecture. A stacking model was subsequently established by integrating the output probabilities of the radiomics, 2D-DL, and multichannel 2.5D-DL models using an ensemble learning strategy. Model performance was evaluated using the AUC, and differences in AUCs between models were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration was assessed using calibration curves. Results The incidence of OLNM was 14% in the training cohort and 16% in the external validation cohort. The stacking model achieved the highest AUCs in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts (0.983, 0.932, and 0.868, respectively), and was numerically superior to multiple single-sequence models. The calibration curve demonstrated good agreement between the predicted probabilities and actual outcomes, and the decision curve analysis indicated a favorable net clinical benefit. Conclusions The stacking model proposed in this study demonstrated good discriminative ability and stability for the preoperative assessment of OLNM in patients with early-stage CC. By integrating outputs from radiomics and deep learning models, this approach may, to some extent, complement conventional imaging assessment and provide additional information for preoperative OLNM risk stratification.

title: Management and Demographic Evaluation of Endodont Treatment Cases Performed Under General Anesthesia
abstract: Abstract Background The aim of this study was to evaluate the clinical and demographic characteristics of patients referred to the Department of Endodontics at Istanbul Beykent University who required endodontic treatment and were scheduled for dental treatment under general anesthesia, with a particular focus on their endodontic management and postoperative evaluation. Methods This retrospective study was conducted by reviewing the clinical records of 14 patients of different age groups who presented to the Department of Endodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Istanbul Beykent University, between March 2024 and March 2026 for treatment and whose dental treatments were completed under general anesthesia. A total of 42 teeth that underwent endodontic treatment were included. Among patients who met the inclusion criteria, the relationships between sex, medical history, type of systemic condition, hospitalization status, percussion pain at the first-week follow-up, root canal filling quality, and the presence of panoramic radiographs were evaluated. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 27.0. Categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. One-sample distributions were evaluated using the chi-square test, while associations between variables were assessed using the Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results The study included 14 patients and 42 teeth that underwent endodontic treatment under general anesthesia. The majority of the patients were female, and neurodevelopmental disorders were the most frequently identified condition in the medical history. Among the systemic conditions, dental phobia and cerebral palsy were the most frequently observed diagnoses. Among the treated teeth, molars constituted the largest proportion, followed by anterior and premolar teeth. At the first-week clinical evaluation, pain assessment could not be performed in a substantial proportion of cases due to communication limitations. The majority of root canal fillings were assessed as ideal, and panoramic radiographic records were available for most of the cases. No statistically significant differences were found between tooth-type distribution and sex or the presence of panoramic radiographs according to the medical history groups (p > 0.05). Conclusion Endodontic treatment performed under general anesthesia appears to be a feasible treatment approach for patients with difficulties in cooperation and communication. However, communication difficulties may constitute an important limitation in the assessment of postoperative pain. The fact that the majority of root canal fillings were of ideal quality suggests that, with appropriate patient selection and treatment planning, endodontic treatment can be successfully performed under general anesthesia.

title: Repeat dental general anaesthesia in children and the role of treatment planning: A Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Aims To map evidence relating to repeat dental general anaesthesia (DGA) in children, describe reported repeat DGA rates and identify potentially associated factors, including treatment-planning arrangements. Methods A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O’Malley and JBI guidance and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Five bibliographic databases were searched, supplemented by grey literature, reference-list searching, database alerts to April 2026 and stakeholder consultation. English-language sources reporting repeat DGA in children were eligible. Results Seventy-five sources were included (72 published; three unpublished). Reported repeat DGA rates ranged from < 1% to 76%. Median rates were 4.9% with paediatric specialist-led treatment planning and 10.1% with non-paediatric-specialist-led planning. However, study period was a potential confounder; among sources published from 2010 onwards, corresponding medians were 4.9% and 3.2%. Radiographic assessment was more frequently reported with specialist-led planning (36% versus 19%). Conclusions Repeat DGA rates varied considerably. Although specialist-led treatment planning was associated with lower rates overall, this association was attenuated when study period was considered and should not imply causality. The findings highlight the potential importance of comprehensive assessment, appropriate diagnostic investigation and access to specialist expertise, and support further prospective multicentre research.

title: Primary Central nervous system vasculitis mimicking Tuberculous Meningitis: A case report
abstract: Abstract Background Primary central nervous system vasculitis (PCNSV) is a rare disease characterized by inflammatory infiltration of blood vessels in the central nervous system (CNS). Owing to the lack of specificity in its clinical features and imaging examinations, it is highly prone to being missed or misdiagnosed. Case presentation A 58-year-old female from South China was admitted with headache in March 2025. Brain MRI suggested possible intracranial inflammation, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination revealed increased cell counts, decreased glucose and chloride levels, and elevated protein levels. CNS viral infection was considered, and empirical antiviral and anti-inflammatory effects with penciclovir and dexamethasone yielded no improvement. Then, diagnostic anti-tuberculosis (TB) treatment was given, there was no improvement in symptoms. Weeks later, the patient's condition worsened, with persistent headache accompanied by nausea, vomiting, cognitive dysfunction and memory decline. Even after intensified steroid therapy, the response was still poor. A subsequent craniotomy biopsy confirmed central nervous system vasculitis. Conclusion This case illustrates that PCNSV can present with symptoms such as headaches and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid indicators, which closely resemble CNS infections. For patients with poor response to empirical antibiotic therapy, early biopsy can help improve diagnostic accuracy and prognosis.

CNS viral infection was considered, and empirical antiviral and anti-inflammatory effects with penciclovir and dexamethasone yielded no improvement. Then, diagnostic anti-tuberculosis (TB) treatment was given, there was no improvement in symptoms. Weeks later, the patient's condition worsened, with persistent headache accompanied by nausea, vomiting, cognitive dysfunction and memory decline. Even after intensified steroid therapy, the response was still poor. A subsequent craniotomy biopsy confirmed central nervous system vasculitis. Conclusion This case illustrates that PCNSV can present with symptoms such as headaches and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid indicators, which closely resemble CNS infections. For patients with poor response to empirical antibiotic therapy, early biopsy can help improve diagnostic accuracy and prognosis.

title: A Prediction-Coupled Self-Explaining Functional Connectivity Learning Framework for rs-fMRI-Based Brain Disorder Classification
abstract: Abstract Existing resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) functional connectivity (FC) models can achieve useful predictive performance, but their explanations are often generated after prediction and are not systematically evaluated for faithfulness and reproducibility. We propose SE-FC, a prediction-coupled self-explaining functional connectivity framework for interpretable FC learning. The explanation pathway learns signed coefficients over FC edges, whose interaction with standardized FC values produces signed edge evidence that directly contributes to the final prediction. Deletion, insertion, and average output probability change (AOPC) analyses showed that SE-FC-derived evidence was more strongly associated with model output than random edge rankings. Cross-run analysis further quantified explanation reproducibility by identifying recurrent consensus patterns while characterizing substantial variability in exact edge selection across independent training runs. Predictive capability was evaluated as supporting evidence under strict leave-one-site-out validation on ABIDE (435 participants, 10 sites) and SRPBS (925 participants, six sites), with three independent repeated training runs for each dataset. SE-FC achieved AUC values of 0.6133 ± 0.0044 on ABIDE and 0.6127 ± 0.0051 on SRPBS, indicating competitive cross-site predictive capability. Overall, SE-FC provides prediction-coupled connectivity evidence with quantitatively assessed model-level faithfulness and cross-run reproducibility while retaining useful predictive performance.

title: Open-Set Recognition for Dental Implant System Identification: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning models for dental implant identification are typically trained on a fixed set of systems, although new systems continuously enter the market. Such closed-set models assign unregistered implants to known systems, often with high confidence. We compared open-set recognition methods for detecting unregistered implant systems while identifying registered ones. Methods In this retrospective study, 100,105 implant images from panoramic radiographs across 15 institutions were obtained from a public dataset. Thirteen systems with > 2,000 images were defined as known classes, while 29 systems (14,004 images) were withheld as unknown classes. A ConvNeXt classifier was trained using ten implant-level splits. Score-based, distance-based (OpenMax), and training-based (ARPL) methods were compared at a threshold accepting 95% of known validation images. Results The classifier achieved 0.901 accuracy for system identification and 0.968 accuracy at the manufacturer level. OpenMax achieved an AUROC of 0.898 and detected 61.4% of unknown images with 0.868 precision, outperforming all other methods across ten splits (AUROC, 0.825–0.844; detection, 29.1–49.4%; adjusted P = 0.012). Its advantage was retained after excluding institutions without known-class images. Unknown systems from manufacturers represented in training were harder to detect than those from new manufacturers (57.5% vs. 64.4%), and undetected implants were often assigned to a small number of known systems, frequently from the same manufacturer. Conclusions Closed-set evaluation overlooks a major risk of automated implant identification. A post hoc distance-based method detected most unregistered implants without retraining and with minimal loss of closed-set accuracy, providing a practical safeguard for existing classifiers and supporting expert review of flagged cases.

title: Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease Based on Multimodal MRI and Amyloid/Tau PET Fusion: Quantification of Modality Complementarity and Interpretability Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis relies on multimodal information, yet the optimal fusion strategy and the true complementarity among modalities remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically compare different modality configurations for AD diagnosis and to quantify modality complementarity. Methods: A total of 874 participants from the ADNI cohort (CN = 608, AD = 266) were included. A total of 39 features were extracted, comprising structural MRI (20 features), amyloid PET (5), Tau PET (10), and clinical variables (4). We employed a three-step feature selection process using variance thresholding, t-tests, and LASSO to evaluate 7 modality configurations and 5 classifiers, and quantified modality complementarity using centered kernel alignment (CKA), Pearson correlation coefficients, and the Jaccard index. Results: The multimodal fusion model achieved an AUC of 0.9558 in the full dataset and 0.9910 in the complete PET subset, outperforming all single-modality and dual-modality combinations. The Jaccard index for MRI and PET was 0.0000, indicating no overlap in misclassification patterns. SHAP analysis indicated that the hippocampal volume ratio (HIPPO_RATIO) was the most important feature. Conclusions: Multimodal fusion integrating structural MRI, amyloid/Tau PET, and clinical variables provides a robust and interpretable tool for AD diagnosis. More importantly, it addresses a key technical gap in multimodal research---the lack of a quantitative framework for assessing modality complementarity---by demonstrating that MRI and PET exhibit completely non-overlapping error patterns, which constitutes the core mechanism driving the improved performance of multimodal fusion.

title: VarSee™ (Lung), a Blood-Based Multi-Protein Biomarker Panel for the Early Detection of Lung Cancer: A Prospective Pilot Diagnostic Accuracy Study
abstract: Abstract Background Most non-small-cell lung cancers are diagnosed at an advanced stage because early disease is largely asymptomatic. Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT), the recommended screening modality for high-risk individuals, is constrained by radiation exposure, limited accessibility and a high false-positive rate. We evaluated VarSee™(Lung), a serum multi-protein biomarker panel coupled to a machine-learning classifier, as a blood-based adjunct for lung-cancer detection. Methods In a consecutive, prospective, single-centre, case-control pilot study with biomarker measurement performed retrospectively on banked serum samples, seven serum proteins (CA125, CA19-9, carcinoembryonic antigen [CEA], cytokeratin-19 fragment [CYFRA 21 − 1], human epididymis protein 4 [HE4], neuron-specific enolase [NSE] and progastrin-releasing peptide [ProGRP]), quantified by chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA), together with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and four clinical covariates, were measured in 100 participants (50 with histologically confirmed lung cancer and 50 non-cancer controls) and entered into a calibrated random-forest classifier (the VarSee™ (Lung) algorithm) to generate a diagnostic score. Diagnostic performance was assessed against a histopathological/CT reference standard using stratified five-fold cross-validation, reported in accordance with STARD 2015 and, for the multivariable model, TRIPOD. Results VarSee™ (Lung) distinguished lung-cancer cases from controls with a sensitivity of 100% (95% CI 92.9–100), a specificity of 96.0% (95% CI 86.5–98.9), a positive predictive value of 96.2%, a negative predictive value of 100%, an accuracy of 98.0% (95% CI 93.0-99.4) and an area under the ROC curve of 0.997 ((95% CI 0.990–1.000). In this small cohort, sensitivity was 100% at every tumour stage (I-IV). The NLR was the dominant predictor (impurity importance 0.501), followed by CA19-9 (0.116) and CYFRA 21 − 1 (0.066); accuracy and AUC were consistent across five candidate classification algorithms (accuracy 0.950–0.980; AUC 0.995–0.997). Conclusions In this pilot, a blood-based seven-protein panel integrated with the NLR discriminated lung cancer from cancer-free controls with high sensitivity and specificity, supporting further evaluation as a radiation-free adjunct for early detection. Given the small, single-centre design and cancer-free (rather than benign-disease-matched) controls, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in a larger, multi-centre study with external validation before any clinical or screening application is considered. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Registry - India, CTRI/2026/03/105171. Retrospectively registered (enrolment began prior to registration).

title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Incidental Prostate Cancer After Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Surgery: A Five-Year Retrospective Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Background Incidental prostate cancer (IPC), defined as cancer unexpectedly identified on histopathology after surgery for presumed benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), has been widely studied internationally, but data from sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce, and none exist from Ethiopia. This study examined the prevalence, predictors, clinicopathological features, and management of IPC among patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or transvesical prostatectomy (TVP) for presumed BPH. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 239 patients who underwent TURP or TVP for presumed BPH at MCM Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, between January 2021 and December 2025. Sociodemographic, clinical, laboratory, and procedural data were abstracted from medical records. Bivariable comparisons used chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and t-tests or Mann–Whitney U tests, as appropriate; univariable and multivariable logistic regression estimated crude and adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Model fit and discrimination were assessed, and sensitivity analyses examined robustness to prostate-specific antigen (PSA) transformation and influential observations Results IPC was identified in 23 of 239 patients (9.6%), with no significant difference by procedure (TURP 11.1% vs. TVP 8.2%, p = 0.445). Patients with IPC had significantly higher rates of hypertension (47.8% vs. 26.4%, p = 0.030), hydronephrosis (39.1% vs. 14.4%, p = 0.006), acute kidney injury (39.1% vs. 8.3%, p < 0.001), and higher PSA and PSA density (both p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, preoperative PSA (AOR = 1.25 per ng/mL, 95% CI: 1.14–1.38), diabetes mellitus (AOR = 5.28, 95% CI: 1.64–16.95), and hydronephrosis (AOR = 3.92, 95% CI: 1.29–11.94) were independently associated with IPC; age was not (AOR = 1.19 per decade, p = 0.459). The model showed good discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.838) and calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0.162), with findings robust across sensitivity analyses. Among IPC cases, 95.7% had International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group ≥ 2, yet no patient received active surveillance, radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, or documented staging investigation; management was uniformly based on androgen deprivation. Conclusions IPC affected nearly 1 in 10 men undergoing BPH surgery, with PSA, diabetes mellitus, and hydronephrosis independently associated with it; PSA density > 0.15 had 90% specificity but only 48% sensitivity. Most cases were clinically significant, yet none received staging or definitive local therapy, highlighting the need for structured incidental-cancer care pathways in similar resource-limited settings.

title: Three-dimensional morphometry of the normal nasal septum on computed tomography: sex- and age-specific reference values from 1,373 adults
abstract: Abstract Purpose. Normative data for the three-dimensional anatomy of the nasal septum are sparse. We applied automated segmentation to a large series of adults with radiologically normal sinonasal anatomy to establish sex- and age-specific reference values for septal size, thickness, and midline deviation. Methods. Retrospective cross-sectional study of 1,373 adults (394 men, 979 women; age 18 to 90 years) with sinus computed tomography reported as normal. The septum was segmented by a validated three-dimensional convolutional network (held-out Dice 0.983), and 12 parameters were computed from each segmentation: volume, surface area, maximal and mean sagittal cross-sectional area, three linear extents, three thickness measures, and maximal midline deviation and deviation angle. Reference percentiles were computed by sex and by sex within four age bands; age trends were estimated by linear and quantile regression. Results. Median septal volume was 16,710 mm³ in men (5th to 95th percentile 13,594 to 20,455) and 12,500 mm³ in women (9,963 to 15,329); median mean thickness was 4.89 and 4.29 mm. All size and thickness parameters were larger in men. In men, volume, depth, height, and maximal thickness increased by 1.2 to 1.4% per decade of age; in women they were constant (sex-by-age interaction P ≤ 0.021). Midline deviation did not vary with age, and its 95th percentile was about 3 mm in both sexes. Conclusion. These sex- and age-specific percentiles provide a quantitative reference for interpreting septal anatomy on computed tomography, planning septal surgery, and selecting reference geometries for airflow modeling.

title: Predicting recurrence of biliary colic after conservative management in the emergency department: a prospective cohort study with a parametric Weibull survival model
abstract: Abstract Background Biliary colic is usually managed conservatively in the emergency department (ED), yet recurrence is frequent and its timing is poorly characterized, particularly in Latin American settings with limited access to elective cholecystectomy. We aimed to develop and internally validate a survival-based model predicting recurrence of biliary colic after conservative ED management. Methods Single-center prospective cohort of adults with uncomplicated biliary colic and ultrasound-confirmed gallstones discharged from the ED of a tertiary hospital in Cuenca, Ecuador, followed for up to 365 days. The primary outcome was symptomatic recurrence requiring an ED visit; cholecystectomy and biliary complications before recurrence were censored. Predictors were screened with Cox regression; multivariable Cox and parametric Weibull models were compared by Harrell's C-index and the Akaike information criterion. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples; calibration was assessed at 7, 15, 30 and 60 days overall and by predicted-risk group. A sensitivity analysis used Fine–Gray competing-risks regression. Results Of 507 patients (median age 38 years; 76.5% women), 223 (44.0%) recurred; 25% of recurrences occurred within 7 days of discharge and recurrence-free survival was 67.8% at 30 days and 43.1% at 365 days. Biliary complications developed in 10.7% and only 7.3% underwent cholecystectomy before recurrence. In the final Weibull model, a positive Murphy's sign (hazard ratio [HR] 7.09; 95% CI 4.73–10.61) and diabetes mellitus (HR 2.18; 95% CI 1.33–3.58) were independent predictors. The shape parameter (γ = 0.419; 95% CI 0.376–0.468) indicated a monotonically decreasing baseline hazard. Discrimination was acceptable (C-index 0.692; bootstrap-corrected 0.692, 95% CI 0.665–0.723) with good calibration from 30 days onwards and underestimation of very early risk in the highest-risk group. Fine–Gray estimates were consistent (subdistribution HR 5.73 and 2.06, respectively). Conclusions Recurrence after conservative management of biliary colic is frequent and concentrated in the first days after discharge. Two bedside variables, Murphy's sign and diabetes mellitus, identify patients at high risk of early recurrence who may benefit from prioritized surgical evaluation and structured early follow-up. External validation in multicenter cohorts is required. Trial registration: Not applicable (observational study).

title: Sex estimation from the three-dimensional nasal septum on computed tomography: an allometric, size-based signal in 1,373 adults
abstract: Abstract Sex estimation from computed tomography (CT) of the head has relied on manual measurements of the skull, paranasal sinuses, and nasal cavity, with modest accuracy and small samples. The nasal septum, the midline osteocartilaginous partition of the nasal cavity, is present on every head CT but has never been evaluated as a sex estimator, and whether any sex signal in the septum reflects size or shape determines how such an estimator would transfer between populations. We tested two hypotheses in 1,373 adults (394 men, 979 women) with radiologically normal sinus CT: that septal morphometry classifies sex at least as accurately as established cranial methods, and that the discriminating information is allometric size rather than shape. The septum was segmented automatically with a validated convolutional network (held-out Dice 0.983) and 17 morphometric variables were derived from each segmentation. Septal volume was 34% larger in men (16,852 versus 12,564 mm³; Cohen's d 2.33, 95% CI 2.18 to 2.47). Under five-fold cross-validation, sex was classified with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95 by random forest and 0.96 by logistic regression on 17 variables; volume alone gave 0.94. After allometric adjustment no shape variable differed by more than d = 0.43, and shape variables alone gave an AUC of 0.58 to 0.63. Both hypotheses were supported: the septum is a strong, fully automatable sex estimator for CT, and its signal is size. Like other size-based skeletal estimators it will require population-specific calibration, which the automated pipeline makes practical.

Both hypotheses were supported: the septum is a strong, fully automatable sex estimator for CT, and its signal is size. Like other size-based skeletal estimators it will require population-specific calibration, which the automated pipeline makes practical.

title: Femoral medullary composition in advanced post mortem decomposition: agreement of attenuation-based volumetric fractions across two PMCT reconstruction protocols
abstract: Abstract In advanced decomposition, conventional post mortem markers become progressively less informative, whereas bone and medullary content remain comparatively preserved. This retrospective study assessed whether femoral medullary composition can be quantified consistently on post mortem computed tomography (PMCT) using a semi-automated segmentation approach and whether attenuation-based volumetric fractions are associated with cadaveric alteration. PMCT examinations from 100 decomposed forensic cases (199 femora) were analysed with the SegMed module in 3D Slicer. Eight medullary fractions were quantified using soft-tissue (ST) and bone (BN) reconstruction protocols. Agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), paired Wilcoxon tests and Bland–Altman analysis; associations with the Radiological Alteration Index (RAI) and estimated post mortem interval (PMI) were assessed using Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Agreement between ST and BN reconstructions was excellent for gas, fat-like marrow, fluid and intermediate-density fractions (ICCs > 0.94), despite small systematic offsets, whereas agreement was lower for residual medullary content on the right (ICC = 0.52) and unstable for debris. Gas fractions were positively associated with RAI, whereas fluid and intermediate-density fractions were negatively associated (|ρ| approximately 0.25–0.37). No volumetric fraction was significantly associated with estimated PMI after correction. Semi-automated PMCT segmentation therefore yielded consistent measurements of the principal femoral medullary fractions across the two reconstruction protocols evaluated. These fractions are candidate quantitative markers of radiological cadaveric alteration, but their value for elapsed-time estimation requires validation in cohorts with more accurately known PMIs.

title: Primary Cardiac Synovial Sarcoma of the Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Mimicking Cardiac Myxoma
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary cardiac synovial sarcoma (PCSS) is exceedingly rare and typically presents with imaging features characteristic of malignancy, including aggressive growth, poorly defined margins, and limited mobility. However, a subset of cases may closely mimic a myxoma with a benign imaging phenotype, thereby posing a significant preoperative diagnostic pitfall and compromising treatment planning. Case summary: A 34-year-old man was admitted with acute cerebral infarction. Echocardiography and coronary CTA demonstrated a solid, pedunculated subaortic mass attached to the left ventricular outflow tract, with marked mobility and imaging features highly consistent with a myxoma. Given the acute phase of cerebral infarction and high perioperative risk, tumor resection was deferred following multidisciplinary team discussion. At 4-month follow-up, the mass showed a mild interval increase in size, and open-heart surgery with mass excision was performed. Intraoperatively, the tumor exhibited a botryoid, semi-translucent appearance but was soft externally and firm internally on palpation. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry revealed positivity for TLE1 and SS18-SSX, and FISH confirmed SS18 gene rearrangement, establishing the diagnosis of PCSS. Adjuvant chemotherapy was administered postoperatively, with no evidence of residual tumor on follow-up imaging. Discussion: This case highlights that PCSS may completely mimic the growth pattern of a myxoma in its early phase, including a pedunculated attachment, marked mobility, and well-circumscribed borders—imaging features that readily lead to a benign misdiagnosis. For masses located in atypical locations with benign imaging features but complicated by systemic embolization, a high index of suspicion for malignancy should be maintained.

title: Technical Note: SegMed, a 3D Slicer module for standardized post mortem CT segmentation of lower-limb long-bone diaphyses
abstract: Abstract Post mortem computed tomography is increasingly used in forensic medicine and anthropology, but quantitative analysis of skeletal and peri-skeletal structures remains limited by heterogeneous anatomical sampling and manual segmentation procedures. This Technical Note presents SegMed, a Python-based 3D Slicer module developed to standardize segmentation and metric extraction from lower-limb long-bone post mortem CT data. In its current version, SegMed is restricted to the lower limb, and the present manuscript focuses on femoral and tibial diaphyseal workflows. The module integrates four steps: semi-automatic extraction of the diaphyseal region from an expert-defined cortical seed point, anatomical alignment of the selected bone segment, Hounsfield unit (HU)-based segmentation of medullary compartments, and optional quantification of peridiaphyseal soft tissues. The module exports quality-control masks, compartment volumes, volumetric fractions, longitudinal profiles, metadata files and analysis-ready CSV/XLSX tables. Optional exploratory indices describing the spatial distribution of segmented compartments are exported for research purposes but are not evaluated in this Technical Note. By combining expert-guided initialization with standardized image processing and structured outputs, SegMed is intended to improve reproducibility in forensic imaging research. The software does not provide diagnostic conclusions, and all outputs require expert visual review and contextual interpretation.

title: Non-invasive Detection of Neuronal Electrical Activity in the Knee Joint Using Quantum Sensing MRI
abstract: Abstract Noninvasive assessment of neuronal activity in the knee may improve understanding of osteoarthritis (OA)-related pain and joint degeneration. A 3T quantum-sensing based MRI framework was developed to estimate firing-rate-related signal fluctuations from free induction decay (FID) phase measurements, separating water and fat signals for compartment-specific estimates. The approach was evaluated in agar-gel phantoms, simulations, and six healthy volunteers and six participants with early knee OA, at rest and during repeated ankle flexion. No firing events were detected in the phantom. Simulation performance improved with signal-to-noise ratio, reaching R 2 = 0.99 at SNR = 250. In vivo, water-derived estimates correlated negatively with T 1ρ relaxation times (cartilage, r = -0.86 to -0.58; meniscus, r = -0.78 to -0.73). Fat-derived estimates differentiated OA participants from healthy volunteers (d = 3.96–4.89; p < 0.05), correlated positively with T 1ρ (cartilage r = 0.59–0.70; meniscus r = 0.70–0.71) and showed moderate exploratory associations with WOMAC scores (r = 0.43–0.55). Repeatability was higher during ankle flexion than at rest. These findings support the technical feasibility of compartment-specific FID phase analysis in the knee. Larger studies with physiological-noise control and independent biological validation are required to determine whether these MRI-derived measures specifically reflect peripheral neuronal activity and have clinical utility in OA.

title: Transcranial optical and optoacoustic super-resolution cortical microangiography in aged and Alzheimer mice
abstract: Abstract Cerebrovascular alterations and dysfunction are increasingly recognized as key contributors to aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet longitudinal in vivo imaging of cortical microvascular networks remains challenged by limited penetration of ballistic photons and transcranial ultrasound aberrations. While super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) has enabled unprecedented capabilities for microangiography via microbubble localization and tracking, aberrations arising from bidirectional ultrasound propagation through the thickened skull of aged mice remain a significant challenge, often necessitating cranial windows. Here, we propose a complementary localization-based framework combining diffuse optical localization imaging (DOLI) and localization optoacoustic tomography (LOT) for super-resolution vascular imaging in aged and AD mice. DOLI capitalizes on the reduced light scattering in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) to achieve transcranial visualization of the cortical microvasculature, while LOT leverages the unidirectional ultrasound propagation in optoacoustics to resolve pial microvessels and penetrating branches in a fully non-invasive manner. Both modalities reveal structural microvascular alterations in aging and AD, including increased vessel convolution and tortuosity at different scales, highlighting their potential for longitudinal studies of cerebrovascular pathology.

title: Posterior cortical gray matter heterogeneity between hyposmia- and RBD-defined prodromal phenotypes in Parkinson's disease: a PPMI voxel-based morphometry study
abstract: Abstract Background Prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD) includes clinically distinct enrollment phenotypes. We examined whole-brain gray matter volume (GMV) in Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) participants recruited through hyposmia-only or REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD)-only pathways and assessed the stability of the findings. Methods Baseline T1-weighted MRI from 465 hyposmia-only and 149 RBD-only participants (N = 614) was analyzed with CAT12/SPM25 voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Models included age, sex, intracranial volume, and scanner family. Whole-brain clusters were defined at voxel p < 0.001 and tested using family-wise error (FWE) correction. We examined scanner-restricted samples, 123 sex/scanner-matched pairs, and 10,000-sign-flip permutation analysis of linear models (PALM). Bilateral cuneus/calcarine estimates and clinical assessments were exploratory. Results Whole-brain analysis identified a posterior phenotype effect (F cluster: k = 4,499; pFWE = 4.15×10⁻⁷), with higher GMV in hyposmia-only participants. In 123 matched pairs, a posterior H > RBD T cluster survived correction (pFWE = 0.0266), whereas the F contrast did not. PALM also identified a posterior effect (two-sided threshold-free cluster enhancement [TFCE] FWE p = 0.0027; voxelwise FWE p = 0.0277). Adjusted bilateral cuneus differences were + 0.211 mL (95% CI 0.095–0.327) in the full cohort and + 0.187 mL (0.041–0.333) after matching. MRI-proximal RBD screening questionnaire scores showed no significant association with regional GMV. Conclusions Posterior cortical GMV differed between these enrollment-defined prodromal phenotypes. The anatomical finding was supported by nonparametric inference, although the matched F test and strictest scanner restriction were nonsignificant. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish its clinical relevance.

title: A foundation model for three-dimensional anatomical reconstruction from sparse X-ray projections
abstract: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) provides three-dimensional anatomical information but requires costly scanners and exposes patients to higher radiation doses than conventional X-ray imaging. Reconstructing three-dimensional anatomy from a few X-ray projections could extend widely available X-ray systems beyond two-dimensional imaging. We present SPARC, a foundation model pretrained once on 47,149 chest scans across diverse acquisition settings, enabling a single model to be adapted to different X-ray imaging configurations and anatomical regions. Across eight datasets covering five body regions, seven mainly outside the chest, SPARC reconstructed volumes with greater fidelity than five existing methods, exceeding the strongest in peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.8-2.6 dB with eight projections and 1.4-2.7 dB with four. CT-based tools for abnormality classification and organ segmentation retained most of their performance when applied directly to SPARC's reconstructions from eight projections, fewer than 3% of the hundreds recorded by a CT scanner. They reached 98% of their area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on CT for 18 chest abnormalities, and 86% and 93% of their Dice score on CT for abdominal organs and lung lobes, with Dice scores 8.8% and 4.4% higher, in relative terms, than with the best competing method. Pretraining considerably increased the adaptation data efficiency. With ten patients, SPARC reconstructed chest CT more accurately than the same architecture trained from scratch on 100 patients. With the models and code released, SPARC could support the clinical translation of sparse-view reconstruction and expand access to three-dimensional imaging where CT scanners are unavailable.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Volumetric Quantification of Urinary Stone Burden and Hydronephrosis From CT Images
abstract: Abstract Purpose Given the limitations of conventional stone burden assessment based on maximum diameter or ellipsoid-derived volume estimates, we aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)–based method for automated quantification of stone and hydronephrosis volumes from CT images. Materials and Methods A 2-step algorithm was developed. First, a U-Net incorporating residual blocks, dense blocks, a morphology-aware block, and attention gates (RDAM U-Net) segmented the kidneys; hyperparameters were optimized using Complex System Response (CSR) experimental design with 5-fold cross-validation. Second, within the segmented kidney, hydronephrosis was identified from low–Hounsfield unit (HU) regions, and renal stones from high-HU regions using morphological processing and 3-dimensional (3D) connected-component analysis. AI-derived stone volumes were compared with ellipsoid-based estimates using Pearson and Spearman correlation, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland–Altman analysis. Results Eighty-two kidney CT cases were used for model development. RDAM U-Net achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.9432 and Dice coefficient of 0.9681, with fewer parameters and a 32.58% shorter parameter-update time than reference attention-based U-Nets. In 39 paired stone measurements, AI-derived and ellipsoid-estimated volumes showed a near-perfect correlation (Pearson r = 0.977; Spearman ρ = 0.966; R² = 0.954; all p < 0.001) and high agreement (Lin's CCC = 0.959; ICC = 0.960). AI volumes were systematically lower than ellipsoid estimates (mean difference, − 51.21 mm³; p = 0.001), with the difference increasing with stone volume. HU-based composition analysis agreed with the clinical record in 12 of 13 classifiable stones (92.3%). Conclusions AI-based CT segmentation enabled automated volumetric quantification of both urinary stone burden and hydronephrosis, providing direct 3D assessment without reliance on geometric assumptions. Integrating stone volume, hydronephrosis volume, and stone composition into a single automated workflow may support more individualized surgical and metabolic management of urolithiasis. Further validation in larger external cohorts is warranted.

title: trans-Resveratrol and ε-viniferin recovery from grapevine pruning residues: process optimization and varietal screening towards industrial valorisation
abstract: Abstract Vine shoots are abundant viticultural by-products and promising renewable sources of high value stilbenoids for sustainable biorefinery applications. Stilbenoids are phytoalexins bearing phenolic moieties produced by Vitaceae under biotic and abiotic stress, and endowed with nutraceutical, cosmeceutical, and agrochemical potential. This study optimized the recovery of trans -resveratrol and ε-viniferin from vine shoots using Box–Behnken response surface methodology by evaluating extraction time (t), solvent mixture (S), and matrix-to-solvent ratio (R) as initial step of the circular economy task of European LIFE - Natural Agro project. The optimized conditions were then applied to conventional solid–liquid extraction (SLE), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), and Soxhlet extraction. The optimal conditions were 100% ethanol, R = 0.12 g mL⁻¹, and t = 35 min. Although Soxhlet extraction gave the highest extraction yield (EY%), UAE produced the most stilbene-enriched extract, with 9.50 mg g⁻¹ dry extract of trans -resveratrol and 25.66 mg g⁻¹ dry extract of ε-viniferin, while reducing extraction time and prolonged thermal exposure. The optimized UAE protocol was subsequently applied to grapevine varieties from Italy, Portugal, and France, revealing marked genotype-dependent differences in stilbene composition. ε-Viniferin was generally more abundant than trans -resveratrol, and Pinot Meunier, Grechetto Gentile, Moscato, and Moscatel Graudo were identified as promising raw materials, depending on the target compound. Spectrophotometric assays further confirmed variety-dependent differences in antioxidant activity, total phenolic content, and total flavonoid content. Overall, the proposed UAE strategy offers a simple, food-grade, and scalable approach for valorising vine-pruning residues as sources of bioactive ingredients.

title: Birth-cohort effects and the limits of ecological evaluation of mammography screening: an age-period-cohort analysis of breast cancer mortality in Japan, 1958–2024
abstract: Abstract Background Ecological evaluations of mammography screening are confounded by birth-cohort effects and concurrent advances in treatment. We examined the age-period-cohort (APC) structure of breast cancer mortality in Japan and quantified how much screening exposure varies independently of that structure. Methods Deaths among Japanese women aged 30–84 years in 1960–2024 were tabulated by 5-year age group and period and analysed with Holford’s identifiable APC model and quasi-Poisson errors. Screening eligibility (≥ 50 years from 2000; ≥40 years from 2004) was added as an age × period interaction, as binary or cumulative eligibility with lags of 0, 5 and 10 years. Separability was quantified as the R² of exposure on the APC terms. Incidence for 1976–2020 was analysed on the same grid. Results Among 437,134 deaths, the age-cohort model fitted far better than the age-period model (deviance 389.2 vs 9,041.8). The cohort deviation from the log-linear trend peaked in women born around 1950 (rate ratio [RR] 1.51; 95% CI, 1.47–1.54). Incidence, including three high-quality regional registries, shared this peak less markedly than mortality (RR 1.22 vs 1.43, 1976–2020). APC terms explained 91% to > 99% of the variation in screening exposure. With a 10-year lag, eligibility was not associated with mortality (RR 1.005; 0.971–1.040); across definitions, RRs ranged from 0.955 to 1.196. Conclusions Non-linear changes in breast cancer mortality in Japan were aligned mainly with birth cohort. title: White-Eye Presentation of Endogenous Klebsiella pneumoniae Endophthalmitis with a Choroidal Abscess Secondary to Colorectal Sepsis: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Endogenous endophthalmitis is sight-threatening and commonly produces marked ocular inflammation. Klebsiella pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis is classically associated with pyogenic liver abscess, whereas colorectal sources and externally quiet presentations are rarely reported. We describe culture-positive multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis with a clinically diagnosed choroidal abscess secondary to colorectal sepsis. Method: Brief report. Results: A 58-year-old man with stage IV rectal adenocarcinoma, tumour perforation and a K. pneumoniae -positive retroperitoneal abscess presented with painless visual deterioration in the left eye. Visual acuity was 6/9 in the right eye and hand movements in the left. Examination of the right eye was otherwise normal. The left eye appeared externally white, without conjunctival injection or lid swelling, despite hypopyon, fibrin and dense vitritis. B-scan ultrasonography showed vitreous loculations, an 11.07-mm dome-shaped choroidal elevation and exudative retinal detachment. K. pneumoniae was isolated from the retroperitoneal abscess, blood and vitreous, supporting haematogenous dissemination. He received four intravitreal injections of vancomycin and ceftazidime with intravenous ceftriaxone. Repeat ultrasonography after two weeks showed persistent vitreous loculations but resolution of the choroidal elevation and a flat retina. Vision deteriorated to no perception of light, systemic instability precluded vitrectomy, and the patient died approximately five weeks later. Conclusion: An externally quiet white eye can conceal severe K. pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis. Acute visual deterioration in a septic or immunocompromised patient warrants urgent posterior-segment assessment, vitreous sampling, intravitreal antimicrobial therapy and systemic source control. Visual prognosis remains guarded despite prompt ocular and systemic antimicrobial treatment.

title: SegRef3D Lite: A browser-based workflow for artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation and quantitative three-dimensional morphological analysis
abstract: Abstract Segmentation is a major bottleneck in three-dimensional morphological analysis. Although artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation workflows can be used to address this issue, their implementations are constrained by dedicated software environments or local computing resources. To address these challenges, we developed SegRef3D Lite, a browser-based platform that integrates two complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation approaches (namely, SegAnything and SegCT/MRI) within a common human-in-the-loop workflow. SegAnything provides general-purpose, prompt-based segmentation by using Segment Anything Model 2, and SegCT/MRI provides anatomy-specific segmentations of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging datasets by using TotalSegmentator. Both approaches generate segmentation masks that can be imported into the same browser-based workspace for visual review, manual correction, quantitative volume measurement, three-dimensional visualization, and surface-model export. In this workspace, routine image handling and refinement are performed locally in the browser, whereas artificial intelligence inference is executed through user-initiated Google Colaboratory workflows, thus eliminating the need for a compatible graphics processing unit on a local computer. We applied our platform to serial block-face photographs, volumetric computed tomography, serial light microscopy, serial electron microscopy, and human abdominal computed tomography. Across these diverse imaging modalities and spatial scales, our platform is able to process outputs from different segmentation approaches by using the same downstream workflow for review, refinement, quantitative analysis, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Therefore, SegRef3D Lite provides an accessible framework for integrating complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation strategies with researcher-guided verification and quantitative morphological analysis. Mini-abstract : SegRef3D Lite integrates general-purpose and anatomy-specific artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation with browser-based human refinement, volume measurement, and three-dimensional reconstruction across diverse morphological imaging modalities.

title: Can Preoperative PET/CT SUVmax Predict Aggressive Pathological Features in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer? A Retrospective Cohort Study of STAS, LVI, and VPI
abstract: Abstract Background Spread through air spaces (STAS), lymphovascular invasion (LVI), and visceral pleural invasion (VPI) are adverse prognostic features in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that can only be assessed postoperatively. This study evaluated whether preoperative primary tumor SUVmax on 18F-FDG PET/CT independently predicts these features. Methods In this retrospective cohort of 478 patients undergoing surgical resection for NSCLC, associations between primary tumor SUVmax and STAS, LVI, and VPI were assessed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for tumor size, histologic subtype, and other clinically relevant covariates. Discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results STAS, LVI, and VPI were present in 269 (56.3%), 237 (49.6%), and 202 (42.3%) patients, respectively. SUVmax was independently associated with all three outcomes: STAS (adjusted OR = 1.051, 95% CI 1.020–1.083, p = 0.001), LVI (adjusted OR = 1.083, 95% CI 1.048–1.119, p < 0.001), and VPI (adjusted OR = 1.044, 95% CI 1.015–1.073, p = 0.002). Discriminative performance was acceptable for LVI (AUC = 0.701) but weak for STAS (AUC = 0.578) and VPI (AUC = 0.584). Sensitivity analyses excluding neoadjuvant-treated patients and interaction testing confirmed these associations were independent of neoadjuvant treatment status. Conclusion Preoperative SUVmax is independently associated with STAS, LVI, and VPI in resected NSCLC, most strongly for LVI. Although its standalone discriminative value is limited, SUVmax—already available at diagnosis—may contribute to multivariable preoperative risk stratification alongside histologic subtype and tumor size.

title: Navigated Robotic Guidance for Minimally Invasive Bertolotti Resection: Technical Feasibility and Workflow Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for trajectory and incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This article evaluates the feasibility of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow for minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A framework is presented for preoperative computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, navigated osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of planned robotic and navigated steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but do not prove superior outcomes. This paper outlines a novel technique; however, further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance is established.

title: X-ray tomography and coordinate metrology benchmark for internal cavities in additively manufactured alloys
abstract: Abstract X-ray computed tomography (CT) is widely used for dimensional inspection of inaccessible internal geometry, but multi-modal public benchmark datasets with reference metrology remain scarce, particularly for internal cavities. This paper releases a CT--coordinate measuring machine (CMM) benchmark for wall-thickness measurements using CT surface extraction of an artefact with a complex internal cavity that is disassembled for tactile probing. Four cases span Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 625 in rough and chemically milled states. Each case includes nominal computer-aided design (CAD) geometry aligned to the CT reconstruction, CT projections, reconstructed volumes, CT surface segmentations, CMM point clouds with predefined thickness-pair vectors, and derived surface- and thickness-deviation labels. The paper defines the benchmark tasks and reporting convention and reports baseline results for reconstruction-based and CAD-informed routes. The benchmark permits validation of CT-based dimensional metrology in noisy and clean environments, including CAD-constrained surface reconstruction approaches that work entirely in projection space, such as elastic registration.

title: PG-HSAM: Prototype-Guided Hierarchical Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation with Limited Annotations
abstract: Abstract Adapting segmentation foundation models to medical images with limited annotations requires effective use of semantic information without substantially increasing model complexity. We propose PG-HSAM, an extension of H-SAM that introduces prototype prior fusion (PPF) and balanced pixel-to-prototype contrastive regularization (BPC). PPF maintains exponential-moving-average class prototypes, converts pixel-to-prototype similarities into a semantic probability prior, and fuses this prior with the first-stage prediction before hierarchical refinement. BPC regularizes the same feature space with class-balanced pixel sampling. For binary segmentation, foreground and background prototypes are jointly normalized to construct the semantic prior. The prototype memory is non-trainable, and BPC is used only during training. Under the limited-label protocols of H-SAM, PG-HSAM achieves mean Dice scores of 80.49%, 85.20%, and 83.51% on Synapse, LA, and PROMISE12, respectively. Compared with H-SAM, the gains are 0.81, 1.26, and 6.56 percentage points, while Synapse HD95 decreases from 18.35 to 13.70. Ablation and hyperparameter studies further verify the contributions of PPF and BPC and show that the improvement is obtained without increasing the model parameter count.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy Treated with Therapeutic Hypothermia: Prognostic Values of Selected Real-World Markers from a Single- Centre Study
abstract: Abstract Background To verify the accuracy and reliability of clinically applicable prognostic markers assessed by neonatologists—specifically, background amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG) at 24 and 36 hours and the presence of abnormal posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) signaling on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)—for predicting mortality and long-term morbidity in newborns undergoing therapeutic hypothermia. Methods This retrospective cohort study included newborns admitted to a tertiary perinatal center (2009–2020) for therapeutic hypothermia. Background aEEG recordings at 24 and 36 hours of life and the presence of abnormal PLIC imaging were evaluated. The ability of these markers to predict mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes was statistically tested. Results Of the 80 infants with complete follow-up data, 15 (18.75%) died, and 17 (21.25%) had an abnormal long-term neurodevelopmental outcome. The predictive ability was as follows: aEEG at 24 hours yielded a sensitivity of 0.81 and specificity of 0.90; aEEG at 36 hours yielded a sensitivity of 0.78 and specificity of 0.83; abnormal PLIC signaling yielded a sensitivity of 0.72 and specificity of 0.77. Conclusions The tested markers demonstrate good prognostic value and are readily applicable in routine clinical practice for multimodal prognostication without requiring highly specialized radiological or neurophysiological expertise.
