title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Contrast-Enhanced CT-Based Radiomics Model for Predicting Extrahepatic Metastasis after TACE in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a prediction model integrating pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) radiomics with clinical features, and to evaluate its value in predicting extrahepatic metastasis (EHM) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods Clinical data of 152 patients with unresectable HCC who underwent TACE at the participating centers between January 2015 and December 2024 were retrospectively collected, and the patients were randomly assigned to a training set and an internal test set at a ratio of 7:3. Seventy additional HCC patients treated at other participating centers served as the external test set.Lesions were delineated on multiphase CECT images for radiomic feature extraction; after LASSO-based feature selection, the selected features were combined with independent clinical risk factors to construct prediction models and a nomogram. Model discrimination and calibration were assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration curves. The predictive performance of the models was validated using data from the external cohort. Results Multivariate analysis showed that age, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and maximum tumor diameter were independent predictors of EHM after TACE. Among the multiphase CT radiomics models, the venous-phase random forest (RF) model performed best (AUC = 0.899, 95% CI: 0.799–0.998), outperforming the logistic regression (LR) and support vector machine (SVM) models. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.923 in the internal test set, outperforming the clinical model alone. In the multicenter external validation cohort, the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.878 (95% CI: 0.801–0.957), indicating good generalizability. Conclusion The clinical-radiomics combined model, constructed from selected CT radiomic features and clinical features, demonstrated robust performance in predicting EHM in both the single-center development cohort and the multicenter external validation cohort. It holds promise for estimating the probability of EHM in patients with HCC after TACE and provides a noninvasive tool for preoperative risk stratification.

title: Molecular Findings, Clinical Severity, and Transplant-Free Survival in Pediatric Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Indian Cohort
abstract: Abstract Background The relationship between molecular findings, clinical disease severity, and heart failure (HF) outcomes in pediatric cardiomyopathy remains uncertain. Objectives To evaluate genetic diagnostic yield and the relative associations of clinical severity, biomarkers, and multimodality imaging with death or heart transplantation in children with cardiomyopathy. Methods This prospective single-center study included 235 children younger than 18 years at a South Indian referral center. Genetic testing, HF functional class, biomarkers, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and longitudinal outcomes were evaluated. Transplant-free survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression. Hierarchical models evaluated incremental prognostic discrimination using Harrell's C-index. Results Genetic testing was performed in 112 children (47.7%), of whom 54 (48.2%) had reported pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants. During a median follow-up of 15 months, 63 children (26.8%) died or underwent heart transplantation. Transplant-free survival did not differ significantly between P/LP-positive and genetic-negative groups (log-rank P = 0.058). Reduced ventricular function and late gadolinium enhancement were associated with adverse outcomes in univariable analyses. Among complete cases, the apparent C-index increased from 0.527 for demographics and cardiomyopathy phenotype to 0.813 after adding HF functional class and 0.842 after biomarkers, with limited additional discrimination from imaging measures. Conclusions Genetic testing demonstrated substantial laboratory-reported P/LP yield, although its effects on clinical management, family screening, and costs were not evaluated. HF functional severity and biomarkers provided the greatest apparent prognostic discrimination for death or transplantation, supporting an integrated clinical approach to pediatric cardiomyopathy assessment.

title: Diagnostic yield of Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) guided Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) in peripheral pulmonary infections: a prospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a key diagnostic tool in evaluating pulmonary infections and infiltrative lung diseases. However, conventional BAL relies on operator-dependent segment selection, potentially limiting diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions. Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) has been shown to improve localization in biopsy procedures but its role in guiding BAL remains unexplored. Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic yield of VBN-guided BAL in patients with clinical features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. Methods: This prospective observational pilot study included 50 adult patients with features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. All patients underwent VBN-guided BAL. Samples were analyzed using microbiological, molecular, and cytological techniques. Diagnostic yield and impact on clinical diagnosis were assessed. Results: A definitive diagnosis was achieved in 42/50 patients (84%). Diagnostic yield was higher in immunocompromised patients (92.9%) compared to non-immunocompromised patients (80.6%), though not statistically significant (p=0.414). The final diagnosis differed from the initial clinical diagnosis in 62% of cases. Common diagnoses included bacterial pneumonia (36%), tuberculosis (28%), and fungal infections (16%). Conclusion: VBN-guided BAL demonstrates high diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions and may significantly alter clinical management. Larger comparative studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Analysis of Risk Factors and Establishment of a Predictive Model for Endplate Collapse After Posterior Short-Segment Fixation Combined with Screw Placement at the Injured Vertebra in Thoracolumbar Fractures
abstract: Abstract Purpose To identify the risk factors for endplate collapse in patients with thoracolumbar fractures undergoing posterior short-segment fixation combined with intermediate screw placement, and to develop and validate a clinical prediction model to aid in early risk stratification and prognosis optimization. Materials and methods Clinical data from 135 patients with thoracolumbar fractures treated with posterior short-segment fixation and screw placement at the injured vertebra were retrospectively analyzed. Based on postoperative imaging findings, patients were stratified into an endplate collapse group (n = 57) and a non-collapse control group (n = 78). Variables collected included demographic and fracture characteristics (age, gender, BMI, fracture location, fracture pattern, mechanism of injury, osteoporotic status), radiographic parameters (screw length at the injured vertebra, severity of endplate and intervertebral disc injury, extent of anterior and posterior complex injury, postoperative mean vertebral body height [MVBH] and Cobb angle [CA]), and postoperative outcomes (fixation duration, postoperative Pfirrmann grade). Univariate analysis identified variables with significant between-group differences. Independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse were determined by multivariable logistic regression analysis. A predictive model was constructed incorporating these factors, and its performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with calculation of area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results Univariate analysis revealed significant differences in BMI, osteoporotic status, screw depth, endplate injury grade, intervertebral disc injury severity (Sander classification), load-sharing classification (LSC) score, postoperative Pfirrmann grade, and postoperative Cobb angle between groups (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade as independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse (all P < 0.05), with screw depth demonstrating the largest odds ratio and thus the strongest association. A predictive model incorporating these three factors was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888 (95% CI: 0.826–0.943), with sensitivity of 78.9% and specificity of 89.7%, indicating favorable predictive performance. Conclusion Postoperative endplate collapse following posterior short-segment fixation with injured vertebra screw placement for thoracolumbar fractures is multifactorial, with osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade serving as major independent risk factors. The predictive model developed in this study effectively stratifies the risk of postoperative endplate collapse and may provide a valuable tool for preoperative risk assessment, intraoperative technical optimization, and postoperative individualized rehabilitation planning, thereby potentially reducing the incidence of endplate collapse and improving functional outcomes.

title: Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy and Metabolic MRI in Epilepsy: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Synthesis of Neurochemical Biomarkers and Clinical Applications
abstract: Abstract Background: Since the introduction of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹H-MRS) in epilepsy research in the 1980s, metabolic MRI has provided unique insights into the neurochemical alterations underlying epilepsy. However, evidence has remained fragmented across imaging modalities, epilepsy syndromes, and clinical applications. We systematically reviewed the literature to define the metabolic phenotype of epilepsy and evaluate the evolving role of metabolic MRI in epilepsy research and clinical practice. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched through April 2026 for original human studies investigating metabolic MRI in epilepsy. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Findings were synthesized through structured qualitative evidence, supported by integrated methodological, scientometric, tabular, and visual analyses. Results: A total of 298 studies were included. Focal epilepsy demonstrated widespread alterations involving N-acetyl aspartate, glutamate, Gamma-aminobutyric acid, choline-containing compounds, myo-inositol, lactate, and other metabolites across epileptogenic and brain networks. Generalized epilepsy was characterized by predominantly bilateral and thalamo-cortical metabolic abnormalities, whereas tumor-associated epilepsy showed distinct metabolic alterations within tumors and the peritumoral zone. Treatment and prognostic studies demonstrated metabolite-specific changes following pharmacological and surgical interventions, and emerging metabolic MRI techniques provided complementary information on bioenergetics, ionic homeostasis, glutamatergic cycling, and metabolic flux. Conclusions: The available evidence supports epilepsy as a disorder of distributed metabolic networks that share a common signature of neuronal dysfunction while exhibiting syndrome-specific alterations in neurotransmission, gliosis, and energy metabolism. Complementary metabolic MRI techniques provide distinct biological information, but their clinical translation will require methodological harmonization and multimodal integration.

title: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
abstract: Abstract The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Anatomically-Guided Attention for False Positive Reduction in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract U-Net-based brain tumor segmentation can produce false positives in anatomically implausible locations, which inflate tumor volume estimates and reduce clinical trust. We investigate whether injecting an anatomical location prior into the network's attention can reduce these errors. We propose a prior informed attention gate that conditions U-Net features on empirical tumor-location prior maps computed from the training annotations, applied as a residual spatial gate at the bottleneck and at every decoder stage. Using the BRISC dataset of 2D contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices (glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor), we compare the proposed model with a vanilla U-Net and a learned-gate ablation under identical training, using 3-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set of 860 images. We evaluate Dice, IoU, precision, recall, Hausdorff distance, HD95 and a dedicated far false-positive measure. The proposed model matched the baseline in Dice (0.709 versus 0.708) and showed a slightly lower but non-significant HD95 (36.5 versus 37.9 px, p = 0.26); it did not significantly reduce far false positives (49.7 versus 48.0 px, p = 0.82). A simple location prior injected through a spatial gate is therefore insufficient on BRISC, and stronger prior integration, longer training and additional datasets are needed to establish any benefit.

title: A Comparative Study of Lightweight Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian CNNs and Ensemble Models for MRI-Based ASD Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Background: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is essential for improving clinical outcomes. Although deep learning (DL) has demonstrated strong potential in analyzing structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (sMRI), most existing frameworks rely on deterministic models that lack uncertainty quantification—an essential component for clinical decision-making—and often involve high computational complexity, limiting real-world applicability. Objective: This study aims to conduct a comprehensive comparative evaluation of three deep learning paradigms to develop a robust and uncertainty-aware framework for ASD diagnosis using multi-orientational MRI data (axial, coronal, and sagittal views). Methods: We systematically evaluated three categories of models: (1) fine-tuned deterministic architectures, including EfficientNetV2B0, EfficientNetB3, and MobileNetV2; (2) ensemble learning strategies, including averaging, majority voting, weighted averaging, and stacked generalization; and (3) lightweight Bayesian convolutional neural networks (CNNs) incorporating Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout and Variational Inference (VI) to estimate predictive uncertainty. This hierarchical framework enables a balanced assessment of diagnostic accuracy and model reliability. Results: Experimental results demonstrate that ensemble models achieved the highest classification performance, with a peak accuracy of 99.51% in the coronal view. Notably, the proposed lightweight Bayesian CNNs delivered competitive performance while providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, enabling the identification of ambiguous and out-of-distribution cases. Additionally, Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that model attention is concentrated in clinically relevant regions, particularly the frontal and temporal lobes, supporting the neurobiological plausibility of the predictions. Conclusion: This study highlights that integrating uncertainty quantification into lightweight deep learning architectures enhances both transparency and reliability compared to conventional deterministic approaches.

title: Primary Male Appendiceal Choriocarcinoma With Background of Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm: Diagnostic Challenges and Poor Prognosis.
abstract: Background/aim Choriocarcinoma is a highly aggressive trophoblastic malignancy that is most commonly gestational in origin. Non-gestational choriocarcinoma in the male gastrointestinal tract is extremely rare, and primary appendiceal involvement is exceptional. Case report We report such a case of a 75-year-old male who presented to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain. Physical examination indicated possible acute appendicitis suspicious for perforation, and computed tomography (CT) scans revealed a 7.5 cm mass in the lower right quadrant as well as numerous liver hypoechoic nodules. No lesions/nodules were identified in his testicles or mediastinum. Emergency surgery with right hemicolectomy and concurrent liver biopsy was performed. Pathology gross exam revealed a 7.5 cm appendiceal mass with associated appendiceal perforation. Histologically, the tumor showed a poorly differentiated carcinoma morphologically composed of syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts and intermediate trophoblasts with adjacent low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN). The carcinoma cells were positive for cytokeratin 7 (CK7), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), GATA-binding protein 3 (GATA 3) and Sal-like protein 4 (SALL4). These features supported a primary appendiceal choriocarcinoma and the liver biopsy demonstrated metastasis of choriocarcinoma with extensive tumor necrosis. Post-surgery lab tests also revealed an exceptionally high serum β-hCG titer of 289,308 mIU/ml. The patient underwent hospice care after surgery and expired one month later. Conclusion This is the first documented case of male primary choriocarcinoma with background of LAMN and poor prognosis. Recognition of the three carcinoma components in combination with the corresponding tumor immunohistochemical markers is the key for the precise diagnosis.

title: Topical Esomeprazole for the Prevention and Treatment of Radiation Dermatitis in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: Protocol for a Phase 2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background Radiation dermatitis (RD) is a common and clinically significant toxicity affecting the majority of patients undergoing external beam radiation therapy, particularly those treated for head and neck cancer (HNC). RD can impair quality of life, limit treatment intensity, and compromise oncologic outcomes; yet, there is no established standard-of-care for its prevention or management. Preclinical studies suggest that a topically reformulated proton pump inhibitor (PPI), esomeprazole (Dermaprazole), has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic properties that may mitigate radiation-induced skin injury. Objective This phase 2 randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the potential safety, feasibility, and efficacy of prophylactic topical Dermaprazole compared with standard supportive care (Aquaphor) in reducing the incidence and severity of clinically significant RD in patients with HNC receiving definitive chemoradiation. Methods This is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial with a 2:1 allocation ratio. A total of 45 adults (≥18 y) with biopsy-confirmed head and neck malignancy planned to receive definitive chemoradiation of at least 66 Gy will be enrolled. Participants will be randomized to receive twice-daily topical Dermaprazole or Aquaphor beginning at computed tomography (CT) simulation and continuing through 2 weeks after completion of radiation therapy. The primary outcome is the rate and severity of RD, assessed weekly during treatment using the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5 by the treating radiation oncologist, with blinded dermatologic assessment based on standardized medical photography. Feasibility outcomes include accrual rate, treatment compliance, and questionnaire completion rates. Secondary outcomes include time to onset and healing of grade ≥2 RD, quality of life assessed using the Skindex-16 instrument, radiation dose thresholds associated with dermatitis, and changes in inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin [IL]-1β, and IL-6). More specifically, secondary outcomes will be assessed through serial CTCAE version 5 evaluations for onset and healing, Skindex16 questionnaires for quality of life, radiation dose-volume parameters for dermatitis thresholds, and serum inflammatory marker concentration measurements before, during, and after treatment. Results The study began in June 2022 and has completed enrollment. Data analysis will commence following completion of data collection, with results expected to be published by 2027. Conclusions Should Dermaprazole demonstrate efficacy in reducing RD in patients undergoing radiation therapy, it may offer an alternative or adjunctive treatment option for the prevention and management of RD, potentially reducing treatment-related morbidity and improving patients' quality of life during radiotherapy. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04865731; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04865731. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/91035.

title: The Digital Twin Paradigm in Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Opportunities and Challenges.
abstract: Unlabelled Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a significant public health challenge. Its treatment is characterized by high anatomical complexity and a critical need for functional preservation of speech, swallowing, and respiration. While multimodality care, including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, has substantially improved patient survival, there are still high rates of life-altering toxicities and low response rates to immunotherapy. Current clinical decision-making largely relies on "digital snapshots"-static representations derived from population-based statistics and time point-specific imaging-which usually fail to account for the rapid anatomical and biological change during the course of treatment. Digital twins hold great promise in accelerating scientific breakthroughs and transforming oncology treatment and precision medicine through the creation of high-fidelity virtual patient representations that integrate real-time biological, anatomical, and clinical data. In this viewpoint, we propose 3 interconnected digital twins to establish a conceptual framework for the HNSCC digital twin. title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
abstract: Background Athletic hamstring injuries (AHSI) remain a persistent challenge because recurrence is common and clinical decisions often depend on incomplete evidence. This consensus statement is intended to give clinicians a practical, unified framework for classification, rehabilitation, and return to sport after athletic hamstring injury. The purpose of this study was to achieve expert consensus on the management of athletic hamstring injuries through a structured, scientific survey approach. Study design Delphi Survey. Methods A modified Delphi process, aligned with CREDES guidelines, was conducted with an expert panel of sports physical therapists identified as having specific expertise in AHSI from the ICCUS Society. Consensus was defined a priori as at least 80% agreement or disagreement on a 5-point Likert scale. Statements addressed three areas: AHSI examination and classification, rehabilitation and management, and return to sport (RTS) testing. Results Sixty statements were developed across three domains. Seventeen experienced clinicians completed the final round. Overall, 54 statements reached consensus, with a mean Likert score of 4.56 ± 0.37 out of 5 (strongly agree), and mean agreement of 89.88% ± 12.1%. Experts supported standardized terminology, MRI and the use of diagnostic ultrasound for diagnosis when appropriate, individualized and criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading and length restoration, early neuromuscular control, gradual running and agility progression, progression to pain-free sprinting, objective strength assessment, sport-specific workloads, and athlete readiness as key RTS criteria. Discussion The findings emphasize active rehabilitation guided by measurable progress rather than reliance on fixed thresholds. Clinicians should combine injury classification, functional presentation, symptom response, objective testing, sport demands, and athlete confidence when advancing rehabilitation and making RTS decisions. Conclusion This ICCUS Society consensus statement offers a practical roadmap for managing AHSI: classify clearly, load progressively, monitor symptoms, test objectively, and return athletes only when sport-specific running, sprinting, strength, training tolerance, and readiness align. Level of evidence 4.

title: Development of machine learning models for fetal birth weight prediction: A single-center study in a Turkish population.
abstract: Fetal birth weight (BW) is a critical indicator of the prognosis of perinatal health. Accurate estimation of BW is essential in determining the appropriate delivery method. This single-center study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning (ML) algorithms in estimating BW. The study population consisted of 456 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies evaluated at a single tertiary center in the Karaman region of Turkiye between 38 and 41 weeks based on their last menstrual period, who gave birth to a phenotypically normal live newborn within 7 days after the ultrasound examination. Seven out of the nine models developed using ML algorithms had the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) values ranging from 184.30 to 190.00 grams. The formula closest to these values was Hadlock III, with an MAE value of 223.33 grams. In our study, the model demonstrating the highest predictive accuracy was provided by Linear Regression algorithm with an MAE value of 184.30 grams. title: Intraoperative artificial intelligence for brain tumor surgery: from tissue diagnosis to real-time surgical guidance.
abstract: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. Yet, in clinical practice the molecular information that matters most to a surgeon-IDH status, 1p/19q codeletion, and methylation class-typically arrives days to weeks after the operation it was meant to inform. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to close that gap. Over the past several years, a growing body of work has demonstrated that AI models can extract diagnostically relevant molecular and histological information from data sources available in the operating room, in real time, at the point of surgical decision-making. In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art intraoperative AI models available to neurosurgeons during brain tumor resections. They examine AI-augmented approaches to established intraoperative techniques, such as cryosection and fluorescence-guided surgery, before turning to novel technologies including nanopore sequencing and stimulated Raman histology (SRH). The authors conclude by discussing barriers to widespread clinical adoption and what lies ahead for this field. For cryosection, models such as LGNet and the Cryosection Histopathology Assessment and Review Machine (CHARM) have demonstrated strong performance on intraoperative discrimination of primary CNS lymphoma and molecular subtyping of glioma, respectively, with CHARM achieving areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88-0.93 across glioma subtypes. In fluorescence-guided surgery, hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning has enabled classification of tumor type, grade, and IDH mutation based on the 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) signal with up to 93% accuracy, extracting molecular information from a modality already present in the operating room. For nanopore-based methylation classification, ensemble models such as Rapid Nanopore Brain Intraoperative Classification (ROBIN) have achieved 90% concordance with the final diagnosis prospectively in under 2 hours. In SRH, foundation models for infiltration detection now outperform FLAIR, contrast enhancement, and 5-ALA fluorescence in identifying tumor margins, while molecular classification models have achieved over 90% glioma subtype accuracy in multi-institutional cohorts. At the single-cell level, morphometric profiling of SRH images has revealed nuclear features distinguishing IDH-mutant from IDH-wildtype tumors, opening new avenues for interpretability. Despite this progress, widespread adoption remains limited by the absence of randomized clinical trials demonstrating patient-level benefit. Addressing this gap and realizing the potential of multimodal AI systems that integrate imaging, pathology, and molecular data represent critical next steps for the field.

title: Sequential arterial feeder targeting with microscope-based augmented reality and multimodal navigation for brain arteriovenous malformation resection: an integrated operative workflow in 158 cases.
abstract: Objective Early proximal arterial control is an established principle of brain arteriovenous malformation (bAVM) microsurgery but remains difficult to execute when feeding arteries are deep, obscured, or not apparent at the cortical surface. Herein, the authors describe the longitudinal clinical implementation of a workflow using multimodal navigation and microscope-based augmented reality (AR) to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection in bAVM resections. Methods Case-specific multimodal datasets were assembled according to clinical relevance and availability from CTA, high-resolution structural MRI with thin-slice T2-weighted imaging, MRA, and 3D rotational DSA studies and were fused within standard clinical neuronavigation platforms. All angiographically identifiable arterial feeders were segmented along their surgically relevant courses, prioritized as operative targets, and incorporated into exposure and corridor planning. Targets were displayed intraoperatively using the available navigation configuration, including microscope-based AR as the technology evolved. Functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were coregistered selectively to provide cortical and tractographic context. Consecutive navigation-assisted bAVM resections performed by a single neurosurgeon from 2013 to 2025 were analyzed. Outcomes included angiographic obliteration, perioperative morbidity, mortality, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score change relative to baseline. Results Of 192 bAVM resections performed during the study period, 158 consecutive navigation-assisted resections comprised the analytical cohort and included Spetzler-Martin (SM) grades I-V. Complete obliteration on initial angiography after microsurgery was observed in 97.5% of cases (154/158). At a median follow-up of 15 months, 93.0% of patients were functionally independent (mRS score 0-2). An increase in the mRS score relative to baseline occurred in 18.4% of patients, most commonly reflecting minor, nondisabling deficits with preserved independence. Loss of independence attributable to surgery occurred in 3.1% of patients, and the mortality rate was 1.3%. Conclusions Multimodal navigation with microscope-based AR was implemented longitudinally to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection, with selective integration of fMRI and DTI providing cortical and tractographic context for lesions near eloquent anatomy. Across SM grade I-V bAVMs, the workflow was feasible and was associated with high rates of angiographic obliteration and functional independence. By translating preoperative angioarchitecture into a planned sequence of discrete intraoperative arterial targets within their structural and functional context, the featured workflow provides a structured framework for operative planning, execution, and teaching in feeder-directed bAVM microsurgery.

title: First reported case of intradural extramedullary epithelioid hemangioma of the cauda equina: resection of an extremely rare vascular neoplasm. Illustrative case.
abstract: Background Intradural extramedullary (IDEM) tumors of the cauda equina are most often meningiomas, nerve sheath tumors, and myxopapillary ependymomas; purely vascular IDEM lesions are exceptionally rare. Fewer than 30 IDEM hemangiomas have been reported, mostly cavernous or capillary. Epithelioid hemangioma (EH), a benign vascular neoplasm arising in soft tissue and bone, has not previously been reported at the cauda equina. Observations A 63-year-old male with prior cutaneous melanoma presented with 3 months of progressive left L5-distribution radicular pain. MRI showed a 1.0 × 2.0-cm well-circumscribed IDEM mass at L4-5 with left L5-S1 foraminal stenosis. Under intraoperative ultrasound localization and continuous multimodal neurophysiological monitoring, en bloc gross-total resection was achieved through L4-5 laminectomy. Histopathological analysis revealed a well-circumscribed vascular neoplasm with lobular endothelial architecture and no cytological atypia; immunohistochemical analysis (ERG, CD31, and CD34 positivity; HHV8, inhibin, and melanocytic marker negativity) established the diagnosis of EH. At the 7-week follow-up, gross-total resection was confirmed on postoperative MRI. Lessons To the authors' knowledge, this is the first reported intradural EH at any spinal level. Recognition of epithelioid endothelial morphology combined with a comprehensive vascular and melanocytic immunohistochemistry panel is essential for diagnosis and separates EH from more common intradural vascular differentials. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26857.

title: [Safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring filtered type-B transnasal specialized airway catheter in anesthesia for ambulatory gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery in obese patients].
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring and filtering type B transnasal specialized airway catheter (hereafter referred to as the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway) during anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy in obese patients. Methods: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 92 obese patients (body mass index≥28 kg/m²) scheduled for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command between June and December 2025. Using a random number table, we split the participants evenly into an adjustable airway group (Group R, n =46) and a standard nasal cannula group (Group C, n =46). Anesthesia was inducted and maintained with remimazolam and alfentanil. Patients in Group R were fitted with the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway for oxygen delivery and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO 2 ) monitoring, and Group C received supplemental oxygen through conventional nasal cannula. The primary outcome was defined as the incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [pulse oximetry saturation(SpO 2 )<90%]. Secondary outcomes were the variations in respiratory rate, heart rate and mean arterial pressure (MAP) at time points before induction (T 0 ), upon endoscope insertion (T 1 ), 5 minutes post-insertion (T 2 ), at the end of surgery (T 3 ), and 5 minutes after waking up (T 4 ). Additional secondary outcomes included arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) and arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) at T 2 in both groups, and partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂) in group R. The duration of endoscopic therapy, dosages of remimazolam and alfentanil, the frequency of hands-on airway interventions, nasal bleeding episodes, and overall physician satisfaction scores were all systematically documented. Results: The baseline demographic and clinical characteristics matched up well between the two groups (all P >0.05). The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly lower in group R compared with group C [2.2%(1/46) vs 32.6%(15/46), χ 2 =14.829, P <0.001]. Patients in Group R exhibited significantly elevated SpO 2 levels at T 1 , T 2 , and T 3 (all P <0.05). At T 2 , Group R demonstrated significantly higher PaO 2 and lower PaCO 2 compared to Group C, their heart rates also stayed distinctly lower ( P <0.05). MAP remained comparable across both cohorts at every measured interval ( P >0.05). Intraoperative PetCO 2 values in Group R were consistently maintained within normative physiological parameters, accompanied by continuous and stable monitoring waveforms. Compared with Group C, Group R registered a significantly lower rate of necessity for airway interventions, shorter endoscopic procedure duration and emergence time, lower remimazolam consumption, and highter physician satisfaction (all P <0.05). Conclusions: During anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under gastrointestinal endoscopy in obese patients, the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway directly protects against hypoxemia by improving oxygen delivery and curtails carbon dioxide retention. Concurrently, accurate ventilation tracking helps maintain a highly stable hemodynamic profile, the clinical safety and efficacy of this airway device substantially surpass those of the conventional nasal cannula.

title: A Repeatable CT-Based Protocol for Nasal Cavity Volumetry and Choanal Airway Classification in Pediatric Syndromic Craniosynostosis.
abstract: Syndromic craniosynostosis (SC), such as Apert and Crouzon syndromes, causes midface hypoplasia that severely limits nasal cavity development. A computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric protocol for nasal cavity volumetry and choanal airway classification in pediatric SC patients, using landmark-based image segmentation software, is described and tested for intra-rater reproducibility. The protocol was applied to 10 SC patients (5 Apert, 5 Crouzon; 2-48 months; paired pre-/postoperative CT) and 10 reference children (60-168 months), not age-matched because CT is rarely indicated in healthy children. Intra-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.987 and 0.909; 95% CI 0.934-0.997 and 0.689-0.976). Nasal cavity volume increased between the paired CT scans in nine of ten patients (Wilcoxon Z = -2.701, p = 0.007; difference in medians +1,584.25 mm 3 ; +76.8%), remaining at only 10.3% of the reference group median postoperatively. title: The Effect of Alzheimer's Disease and Diabetes on the Volume of Brain Structures.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) are increasingly prevalent chronic disorders with overlapping effects on brain structure. However, direct volumetric comparisons among patients with AD alone, DM alone, both conditions, and healthy controls remain limited. This retrospective study compared regional brain volumes in 160 adults (18-90 years) assigned equally to four groups (n = 40 each): AD+type 1 DM, AD-only, type 1 DM-only, and healthy controls. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were analyzed using VolBrain, an automated, multiatlas, patch-based segmentation platform, on 3D T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MPRAGE) images acquired at 1.5 T. Regions evaluated included white and gray matter, subcortical structures, selected cortical gyri, and the ventricular system. Analyses were stratified by sex. No significant volumetric differences were observed between the AD+DM and AD-only groups. Compared with DM-only, differences were limited to the right amygdala (p = 0.004) and left thalamus (p = 0.001) in females. Relative to controls, both AD groups showed reductions in the bilateral amygdala, bilateral caudate, right thalamus, and middle temporal gyrus, together with third-ventricle enlargement (all p ≤ 0.005). The DM-only group showed fewer abnormalities. Reduced left caudate volume was the only finding consistently observed across all patient groups and both sexes (p ≤ 0.007). Overall, AD and DM showed partially overlapping regional differences in brain volume. The consistent left caudate reduction may represent a shared structural marker and warrants further prospective and longitudinal investigation in AD-DM comorbidity.

title: Host Fitness in Gastrointestinal Oncology: Beyond Tumor Biology.
abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancers face site-specific threats to nutritional intake, muscle function, organ reserve, and recovery. This critical narrative review examines host fitness as an organizing concept for these vulnerabilities rather than as a validated composite score. A targeted PubMed update identified publications from 2022 through September 14, 2026, using gastrointestinal cancer terms combined with prehabilitation, microbiome-immunotherapy, geriatric assessment, exercise, and digital assessment terms, while retaining relevant foundational studies. The review distinguishes guideline-supported care from prognostic associations and research-stage applications. Geriatric and nutritional assessments can guide established supportive care, whereas computed tomography-derived body composition and inflammatory indices primarily provide prognostic information. Microbiome signatures, epigenetic clocks, and integrated digital models require further validation before they can guide treatment decisions. Intervention effects vary by tumor site and treatment phase: selected prehabilitation trials demonstrate short-term benefits, although findings remain inconsistent, while long-term exercise after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer represents a distinct evidence base. An operational assessment protocol and multidisciplinary workflow are presented to link documented impairments with existing care pathways and repeated assessment. No host-fitness threshold is proposed for treatment escalation, de-escalation, or sequencing. Prospective studies should establish incremental predictive value and patient benefit beyond existing assessments before this integrated framework is used to support precision treatment decisions.

title: Application of Explainable Machine Learning for Individualized Risk Stratification and Surgical Optimization in Geriatric Intertrochanteric Fractures.
abstract: Mechanical failure remains a critical complication in the fixation of intertrochanteric fractures. While the Tip-Apex Distance (TAD) is a well-established prognostic metric, the independent biomechanical impact of the nail entry point remains controversial due to confounding surgical variables. This study aimed to evaluate the stability offered by a medialized entry point using interpretable machine learning. A retrospective cohort of 628 patients treated with cephalomedullary nailing was analyzed. A Random Forest model was developed using 12 clinical and radiographic variables to predict implant failure. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to disentangle confounding factors and visualize non-linear interactions between the entry-point strategy and TAD. The medialized entry point group exhibited a significantly lower failure rate compared to the standard group (25.3% vs. 44.2%; p < 0.001). The predictive model demonstrated robust performance (AUC: 0.877) on an independent testing set. Crucially, SHAP interaction analysis revealed a "buffering" effect: while risk profiles were comparable at optimal TAD levels, the medialized trajectory significantly attenuated the probability of failure when the TAD exceeded 25 mm, potentially mitigating the increased risk associated with suboptimal screw placement. The findings identify the medialized entry point as a significant independent predictor of success, increasing the biomechanical tolerance of the fixation construct. This surgical modification offers a valuable safety margin, particularly in cases where anatomical reduction or ideal screw positioning is challenging.

title: Ultrasound Biomicroscopic Features of Ciliary Epithelial Detachment in Bilateral Hypotony: A Novel Diagnosis.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to describe the clinical and ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) features of a previously unreported entity, ciliary epithelial detachment, in a patient with metastatic melanoma treated with nivolumab and presenting with bilateral hypotony. Visual acuity was 0.6 logMAR in the right eye and 1.3 logMAR in the left, with intraocular pressures of 7 mmHg in the right eye and 5 mmHg in the left. UBM revealed abnormal ciliary body morphology with truncation of ciliary processes and a distinct separation at the level of the ciliary epithelium in both eyes, most prominent inferotemporally. No evidence of fibrovascular proliferation or tractional distortion suggestive of cyclitic membrane was identified. These findings suggest a novel imaging phenotype: a ciliary epithelial detachment. Recognition of this entity may improve interpretation of anterior segment imaging in hypotony and refine diagnostic classification of ciliary body pathology.

title: Correlation of Spectral Doppler Indices of Superior Thyroid Artery and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Values in Benign and Malignant Thyroid Nodules in a Tertiary Level Hospital.
abstract: Background Thyroid nodules are common in clinical practice, with a small but significant proportion harboring malignancy. Conventional ultrasonography has limitations in differentiating benign from malignant nodules. Advanced imaging techniques such as spectral Doppler ultrasonography and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MRI) with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements may improve diagnostic accuracy. Aim The study aimed to assess the role of spectral Doppler ultrasound values of the superior thyroid artery in thyroid nodules and correlating with ADC values using diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) to differentiate benign and malignant thyroid nodules. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Radiology, ACS Medical College and Hospital, Chennai, from November 2023 to November 2024. Forty-two patients aged 18-70 years with suspected thyroid nodules were included using purposive sampling. Spectral Doppler ultrasonography was performed to assess pulsatility index (PI) and resistive index (RI), followed by DW-MRI using a 1.5 Tesla Siemens Magnetom Essenza scanner for ADC value measurement. Histopathology served as the reference standard. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26.0, with independent t-test and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis; P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The majority of participants were females (71.4%) and belonged to the 41-50 years of age group (31.0%). Malignant nodules demonstrated significantly higher PI (1.30 vs. 0.87; P = 0.04) and RI (0.80 vs. 0.60; P = 0.02), along with significantly lower ADC values at b = 0 and b = 1000 s/mm2 (P < 0.05). ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance with area under the curve values of 0.974 for ADC (b0), 0.984 for ADC (b1000), 0.993 for PI, and 0.978 for RI. Conclusion Spectral Doppler indices and ADC values are reliable noninvasive imaging biomarkers for differentiating benign from malignant thyroid nodules, with high diagnostic accuracy. Their combined use can enhance early diagnosis and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage Using Clinical and Computed Tomography Markers: A Prospective Study.
abstract: Background Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) represents a disproportionately high stroke burden (20%-30%) in low- and middle-income countries like India, necessitating accurate, early risk stratification using readily available clinical and radiographic features. Materials and methods This prospective observational study included 185 patients with spontaneous ICH at a tertiary care center. Baseline clinical severity was assessed using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and the ICH score. Radiographic markers included hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and radiographic signs (swirl, blend, black hole, satellite, and spot signs). The primary outcome was unfavorable functional status (modified Rankin scale: 4-6, including mortality) at 90 days. Univariate analyses focused on identifying predictors associated with a poor outcome, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Results The mean age was 56.0 ± 12.4 years, with 72.4% prevalence of hypertension. The unfavorable outcome rate was 37.3% (N = 69), with 22.2% mortality. Univariate analysis (P < 0.05) revealed strong associations between poor outcome and greater hematoma volume, lower GCS score, higher ICH score, IVH, swirl sign, blend sign, satellite sign, hydrocephalus, herniation, and ≥2 multiple noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) signs. Multivariable analysis identified hematoma volume, GCS score, ICH score, herniation, satellite sign, and male gender as independent predictors. Conclusion Clinical severity indicators and multiple NCCT signs in univariate analysis serve as robust markers of poor functional outcome. The independent prognostic value of the satellite sign and herniation highlights the utility of readily available radiographic features for immediate risk stratification.

title: Outcome of Children Treated with Rituximab for Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome: Renal Histopathology as a Response Marker.
abstract: Background Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) in children remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) are commonly used as first-line therapy, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission, and prolonged use may result in nephrotoxicity. Rituximab has emerged as a potential therapeutic option for refractory SRNS; however, treatment responses appear variable, and the influence of underlying renal histopathology remains incompletely understood. Objectives To evaluate the association between renal histopathological findings and clinical response to rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS). Methods Study Design and Setting:This prospective observational study was conducted between 2011 and 2020 at a university-affiliated tertiary pediatric nephrology center. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) and to examine the association between renal histopathological findings and treatment response. Twenty-four children aged 2-12 years were enrolled.Follow-up:Patients were followed prospectively after completion of rituximab therapy through regular clinical and laboratory assessments. The mean follow-up duration after the last rituximab infusion was 5.1 years (range: 6 months-8 years).Treatment Response Definitions:Complete remission was defined according to International Pediatric Nephrology Association (IPNA) recommendations as a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) ≤20 mg/mmol (≤0.2 mg/mg) or negative/trace proteinuria on dipstick testing on at least three consecutive occasions.Partial remission was defined as a UPCR >20 mg/mmol but <200 mg/mmol together with serum albumin ≥30 g/L.No response was defined as failure to achieve either complete or partial remission.Genetic Evaluation:Genetic testing was performed in all patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), classic minimal change disease (MCD), and MCD with IgM deposition. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants associated with monogenic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome were identified in the tested patients. Genetic testing was not performed in patients with IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, C1q nephropathy, or dense deposit disease. Results Twenty-four children with SRNS were included (13 males and 11 females; age range 2-12 years). Histopathological diagnoses included focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) in 9 patients (37.5%), minimal change disease (MCD) in 4 (16.7%), MCD with IgM deposition in 6 (25.0%), dense deposit disease in 2 (8.3%), membranous nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), IgA nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), and C1q nephropathy in 1 (4.2%). Overall, 10 patients (41.7%) achieved complete remission and 3 (12.5%) achieved partial remission, predominantly among patients with MCD and MCD with IgM deposition. Responses were uncommon among patients with FSGS. Eleven patients (45.8%), all of whom were non-responders, progressed to end-stage kidney disease. No major adverse effects of rituximab were observed; mild infusion reactions occurred in three patients and mild cellulitis in one patient. Conclusion In this cohort of children with refractory SRNS, favorable responses to rituximab were observed predominantly among patients with CNI- resistant MCD and MCD with IgM deposition, whereas responses among patients with FSGS were uncommon. These findings suggest that renal histopathology may help identify patients more likely to benefit from rituximab therapy; however, the small sample size, heterogeneous histopathological distribution, and observational study design preclude definitive conclusions. Larger prospective multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive genetic evaluation are required to determine whether histopathology can serve as a reliable predictor of rituximab responsiveness.

title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
abstract: Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). Aims We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. Methods Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index. Results Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). Conclusions Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. originalAbstract:
Background

Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).

Aims

We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.

Methods

Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.

Results

Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).

Conclusions

Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

title: Magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction and selected quantitative ultrasound methods for hepatic steatosis: histology-referenced diagnostic performance and longitudinal responsiveness-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose To synthesize histology-referenced diagnostic performance at study-selected thresholds and the longitudinal responsiveness of magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and selected quantitative ultrasound methods in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Methods Four databases were searched from database inception through July 1, 2026. Sensitivity, specificity, and odds ratios were pooled with 95% confidence intervals using heterogeneity-selected fixed- or random-effects models. Small-study effects were assessed using funnel plots and Begg tests; longitudinal changes were pooled when change-score standard deviations were reported. Results In total, 44 articles were included: 34 contributed histology-referenced diagnostic data, and 11 were assessed for longitudinal responsiveness, with 1 article contributing to both. At steatosis grade (S) ≥ 1/S ≥ 2/S ≥3, MRI-PDFF sensitivity and specificity was 93.6%/81.5%/83.1% and 87.1%/86.7%/83.2%, respectively; the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) was 86.8%/81.2%/86.4% and 98.9%/71.0%/64.6%, respectively. The attenuation coefficient/attenuation imaging sensitivity/specificity was 83.2%/98.1%, 86.4%/79.9%, and 99.3%/76.4%, respectively. Ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter and ultrasound-derived fat fraction evidence was limited. Three head-to-head longitudinal studies included 298 participants, of whom only 158 had analyzable change-score data; in these, pooled changes were -4.53 percentage points for MRI-PDFF and -12.71 dB/m for the CAP. Thirty-two of the 34 diagnostic studies were at high-risk of bias from cohort-selected thresholds. Begg tests did not detect significant small-study effects, although their power was very limited in analyses that included only 2 or 3 studies. Conclusion At study-selected thresholds, MRI-PDFF showed balanced sensitivity and specificity across steatosis grades, whereas quantitative ultrasound varied by method, platform, and threshold. These findings support comparative synthesis but do not establish validated cut-offs or superiority of either modality. Clinical significance Study-selected thresholds limit clinical translation. MRI-PDFF proton density fat fraction and quantitative ultrasound are complementary, with use depending on clinical purpose, platform, and precision needs.

title: Comparative reasoning in radiology artificial intelligence: longitudinal and reference-case approaches.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in radiology remains predominantly examination-centric, whereas clinical interpretation frequently depends on comparison across time or with relevant prior cases. This narrative review examines comparative reasoning in radiology AI through two related but clinically distinct forms: longitudinal reasoning, which compares examinations from the same patient over time, and reference-case reasoning, which uses clinically analogous cases from other patients to support interpretation. We propose a capability hierarchy that distinguishes simple access to comparative information from higher-level capabilities, including selection of relevant historical context, anatomical and lesion-level correspondence, characterization of interval change, temporal-state interpretation, multi-interval trajectory reasoning, and entity-specific assessment of clinical similarity. This distinction matters because providing prior examinations or retrieving visually similar cases does not itself demonstrate meaningful comparative reasoning. We review developments in prior-examination selection, registration, lesion tracking, temporal vision-language modeling, treatment-response assessment, analogous-case retrieval, and longitudinal report generation. Particular emphasis is placed on evaluation strategies that determine whether model performance depends appropriately on clinically relevant comparative information rather than on additional input volume, global image similarity, acquisition characteristics, or other shortcuts. Key challenges include incorrect prior selection, lesion mismatching, temporal inconsistency, clinically irrelevant reference-case retrieval, data leakage, misleading comparative language, and propagation of historical errors. Future progress will require models that preserve entity identity, reason coherently across multi-visit imaging histories, identify clinically informative reference cases, and demonstrate benefit under realistic clinical conditions. Comparative reasoning is therefore a necessary step in the transition from examination-level toward patient-level radiology AI.

title: Non-nutritional rickets: Approach, precision medicine, and outcomes.
abstract: Rickets are chronic bone disorders marked by impaired mineralization of the growing skeleton. While most cases arise from nutritional deficiencies, non-nutritional forms are frequently underrecognized. Subtle signs such as alopecia in vitamin D dependent rickets type 2A, cataract in Lowe syndrome, dental abscesses or sensorineural hearing loss in X-linked hypophosphatemia can prompt timely diagnosis and referral. A structured approach combining growth and skeletal assessment, targeted biochemistry (calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, parathyroid hormone, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), radiography, and early genetic testing once nutritional deficiency or renal failure are excluded improves diagnostic accuracy. Molecular confirmation enables precise subclassification into hypophosphatemic and calciopenic rickets, supporting genotype-directed therapy, including burosumab for X-linked hypophosphatemia. Early, tailored treatment enhances radiographic healing, growth, and function. Emerging genotype-phenotype correlations further inform genetic counselling and prognosis, strengthening the multidisciplinary management of these complex disorders.

title: A Primer on Radiomics for the Practicing Orthopaedic Surgeon.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is permeating many aspects of daily life. Medicine, and specifically orthopaedic surgery, is being influenced by the rapid growth and success of AI in serving as an adjunct to medical expertise. AI includes many nested subfields and applications such as computer vision, language models, and predictive analytics. Using standard machine learning methods, clinical decision support tools are being developed for clinicians to provide evidence-based, individualized care. Some models predict clinical and functional outcomes after a procedure, whereas others may incorporate administrative metrics to predict factors, such as length of stay, return to the emergency department, and complications. The application of AI to medical imaging focuses on the extraction of a large amount of quantitative data in the form of predefined features from clinical images that humans cannot perceive, a field known as radiomics. There has been recent interest, particularly in oncology, to apply radiomics to aid in diagnosis and prognostication of outcomes. Given the robust growth of radiomics literature, and the anticipated application in orthopaedic surgery, the purpose of this review article is to educate the orthopaedic surgery community on the practical importance and the basics of radiomics.

title: ConfUSIus: an accessible and scalable toolkit for functional ultrasound imaging analysis
abstract: Functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) maps brainwide hemodynamics at high resolution, yet analysis requires expert knowledge as pipelines remain fragmented across laboratories. We introduce ConfUSIus, an open-source Python package and graphical interface for accessible, scalable, and reproducible fUSI analysis. Its common data model unifies heterogeneous fUSI recordings across beamformed IQ processing, motion correction, registration, denoising, and statistical analysis. ConfUSIus lowers barriers and facilitates method development, comparison, and sharing.

title: Cerebrovascular Structure-Flow Gradients Revealed by Volumetric Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
abstract: Characterizing the joint organization of microscale cerebrovascular structure and flow in vivo is challenging. Volumetric ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) provides spatially resolved measures of microvascular structure and flow from the same acquisition, but how these features are jointly organized across brain networks remains unclear. Here, we characterized local vascular phenotypes from transcranial volumetric ULM in mice and examined whether they contained reproducible low-dimensional organization. Local measures of vascular structure and flow dynamics were summarized within corresponding brain regions across mice. Subject-specific vascular phenotype similarity matrices were combined into a group-consensus graph and analyzed using diffusion embedding. Two leading gradients, showing distinct spatial distributions across brain networks, were reproducibly recovered across subject and spatial scales. The principal gradient was associated with local vascular density and flow complexity, defining a vascular structure-related axis. The secondary gradient was associated with flow speed and acceleration, defining a flow-dynamics-related axis. These gradients provide a low-dimensional representation of the cerebrovascular structure and flow and provide a reference for studying coordinated vascular changes across disease, aging, and intervention.

title: Real-time Volumetric Imaging for Minimally-Invasive Thoracic Interventions: A Deformable Phantom Study
abstract: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the ability of VoxelMap, a deep learning framework for 3D respiratory motion estimation, to generate volumetric images in real-time from 2D projections acquired for two deformable lung phantoms on a clinical interventional C-arm angiography system. Materials and MethodsVoxelMap was evaluated using the PixelPrint4D and Casper deformable physical thoracic respiratory phantoms. Four-dimensional cone-beam CT (4D CBCT) images acquired on a clinical fixed-room C-arm angiography system were used for network training and volumetric ground truth. Prediction accuracy was evaluated on withheld respiratory phases using structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Model inference time was measured to assess suitability for continuous real-time processing. Deep ensembles were also used to assess model uncertainty. Correlation between ensemble uncertainty and prediction error was evaluated for both phantoms. ResultsVoxelMap achieved high prediction accuracy across withheld respiratory phases in both physical phantoms. SSIM values exceeded 0.92 in all experiments, with a higher performance observed for the Casper phantom (0.969-0.973) than for the PixelPrint4D phantom (0.927-0.943). Model inference times were less than 15 ms for both phantoms which is compatible with real-time processing. Ensemble uncertainty was positively correlated with prediction error in both phantoms, indicating that higher uncertainty was associated with less accurate volumetric predictions. ConclusionsOur study demonstrated that VoxelMap generates accurate volumetric deformations of respiratory anatomy from projections acquired on a clinical interventional C-arm system, with computational inference times compatible with continuous processing. By deriving volumetric information directly from two-dimensional fluoroscopic projections, VoxelMap has the potential to augment continuous fluoroscopic guidance with continuously updated volumetric information. Ensemble uncertainty may provide a potentially useful indicator of prediction reliability. Further studies using clinically representative training data and patient studies is required to establish clinical utility. Our code is available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap.

title: Topographic reference modelling of white matter hyperintensities across the adult lifespan
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are among the most common MRI findings in older adults. They are widely regarded as markers of brain aging and cerebral small-vessel disease, and associated with risk for cognitive decline, Alzheimers disease and related dementias (ADRD), and stroke. White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are typically interpreted by total lesion burden, but lesions with similar volumes can occupy different anatomical locations, potentially reflecting distinct pathological processes. Here we present voxelwise topographic reference modelling (vTRM), a framework for characterizing individual WMH masks against age- and sex-stratified frequency maps derived from cognitively unimpaired individuals. Using 42,469 FLAIR-derived lesion masks from twelve adult cohorts, we mapped population-level WMH spatial vulnerability, characterized age-related changes in its distribution across periventricular, lobar and arterial-territory compartments, and constructed paired percentile charts for lesion burden and spatial typicality. A quadrant-based classification defined by these two percentile dimensions revealed graded relationships with ADRD pathophysiology, neurodegeneration, and cognitive impairment, while identifying WMH patterns differentially associated with ageing-related, vascular and neurodegenerative processes among individuals with similar lesion volumes. These reference charts establish a benchmark for normative WMH ageing, enabling quantification of individual deviations from typical age-, sex- and burden-related patterns and identification of WMH phenotypes associated with vascular, neurodegenerative or mixed etiologies. The framework, together with a deployable 3D U-Net model trained on these data for automated WMH segmentation, is available through the Brain Lesion Analytics platform (https://brainlesionanalytics.org/).

title: Ultradeep optical coherence tomography
abstract: Deep optical imaging of intact brain tissue is limited by scattering and absorption, restricting our ability to study subcortical structures. Here, we introduce ultradeep optical coherence tomography (OCT), which combines hardware and computational approaches to enhance the signal from deep tissue regions. Ultradeep OCT utilizes a longer illumination center wavelength of 1575 nm, spectral-domain balanced detection and imaging in the conjugate configuration with the zero optical path difference positioned deep in the tissue. Autocorrelation artifacts are measured and subtracted, and multiple frames are coherently averaged to improve the signal-to-noise ratio further. These techniques, along with computational refocusing and bandwidth control, allowed us to extend structural imaging depth in biological tissues. Ultradeep OCT demonstrated physical imaging depths of 2.3 to 2.8 mm (mean 2.5 mm) in the ex vivo mouse brain and 2.5 to 3.0 mm (mean 2.8 mm) in chicken tissue. The resulting volumes in the ex vivo mouse brain samples depict the dorsal hippocampus and its two major subregions with sufficient contrast to allow segmentation and three-dimensional reconstructions. Features in the thalamus could also be discerned. These findings demonstrate the potential of ultradeep OCT as a label-free approach for visualizing deep-brain structures at a spatial scale complementary to magnetic resonance imaging and microscopy. This approach could enable optical imaging studies of hippocampal structural changes in mouse models of neurodegenerative disease.

title: Assessment of Dissemination in Time in Multiple Sclerosis Using a Single 3D T2-FLAIR magnetic resonance imaging Radiomic Signature
abstract: Background: In multiple sclerosis (MS), dissemination in time (DIT) is an important component of demonstrating disease activity and establishing the chronology of lesion development. DIT is routinely assessed from contrast-enhanced or follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Although proved useful, these methods are not without caveats motivating alternative approaches to study lesion chronology. We investigated whether single T2-FLAIR MRI contains sufficient information to distinguish temporally distinct MS lesion categories using radiomic features. Methods: In a retrospective longitudinal cohort of 273 participants with MS (1,311 MRI acquisitions), persistent brain lesions were temporally stratified using serial T2-FLAIR MRI. Long-standing established (LS-E) lesions were defined as observed for six years at least, and recent incident (R-I), as lesions that appeared over the span of two years in a follow-up MRI and were present until the last scan available. Radiomic features were extracted from lesion-level T2-FLAIR MRI. Feature selection was performed in an independent discovery cohort (Group 1, N=55). Selected features were then used to train a support vector machine classifier in a separate development cohort with repeated group-wise cross-validation (Group 2, N=163). Final performance was assessed in an held-out test cohort (Group 3, N=55). An exploratory analysis was then performed on baseline MRI from 64 subjects with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), acquired after their first clinical demyelinating event. Results: Longitudinal tracking identified 814 classifiable lesions in Group 1, 3203 in Group 2, and 984 in Group 3. In Group 1, 18 radiomic features met predefined selection criteria (FDR-adjusted p smaller than 0.05 and absolute Cohen's d greater than 0.8), spanning intensity, shape, and texture domains. In the independent test cohort, the support vector machine classifier achieved an area under the curve of 0.78, with correct classification rates of 66% for R-I lesions and 73% for LS-E lesions. In the exploratory CIS analysis, predicted lesion temporal composition showed substantial inter-patient heterogeneity, with approximately one in ten participants presenting radiomic features compatible with LS-E lesions at their first clinical event. Conclusions: Single T2-FLAIR MRI contains measurable information related to MS lesion chronology. This proof-of-concept framework supports the feasibility of a line of research based on radiomics temporal lesion characterisation without contrast administration or dense longitudinal follow-up MRI, with potential relevance for studying lesion evolution and supporting DIT assessment.

title: NeuroWeave-3D: Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Completion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing MRI Modalities
abstract: Multi-parametric MRI segmentation models are accurate when all prescribed sequences are available but can be brittle under missing or corrupted modalities. We propose NeuroWeave-3D, a 3D glioma segmentation framework that treats missing modalities as uncertain evidence rather than deterministic channels to reconstruct. The model combines spatial modality routing, probabilistic latent feature completion, complete-to-missing consistency, and voxel-level uncertainty estimation. A curriculum over all non-empty MRI modality subsets trains one network for arbitrary sequence availability. We define a BraTS-centered evaluation that reports complete-input accuracy, macro and worst-case missing-modality performance, corruption robustness, calibration, and failure detection.
